Quin & celebratissimum illud spei nostræ stræ fundamentum, syllogismus videlicet Euangelii practicus, Qui-cunque crediderit in Iesum Christum, ille remissionem peccatorum & vitam æternam consequetur: Atqui ego miser peccator credo in Iesum Christum, & certò persuasus sum illum vnicum esse saluatorem mundi: Ego igitur quoque remissionem peccatorum ac vitam æternam consequar: Idem quod statuimus discrimen, luculenter euincit, in quo necesse est, medium terminum ab vtroque extremo distingui: ideò enim scio, Deum mihi reconciliatum & peccata mihi condonaturum, vitæque æternæ participem factúrum esse: quia certus sum me credere, cuius consequentiæ ratio, ab ipsa veracitate Dei ciúsque potentia & voluntaria dispensatione ac misericordia, desumitur, quâ causa & ratio alia superior, cùm tota Scriptura sacra omnem salutis nostræ rationem in solam Dei Δόξαν, & vnicum eius beneplacitum transcribat, reddi nulla potest, ac proinde efficitur syllogismus apodicticus. Quia verò fides est ἐκ πίστεως τι, & necessario proprium suum obiectum præsupponit, hinc liquidò constat, inter fidem ac fiduciam & obiectum fidei ac fiduciæ, discrimen statuendum esse. Hic syllogismus, quem spes conficit, est celebris illa bonorum ἐλπιζομένων ὑπόστασις & βλεπομένων ἔλεγχος, cuius propositio ex Euangelii ac fidei & πληροφορίας illius τῆς σωτηρίας thesauro depromitur, & cui propositioni habita fides, præsupponit, tum scripturę Θεοπνευστία, ac autoritatem omni exceptione maiorem, & secundum illam veritatis & potentiæ diuinæ solidam notitiam, vti exemplum Abrahami nos perspicuè docet, Rom. 4. v. 18. 19. 20. 21. Qui Abraham contra spem sub spe credidit, vt fieret Pater multarum gentium: secundum id quod ei dictum fuerat, ita erit semen tuum, ac minimè imbecillis fuit, non considerauit suum ipsius corpus iam emortuum, quum centum circiter natus esset annos, nec emortuam vuluam Saræ. Aduersus promissionem autem Dei non disceptauit infidelitate, sed robustus factus est fide, tributa gloria Deo, ac plenè persuasum habens, eum, qui promiserat, posse etiam facere: tum agnitionem miseriæ & desiderium liberationis ac gratiæ. Matth. 5. vers. 6. Beati qui esuriunt & sitiunt iustitiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur. & 11. v. 28. Venite ad me omnes qui fatigati & onerati estis, & ego faciam vt requiescatis. Marc. 2. 17. Iis qui valent non opus est medico, sed iis qui male affecti sunt: non veni vt vocarem iustos, sed peccatores ad resipiscentiam. Ioh. 7. v. 37. Si quis sitit, veniat ad me & bibat. Galat. 3. v. 22. Conclusit Scriptura omnia sub peccatum, vt promissio ex fide Iesu Christi daretur cre-
units.tr: But before we believe in Jesus Christ, we are neither friends of God, nor his sons, nor heirs of eternal life, since we are children of wrath and therefore liable to the curse and eternal damnation. And for how long, indeed for how many years, are the ears of many people beaten with the external preaching of the gospel before they can be moved to have faith in its truth, even though they are always commanded to believe in the meantime? From all this, I think, it is clear that the object of trust, and of that special application, must be distinguished from the object of faith itself and of full assurance [πληροφορίας]; and therefore that trust, the trust of justifying faith, is neither the form nor an essential part of it [ποιήσεως], but its effect and fruit. Our view is confirmed by the whole truth of the gospel, which promises life and eternal salvation only to those who believe in Christ. Just as the gospel promises us reconciliation with God the Father, forgiveness of sins, and eternal life, so too we can be certain of obtaining those benefits, because all certainty of our salvation rests on the word of God and his promises. But the gospel promises forgiveness of sins, reconciliation with God the Father, and eternal life to no one except under the condition of faith, that is, only if he believes that Christ is the promised and provided Saviour of the world, and his own Saviour too, if he believes this. For in the gospel's sense it is true that all who believe in Christ will be saved; but it is not true of Peter and Paul unless the condition of faith, under which eternal life is promised to us, is posited in them. That is, this is true of them not materially but formally considered, as the Schoolmen say. Therefore no one can be certain of his salvation unless he has fulfilled the stipulated condition, that is, unless he has believed that Christ is the Saviour of the world and his own too, if he believes it. From all this it necessarily follows that faith and trust are not to be considered in the same way with respect to eternal life as their object. For faith joins the common consequent, namely the reward of eternal life, with the common antecedent, namely that all believers in general (this common antecedent, joined to the consequent, being an attribute that can be predicated of it only by the free will and dispensation of God) are heirs; and it joins it, specially but conditionally and not absolutely, to its own subject, in which the habit of faith is infused. Both of these hold because of the nature of the gratuitous covenant, the truth of the divine promise, and the omnipotence of God. Trust, however, states that common consequent or attribute of its own subject or proper antecedent specially, simply and absolutely, on account of the certainty of faith, whose condition it presupposes the subject to have fulfilled. And therefore it is also clear that to believe in Christ and to believe that I shall be saved are not one and the same thing, although the latter necessarily and always follows the former. I join them with an indissoluble bond, and I do not separate or sunder them; but because they are wrongly confused, I distinguish them. Indeed, the very famous foundation of our hope, the practical syllogism of the gospel, clearly proves the same distinction: "Whoever believes in Jesus Christ will obtain forgiveness of sins and eternal life. But I, a wretched sinner, believe in Jesus Christ, and am firmly persuaded that he is the only Saviour of the world. Therefore I too shall obtain forgiveness of sins and eternal life." In this syllogism the middle term must necessarily be distinguished from each of the extremes. For I know that God is reconciled to me, will forgive my sins, and will make me a partaker of eternal life, because I am certain that I believe. The reason for this inference is drawn from the very truthfulness of God, his power, his voluntary dispensation and his mercy. No higher cause or reason can be given for it, since the whole of holy Scripture ascribes every reason for our salvation to the sole glory [Δόξαν] of God and his one good pleasure; and therefore the syllogism is demonstrative. But because faith is "from faith" [ἐκ πίστεως τι] and necessarily presupposes its own proper object, it is clear that a distinction must be drawn between faith and trust, and between the object of faith and the object of trust. The syllogism that hope constructs is the famous one: "the substance [ὑπόστασις] of things hoped for, and the evidence [ἔλεγχος] of things not seen" (Heb. 11:1). Its major premise is drawn from the treasury of the gospel and of that full assurance [πληροφορίας] of salvation [τῆς σωτηρίας], and it presupposes that faith in this premise is held, both on the ground of the divine inspiration [Θεοπνευστία] of Scripture, whose authority surpasses every objection, and on the ground of solid knowledge of the truth and power of God, as the example of Abraham clearly teaches us (Rom. 4:18–21): "Abraham, against hope, believed in hope, that he should become the father of many nations, according to what had been said to him: So shall your seed be. And he was not weak; he did not consider his own body, already dead, since he was about a hundred years old, nor the dead womb of Sarah. He did not waver through unbelief at the promise of God, but was made strong in faith, giving glory to God, and being fully persuaded that he who had promised was able also to do it." Hope also presupposes knowledge of one's wretchedness and a desire for deliverance and grace: "Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled" (Matt. 5:6). "Come to me, all who labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Matt. 11:28). "Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick do; I came not to call the righteous but sinners to repentance" (Mark 2:17). "If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink" (John 7:37). "Scripture has shut up all things under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe" (Gal. 3:22).

units.la: Ccc dentibus. Deinde notitiam Christi,Σωτῆρος,id est,personæ & officii ipsius:Esa.53. versu vndecimo: In scientia fui seruus meus iustificabit multos. Ioh.17. versu tertio,Hæc est vita æterna vt te solum agnoscant verum Deum, & quem misisti Iesum Christum. Denique bonorum & beneficiorum, quibus peccatores ad fidem & resipiscentiam inuitantur, cognitionem. Ephes. primo, versu 17.18.19 Deus Domini nostri Iesu Christi, det vobis Spiritum sapientiæ & reuelationis per agnitionem ipsius, illuminatis oculis mentis vestræ, vt sciatis quæ sit spes illa vocationis ipsius, & quæ opes gloriæ hæreditatis ipsius in sanctis, & quæ sit excellens illa magnitudo potentiæ ipsius in nobis, qui credimus, pro efficacitate fortis roboris ipsius. Assumptio vero desumitur, tum ex sensu & effectis fidei, maximè vero bonorum operum, id est, pietatis erga Deum & charitatis erga proximum, syncero studio, ex quibus, ceu fructibus & effectis propriis, certissimè concludere possumus, nos salutari illo fidei dono diuinitus instructos esse, Tit. 1.1. Paulus servus Dei, Apostolus autem Iesu Christi, secundum fidem electorum Dei & agnitionem veritatis, quæ est secundum pietatem. Iac primo, versu decimo octauo. Ostende mihi fidem tuam ex operibus tuis, & ego ostendam tibi ex operibus meis fidem meam.1.Ioh.2.versu tertio. Per hoc scimus nos eum nosse, si mandata eius obseruamus. Tum etiam ex interno,& infallibili testimonio Spiritus sancti, testantis vna cum Spiritu nostro, nos esse filios Dei. Hac igitur fiducia fretus homo fidelis, sibi specialiter applicat, quicquid fidei à Deo per Christum in Scripturis promissum est, videlicet Dei patris gratiam, misericordiam, dilectionem, benignitatem, beneplacitum, omniaque beneficia eius, gratuitam reconciliationem, remissionem peccatorum, imputationem iustitiæ Christi, gratuitam acceptationem coram Deo,δικαίωσιν, liberationem à lege, & mortis, ab execratione legis, propitiationem pro peccatis nostris, salutem, vitam æternam, gloriosam cum Deo communionem, hæreditatem vitæ cœlestis, pacem, gaudium, spémque Dei gloriæ, &c. Denique Spiritum sanctum,& omnes illius salutares actiones, & immensum gratiarum, virtutum, donorumque eius cumulum. Hinc pax & tranquillitas conscientiæ, adeoque ἀσυμία illa & constantissima mentis recreatio, ac incredibilis animi lætitia & serenitas, qua fit,vt superatis,imò expulsis conscientiæ terroribus,quibus animus desperabundus percellebatur, nempe ex interiore quidem illo & occulto, sed horribili iudicii diuini senni sensu, in patefacta & apprehensa gratia ac benevolentia Dei, securè acquiescit, & ineffabili gaudio perfunditur, eiusque fruitione vere est beatus. Hinc excellens illa fidelium victoria, & gloriosus triumphus, quem illi adversus rationis & mundi iudicium, de omnibus tentationibus peccati & crucis, in mediis calamitatibus & afflictionum fructibus, aguntur. Rom. 8. v. 31. & seqq.. Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Is quidem qui proprio Filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit eum, qui non etiam omnia cum eo nobis gratificabitur? quis intentabit crimina adversus electos Dei? Deus is est qui iustificat: quis est qui condemnet? Christus est, qui mortuus est, imo vero qui etiam excitatus est, qui etiam est ad dextram Dei, qui etiam interpellat pro nobis. Quis nos separabit a charitate Christi? num afflictio, num angustia, num fames, num nuditas, num periculum, num gladius? Imo in his omnibus plusquam victores sumus, per eum qui dilexit nos. Nam mihi persuasum est, neque mortem, neque vitam, neque Angelos, neque principatus, neque potestates, neque praesentia, neque futura, neque sublimitatem, neque profunditatem, neque ullam rem aliam creatam, posse nos separare a charitate Dei quae est in Christo Iesu Domino nostro. & 1. Cor. 15. v. 54. 55. 56. 57. Absorpta est mors ad victoriam, Ubi tua o mors victoria? ubi tuus o sepulchrum stimulus? Stimulus vero mortis est peccatum, vis autem peccati lex. Sed Deo sit gratia, qui dedit nobis victoriam per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum. Qui aliter sentiunt, & fidem cum fiducia, ac utriusque obiecta confundunt, summis ac gravissimis difficultatibus se inuoluunt, ex quibus quomodo se expedire queant, videre non possum.
units.tr: teeth. Next, the knowledge of Christ as Saviour [Σωτῆρος], that is, of his person and office: By his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many (Isa. 53:11). And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent (John 17:3). Finally, the knowledge of the good things and benefits by which sinners are invited to faith and repentance: The God of our Lord Jesus Christ give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him; the eyes of your understanding being enlightened, that ye may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints, and what is the exceeding greatness of his power to us-ward who believe, according to the working of his mighty power (Eph. 1:17–19). The assumption, however, is drawn from the feeling and effects of faith, and above all from good works, that is, from sincere devotion to God and love toward one's neighbour. From these, as their own fruits and effects, we can most certainly conclude that we have been divinely endowed with that saving gift of faith: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness (Titus 1:1). Shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works (James 1:18, 2:18). And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments (1 John 2:3). Then also from the inward and infallible testimony of the Holy Spirit, who bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God. Relying on this confidence, the faithful man applies to himself specifically whatever of faith has been promised in Scripture by God through Christ: namely, the grace, mercy, love, kindness and good pleasure of God the Father, and all his benefits: free reconciliation, the remission of sins, the imputation of the righteousness of Christ, gratuitous acceptance before God, justification [δικαίωσιν], deliverance from the law and from death, from the curse of the law, propitiation for our sins, salvation, eternal life, glorious communion with God, the inheritance of heavenly life, peace, joy, and the hope of the glory of God, and so on. Finally, he applies to himself the Holy Spirit and all his saving operations, and the immense abundance of his graces, virtues and gifts. From this come peace and tranquillity of conscience, and that tranquillity [ἀταραξία] and most constant refreshment of mind, and the incredible joy and serenity of soul, by which it happens that the terrors of conscience, by which a despairing soul was struck down, are overcome and indeed driven out. The soul, having been relieved of the dreadful sense of divine judgment, which is inward and hidden, rests securely in the revealed and apprehended grace and goodwill of God, is flooded with inexpressible joy, and by enjoying it is truly blessed. From this comes that excellent victory of the faithful, and the glorious triumph which they win against the judgment of reason and the world, over all the temptations of sin and of the cross, in the midst of calamities and as the fruit of afflictions. If God be for us, who can be against us? He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things? Who shall lay anything to the charge of God's elect? It is God that justifieth. Who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us. Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us. For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord (Rom. 8:31–39); and So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory. O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory? The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law. But thanks be to God, who giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ (1 Cor. 15:54–57). Those who think otherwise, and confuse faith with confidence and the objects of each, entangle themselves in the greatest and most serious difficulties, and I cannot see how they can extricate themselves from them.

units.la: Alter fidei effectus, qui mediante fiducia producitur, est Spes, id est, certa vitae aeternae gloriae velestis una cum Christo in coelo plenè fruendae, expectatio: Roman. cap. 5. ver. 5. Porro spes non pudeficit, quod charitas Dei effusa sit in cordibus nostris per Spiritum S. qui datus est nobis: & 8. v. 21. 23. 24. 25. sub spe, quod & ipsa vindicabuntur ex servitute interitus in libertatem gloriae filiorum Dei, &c. Neque illa solum, sed & ipsi, qui primitias Spiritus habemus, nos ipsi, inquam, apud nos ipsos suspiramus, adoptionem expectates, redemptionem corporis nostri. Nam spe servati sumus: spes autem si cernatur, non est spes: quod etiam quis cernit, cur speret? Si vero quod non videmus speramus, per patientiam expectamus.
units.tr: The other effect of faith, which is produced through confidence, is hope, that is, the certain expectation of eternal life and of the glory of heaven to be fully enjoyed with Christ: And hope maketh not ashamed, because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us (Rom. 5:5); and in hope, that the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God (Rom. 8:21), and not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body. For we are saved by hope; but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for? But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it (Rom. 8:23–25).

units.la: Tertius fidei effectus est studium bonorum operum, & gratitudinis erga Deum, tum secundum veritate, qua videt homo fidelis agnoscit, & profitetur summum illud & ineffabile gratuitæ redemptionis beneficium, tum secundùm iustitiam, qua videlicet debitæ pietatis erga Deum, & charitatis erga proximū officia pro viribus præstare conatur. Matth.7. verf.16.17. Num colligunt ex spinis uuam,aut ex tribulis ficus? Ita omnis arbor bona fert fructus bonos, putris autem arbor fert fructus malos:non potest arbor bona fructus malos facere, neque arbor putris fructus bonos ferre. Galat.5.verf.6. In Christo Iesu nec circumcisio quicquam valet,neque præputium,sed fides per charitatem agens. 1.Timoth.1.ver.6. Finis mandati est charitas,ex puro corde,& conscientia bona,&fide non simulata. Tit.1.v.1. Paulus servus Dei,Apostolus autem Iesu Christi,secundum fidem electorum Dei,&agnitionem veritatis,quæ est secundum pietatem:& 2.verf.11.12. Illuxit gratia illa Dei salutifera omnibus hominibus,erudiens nos,ut abnegata impietate,& mundanis cupiditatibus, temperatè, & iustè, & piè viuamus in hoc præsenti seculo. Iacob.2.v.14. Quæ vtilitas,fratres mei,si fidem dicat aliquis habere se,opera verò non habeat, num potest fides illa eum seruare? v.17. Fides si opera non habeat,mortua est per se. v.18. Tu fidem habes,& ego opera habeo,ostende mihi fidem tuam ex operibus tuis,&ego tibi ostendam fidem meam ex operibus meis:& v.26. Sicut corpus absque spiritu mortuum est, ita & fides absque operibus mortua est. 1.Ioh.3. v.10. Per hoc manifesti sunt filij Dei, & filij diaboli: quisquis non exercet iustitiam,non est ex Deo,& qui non diligit fratrem suum. Hoc pietatis & bonorum operum studium ita effectum ipsius fidei iustificantis appellamus, vt tamen bona opera ad salutem consequendam necessaria esse agnoscamus, necessitate videlicet cultus & obsequii nostri Deo debiti,necessitate bonæ conscientiæ,quæ amittitur,neglectis bonis operibus,denique necessitate officii erga proximum, quem sanctis inculpatæ vitæ exemplis Christo lucrifacere tenemur, ac proinde sine bonis operibus neminem salutem consequi posse,ex scripturis ipsis affirmamus. Matth.5. v.20. Nisi excellentior fuerit iustitia vestra,quàm Scribarum & Pharisæorum,nequaquam ingrediemini in regnū cœlorum.Et 7. v.25. Non omnis qui dicit Domine,Domine,ingredietur in regnū cœlorum, sed qui facit voluntatem Patris mei qui in cœlis est:&25.v.34.35.36. Venite benedicti Patris mei,hereditario iure possidete regnum paratum vobis inde à iactu fundamentis mundi: Esuriui enim,& dedistis mihi quo vescerer,&c. Iacob.1.v.25. Qui intro-spexerit in perfectam illam legem libertatis, & in ea permanserit, is quia non fueris auditor obliuiosus,sed effector operis, beatus erit in opere suo, id est, propter opus suum. Et alibi passim.
units.tr: The third effect of faith is the pursuit of good works and gratitude toward God, both according to truth, by which the faithful man sees, acknowledges and professes that highest and inexpressible benefit of free redemption, and according to righteousness, by which he endeavours, as far as his strength allows, to perform the duties of due piety toward God and of love toward his neighbour. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit (Matt. 7:16–18). For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which worketh by love (Gal. 5:6). Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned (1 Tim. 1:5–6). Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness (Titus 1:1); and, For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world (Titus 2:11–12). What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? Can faith save him? (James 2:14). Faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone (James 2:17). Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works (James 2:18). And For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also (James 2:26). In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother (1 John 3:10). We call this zeal for piety and good works an effect of justifying faith in such a way that we nonetheless acknowledge good works to be necessary for obtaining salvation: necessary by the necessity of the worship and obedience we owe to God; necessary for the sake of a good conscience, which is lost when good works are neglected; and finally necessary by the duty we owe to our neighbour, whom we are bound to win to Christ by the holy examples of an blameless life. Accordingly, we affirm from Scripture itself that no one can obtain salvation without good works. Except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven (Matt. 5:20). And Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven (Matt. 7:21); and Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: for I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat, etc. (Matt. 25:34–35). But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed (James 1:25), that is, on account of his work. And elsewhere, everywhere.

units.la: Quartus fidei effectus ac fructus, qui cæteros propemodum omnes in sese complectitur, est vnio cum Christo, id est, spiritualis, eaque arctissima, ac proinde mystice essentialis coniunctio, qua fideles à Deo & Iesu Christo Σωτῆρι per Spiritum sanctum, & fidem ipsi Christo immediatè, & per Christum Mediatorem Deo connexi, vnum cum ipso & Deo fiunt, & omnium bonorum eius participes redduntur, ad salutem suam, & Christi Mediatoris ac Dei gloriam. Ioh. 15. v. 4. 5. Manete in me, & ego in vobis, sicut palmes non potest ferre fructum à semetipso, nisi manserit in vite: ita nec vos, nisi in me manseritis. Ego sum vitis, vos palmites, is qui manet in me, & in quo ego maneo, hic fert fructum multum: nam absque me nihil potestis facere. & 17. v. 11. Pater sancte, serua eos per nomen tuum, quos dedisti mihi, vt sint vnum sicut & nos. Et v. 21. 22. Vt omnes vnum sint, sicut tu Pater in me, & ego in te, vt & ipsi in nobis vnū sint, vt credat mundus me à te missum esse, & ego gloriam quam dedisti mihi dedi eis, vt sint vnum, sicut & nos vnum sumus. Eph. 1. v. 22. 23. Omnia subiecit pedibus eius, eumque constituit caput super omnia ipsi Ecclesiæ, quæ est corpus ipsius, & complementum eius, qui omnia implet in omnibus. & 5. verf. 30. Quoniam membra sumus corporis eius, ex carne eius, & ex ossibus eius. Ex hac vero vnione fluit ipsa communio cum Christo, qua fideles ipsi vniti, omnia, quæ ipsius sunt, cum eo, per complantationem, quæ fit similitudine mortis & vitæ ipsius conformatione, ac beneficiorum vtrinque promanantium participationem, communia habent, seruata tamen distinctione, quæ inter caput & membra est, inter eum qui communicat, & qui participat, qui sanctificat, & qui sanctificantur. Rom. 6. v. 4. Sepulti sumus vna cum eo per baptismum in mortem, vt sicut excitatus est Christus ex mortuis in gloriam Patris, ita & nos nova vita ambulemus. v. 5. Nam si cum eo plantati coaluimus conformatione mortis eius, nimirum etiam resurrectionis conformatione coalescemus. v. 8. Quod si mortui sumus cum Christo, credimus fore, vt etiam viuamus cum eo. verf. 11. Ita & vos colligite videlicet ipsos tum mortuos esse peccato, tum vero viuere Deo per Christum Iesum Dominum nostrum. Et 8. v. 1. Nulla est condemnatio iis qui sunt in Christo Iesu, qui non secundum carnem incedunt, sed secundum Spiritum. v. 10. Si Christus in vobis est, corpus quidem mortuum est propter peccatum, Spiritus autem vita est propter iustitiam. verf. 11. Si Spiritus eius, qui excitauit Iesum à mortuis, habitat in vobis, is qui excitauit Christum ex mortuis, viuificabit etiam mortalia vestra corpora, per inhabitantem eius Spiritum in vobis. v. 32. Is quidem qui proprio Filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit eum, qui non etiam cum eo nobis gratificabitur? 1.Cor. 1. verf.30. Ex ipso vos estis in Christo Iesu, qui factus est nobis sapientia a Deo, iustitia, & sanctificatio, & redemptio. Eph.2. v.5.6. Quum per offensas mortui essemus, una viuificauit nos per Christum, cuius gratia estis seruati, unaque excitauit, unaque collocauit in caelis in Christo Iesu. Philip.3. verf.10 11. Vt agnoscam eum, & vim resurrectionis ipsius, & communionem perpessionum ipsius, dum conformis fio ipsius morti: ecquo modo perueniam ad resurrectionem mortuorum. Coloff.2. v.10.11.12.13. Et estis in eo completi, qui est caput omnis imperii ac potestatis, in quo etiam circumcisi estis circumcisione quae fit sine manibus, dum corpus carnis peccato obnoxium exuistis per circumcisionem Christi. Consepulti cum eo per baptismum, per quem etiam cum eo resurrexistis, per fidem Dei efficaciter agentis, qui excitauit eum ex mortuis, vosque mortuos in peccatis, & praeputio carnis vestrae, cum eo viuificauit, condonatis vobis omnibus peccatis: & alibi passim. Hinc liberatio a dominio & seruitute peccati, a lege item, tum qua illa chirographum fuit aduersus nos, tum qua rigidus ac seuerus exactor debiti nostri, ac inutilis & inefficax propter carnem nostram: hinc resurrectio nostra in novam ac spiritualem vitam, & conuersatio in caelis secundum Spiritum, hinc adoptio in filios Dei, iustificatio, sanctificatio, & post hanc vitam resurrectio corporum, eorumque cum Christi corpore glorioso conformitas, & fruitio caelestis beatitatis, & beneficia reliqua omnia quae ex conformatione nostri, & communione cum Christo, tum in hac, tum in futura vita in nos redundant.
units.tr: The fourth effect and fruit of faith, which comprises almost all the others within itself, is union with Christ: a spiritual union, and that the closest, and therefore a mystically essential conjunction. By it the faithful, joined to God and to Jesus Christ the Saviour [Σωτῆρι] through the Holy Spirit, and joined to Christ himself immediately by faith and to God through Christ the Mediator, become one with him and with God, and are made partakers of all his good things, to their own salvation and to the glory of Christ the Mediator and of God. John 15:4, 5. Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abide in the vine, so neither can you, unless you abide in me. I am the vine, you are the branches: he who abides in me, and I in him, the same bears much fruit; for without me you can do nothing. And 17:11. Holy Father, keep through your name those whom you have given me, that they may be one, as we are. And vv. 21, 22. That they all may be one, as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us, that the world may believe that you have sent me; and the glory which you gave me I have given to them, that they may be one, as we are one. Eph. 1:22, 23. He has put all things under his feet, and has appointed him head over all things to the Church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all. And 5:30. For we are members of his body, of his flesh and of his bones. From this union flows the communion with Christ itself, by which the faithful, being united to him, have in common with him all that is his: through the planting together, which takes place by the likeness of his death and life, through the conformity to him, and through the sharing of the benefits flowing from each to the other; yet the distinction is preserved that lies between head and members, between him who imparts and those who receive, between him who sanctifies and those who are sanctified. Rom. 6:4. We were buried with him by baptism into death, so that, as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life. v. 5. For if we have been planted together with him in the likeness of his death, we shall surely also be joined together in the likeness of his resurrection. v. 8. But if we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him. v. 11. So you too, reckon yourselves indeed dead to sin, but alive to God through Christ Jesus our Lord. And 8:1. There is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit. v. 10. If Christ is in you, the body is indeed dead because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness. v. 11. If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies, through his Spirit dwelling in you. v. 32. He who did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all, how will he not also with him freely give us all things? 1 Cor. 1:30. From him you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, righteousness, sanctification and redemption. Eph. 2:5, 6. When we were dead through our trespasses, he made us alive together with Christ, by whose grace you have been saved, and raised us up together, and seated us together in the heavens in Christ Jesus. Phil. 3:10, 11. That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, becoming conformed to his death, if somehow I may attain to the resurrection of the dead. Col. 2:10–13. And you are complete in him, who is the head of every rule and authority; in him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, when you put off the body of the flesh, subject to sin, through the circumcision of Christ. Buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead, and when you were dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made you alive together with him, having forgiven you all your sins. and elsewhere in many places. Hence comes liberation from the dominion and slavery of sin; also from the law, both that which was a handwriting against us and that which, as a harsh and severe exactor of our debt, was useless and ineffective because of our flesh. Hence comes our resurrection into a new and spiritual life, and our conversation in heaven according to the Spirit; hence adoption into the sons of God, justification, sanctification, and after this life the resurrection of the bodies, their conformity to the glorious body of Christ, and the enjoyment of heavenly blessedness, and all the other benefits which flow into us, both in this life and in the future, from our conformity to and communion with Christ.

units.la: Restant adiuncta fidei iustificantis, videlicet vnitas & perduratio. Vnitas est quod fides iustificans vna est specie in omnibus qui iustificantur & saluantur, non multiplex: Eph 4. v.5. Vnus Dominus, vna fides, vnum baptisma: unde illam ἑνότητα appellauit Apostolus, 2.Pet.1. v.1. Simon Petrus seruus & Apostolus Iesu Christi, iis qui aeque pretiosam fidem (ἰσότιμον πίστιν) nobiscum sortiti sunt: licet numero & gradu diuersa sit. Numero, quia vnusquisque sua fide viuit, non aliena. Luc 7. v.50. & 8. v.48. Fides tua te seruauit. Gradu quia vnicuique mensuram eius prout vult, admetitur Dominus. Rom.12. v.3. Quisque sapiat ad sobrietatem, prout cuique Deus partitus est mensura fidei. Matth.8. v.10. Amen dico vobis, nec in Israel quidem tantam fidem inueni. Et 15. v.28. O mulier, magna est fides tua! Perduratio est donum pernum perseueran-tiæ, quo fit vt illa nunquam penitus deficiat, exa-rescat, aut extinguatur, quantumuis interdum tentationum pro-cellis obruatur, ac veluti sepeliatur. Rom.8. ver.38.39. Mihi persua-sum est, neque mortem, neque vitam, neque Angelos, neque principatus, neque potestates, neque instantia, neque futura, neque sublimitatem, ne-que profunditatem, neque vllam rem aliam creatam, posse nos separare à charitate Dei, quæ est in Christo Iesu Domino nostro. Iohan.10. v.27. 28. Oues meæ vocem meam audiunt, & ego eas agnosco, & sequuntur me: & ego vitam æternam do eis, nec peribunt in æternum, neque rapiet eas quisquam ex manu mea. Rom.11.verf.29. Dona & vocatio Dei sunt ἀμεταμέλητα. Luc.22.verf.31.32. Simon, Simon, ecce Satanas appetiit vos, quos ventilaret sicut triticum: sed ego rogaui pro te, ne deficiat fides tua. 1.Petr.1.v.5. Qui virtute Dei custodimur per fidem ad salutem, quæ parata est patefieri tempore vltimo. & v.23. Renati non ex semine mortali, sed ex immortali per sermonem Dei viui, & manentis in æternum: & alibi passim. Deus Opt. Max. salutarem illum fidei fruticem, quem prædicatione Euangelii, & illuminatione Spiritus sancti in mentibus nostris eduxit, gratiæ suæ radiis conserues, foueat, & augeat, donec aliquando gloriosum illud præmium, vitam videlicet æternam, cum omnibus electis consequamur, per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum. Amen.
units.tr: There remain the attributes that accompany justifying faith, namely its unity and its perseverance. Unity means that justifying faith is one in kind in all who are justified and saved, not manifold. Eph. 4:5. One Lord, one faith, one baptism. Hence the Apostle called it [ἑνότητα] unity, 2 Pet. 1:1. Simon Peter, servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained a faith of equal honour [ἰσότιμον πίστιν] with us. Yet it differs in number and in degree. In number, because each lives by his own faith, not by another's. Luke 7:50 and 8:48. Your faith has saved you. In degree, because the Lord measures out to each a portion of it as he wills. Rom. 12:3. Let each think with sober judgment, according as God has allotted to each a measure of faith. Matt. 8:10. Truly I say to you, I have not found such great faith even in Israel. And 15:28. O woman, great is your faith! Perseverance is the gift of an everlasting perseverance, by which faith never wholly fails, withers, or is extinguished, however much at times it may be overwhelmed by the storms of temptations and, as it were, buried. Rom. 8:38, 39. I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. John 10:27, 28. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me; and I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish, and no one shall snatch them out of my hand. Rom. 11:29. The gifts and calling of God are [ἀμεταμέλητα] irrevocable. Luke 22:31, 32. Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has demanded to sift you like wheat; but I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail. 1 Pet. 1:5. Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation, ready to be revealed in the last time. And v. 23. Born again not of perishable seed but of imperishable, through the living and abiding word of God; and elsewhere in many places. May God, the best and greatest, keep, cherish and increase that saving shoot of faith which he has brought forth in our minds by the preaching of the Gospel and the illumination of the Holy Spirit, by the rays of his grace, until at last we attain that glorious reward, namely eternal life, together with all the elect, through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

units.la: CAPVT XXXI.
units.tr: CAPUT XXXI.

units.la: In quo sententia Aduersarij de Fide Iustificante, exponitur, ac refellitur.
units.tr: In which the opponent's view of justifying faith is set out and refuted.

units.la: STORRODIVS Institutionum suarum capite secundo (nam loco & doctrinæ de scriptura sacra, statim doctrinam de fide in Deum subiicit) duabus partibus videlicet καταφατικῇ & ἀποφατικῇ disputationem de fide iustificante absoluit: illa quidem doctrinam Samosatenianorum breuiter proponit, & quibus potest argumentis confirmat: hac vero tum Pontificiorum, tum nostram sententiam & doctrinam de nominato articulo pro viribus refutat. Nos vestigia ipsius sequemur. Quantum igitur ipsam prothasin, & fidei definitionem concernit, quæ habetur sectione prima, dicit, Credere in Deum nihil aliud esse quam fiduciam in ipsum collocare, & ipsi obedire. Atque hanc vtramque definitionem, quod videlicet fides nihil aliud fit, quàm fiducia in Deum collocata, fiducia vero nihil aliud quàm præceptis diuinis præstita obedientia, quatuor argumentis ex scriptura sacra desumptis probare conatur.
units.tr: Storrodius, in the second chapter of his Institutes (for, instead of placing it where it belongs, he puts the doctrine of faith in God straight after the doctrine of Holy Scripture), has completed his discussion of justifying faith in two parts: cataphatic [καταφατικῇ] and apophatic [ἀποφατικῇ]. The former briefly sets out the doctrine of the Samosatenes and confirms it with such arguments as he can muster; the latter refutes, as well as it can, both the view of the Papists and our own opinion and doctrine on the said article. We shall follow in his footsteps. As for the proposition itself and the definition of faith, which is given in the first section, he says: To believe in God is nothing other than to place one's trust in him and to obey him. He tries to prove this twofold definition from four arguments drawn from Holy Scripture: that faith is nothing other than trust placed in God, and that trust is nothing other than obedience rendered to the divine precepts.

units.la: Argumentum I. desumitur ex Psalm. 78. v. 21 22. vbi Deus ideo in populum Israeliticum succensuisse & iratus fuisse legitur, quia videlicet Israelitæ in ipsum non crediderant, nec confisi erant in salute eius. Hanc ipsam vero incredulitatem nihil aliud fuisse, quam quod illi fiduciam suam in Deum non collocarint, nec debitam obedientiam ipsi præstiterint. Ex toto Psalmo, inprimis vero ex ver. 7.8.9.10. vbi Asaph posteros populi illius hortatur, vt in Deo ponant fiduciam suam, & custodiant præcepta eius, neque imitentur maiores ipsorum, qui non seruauerant fœdus Dei, & in præceptis eius ambulare renuerant, manifestum esse inquit.
units.tr: The first argument is drawn from Psalm 78, verses 21 and 22, where God is read to have been kindled to anger and wrath against the people of Israel because, that is, the Israelites did not believe in him nor trust in his salvation. This very unbelief, however, was nothing other than their not having placed their trust in God nor having rendered him the obedience due to him. That this is plain from the whole Psalm, and especially from verses 7 to 10, where Asaph exhorts the posterity of that people to place their trust in God and keep his precepts, and not to imitate their forefathers, who had not kept God's covenant and had refused to walk in his precepts, he says.

units.la: Argumentum tale est.
units.tr: The argument runs as follows.

units.la: Si Deus ideo in populum Israeliticum succensuit, & iratus fuit, quia videlicet Israelitæ in ipsum non crediderant, nec confisi erant in salute salute eius: hac ipsa vero incredulitas nihil aliud fuit, quàm quod Israelita fiduciam suam in Deum non collocarint, nec debitam obedientiam ipsi praestiterint, tum sequitur fidem in Deum esse fiduciam in ipsum collocatam, & obedientiam, quae ipsius praeceptis praestatur:
units.tr: If God was kindled to anger and wrath against the people of Israel because, that is, the Israelites did not believe in him nor trust in his salvation, and this unbelief was nothing other than the Israelites not having placed their trust in God nor having rendered him the obedience due to him, then it follows that faith in God is trust placed in him, and obedience which is rendered to his precepts.

units.la: Atqui prius verum est: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: But the first is true. Therefore the second is too.

units.la: Assumptionis pars posterior sic probatur.
units.tr: The latter part of the assumption is proved thus.

units.la: Si Asaph in eodem Psalmo posteros Israelitici populi hortatur, ut in Deo ponant fiduciam suam, & custodiant praecepta eius, neque imitentur maiores ipsorum, qui non seruauerant foedus Dei, & in praeceptis eius ambulare renuerant: tum sequitur illam Israelitarum incredulitatem, ob quam Deus excanduerat, nihil aliud fuisse quàm quod illi fiduciam suam in Deum non collocarint, nec debitam obedientiam ipsi praestiterint.
units.tr: If Asaph, in the same Psalm, exhorts the posterity of the Israelite people to place their trust in God and keep his precepts, and not to imitate their forefathers, who had not kept God's covenant and had refused to walk in his precepts, then it follows that that unbelief of the Israelites, for which God had burned with anger, was nothing other than their not having placed their trust in God nor having rendered him the obedience due to him.

units.la: Atqui prius verum est, ut patet ex verf. 7. 8. 9. 10.
units.tr: But the first is true, as is plain from verses 7, 8, 9 and 10.

units.la: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: Therefore the second is too.

units.la: Argumentum II. desumit ex Daniel. 6. v. 23. vbi Deus dicitur ideo Danielem saluum & illaesum in leonum fouea conseruasse, & ex illa liberasse, quia videlicet in illum crediderat. Hanc vero Danielis fidem nihil aliud fuisse quàm fiduciam in Deo collocatam, & obedientiā mandatis ipsius praestitam, tam manifestum esse inquit, vt nulla probatione indigeat: dubitanti vero, colloquium illud Regis habitum cum Daniele fidem facere posse.
units.tr: The second argument is drawn from Daniel 6, verse 23, where God is said to have preserved Daniel safe and unharmed in the lions' den and to have freed him from it because, that is, Daniel had believed in him. This faith of Daniel, however, was nothing other than trust placed in God and obedience rendered to his commands; this is so plain, he says, that it needs no proof. To one who doubts, however, that conversation which the king held with Daniel can furnish proof.

units.la: Argumentum tale est.
units.tr: The argument runs as follows.

units.la: Si Deus Danielem ideo saluum & immunem ab iniurijs leonum conseruauit, quia videlicet Daniel in Deum credidit: tum sequitur fidem iustificantem nihil aliud esse, quàm fiduciam in Deum collocatam, & obedientiam, quae ipsius mandatis praestatur: quia videlicet ex colloquio Regis Darij cum Daniele habito, apparet fidem Danielis nihil aliud quàm fiduciam in Deum collocatam, & obedientiam praeceptis ipsius praestitam fuisse.
units.tr: If God preserved Daniel safe and free from the injuries of the lions because Daniel believed in God, then it follows that justifying faith is nothing other than trust placed in God and obedience rendered to his commands, because, that is, it appears from the conversation which King Darius held with Daniel that Daniel's faith was nothing other than trust placed in God and obedience rendered to his precepts.

units.la: Atqui prius verum est: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: But the first is true. Therefore the second is too.

units.la: Argumentum tertium desumit ab exemplo Niniuitarum, quod Iohan. capite 3. describitur, Quorum fidem inquit, nihil aliud fuisse, quàm fiduciam illam, quâ certò fuerunt persuasi, Deum si sese coram illo humiliarent ac resipiscerent, poenam quam ipsis minatus erat, condonaturum esse.
units.tr: The third argument is drawn from the example of the Ninevites, which is described in John chapter 3. Their faith, he says, was nothing other than that trust by which they were firmly persuaded that God, if they humbled themselves before him and repented, would forgive the punishment with which he had threatened them.

units.la: Argumentum tale est.
units.tr: The argument runs as follows.

units.la: Si fides Niniuitarū nihil aliud fuit quàm fiducia illa, qua certò persuasi fuerunt, Deum ipsis, si sese coram illo humiliarent ac resipiscerent, poenam quam ipsis minatus fuit, clementer condonaturum esse: tum sequitur fidem iustificantem nihil aliud esse, quàm fiduciam in Deum collocatam, & obedientiam praeceptis ipsius praestitam:
units.tr: If the faith of the Ninevites was nothing other than that trust by which they were firmly persuaded that God, if they humbled themselves before him and repented, would mercifully forgive the punishment with which he had threatened them, then it follows that justifying faith is nothing other than trust placed in God and obedience rendered to his precepts.

units.la: Atqui prius verum est: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: But the first is true. Therefore the second is too.

units.la: Argumentum quintum ita tractat, vt affirmet primò, Fidem illam ob quam hactenus sancti homines Deo placuerint, talem (qualem videlicet hactenus definiuit) fuisse, neque etiam quenquam nisi eandem ob fidem Deo placere posse, vt in epist. ad Heb. cap. 11. ver. 6. diserte docetur: Nam qui accedit ad Deū, hunc credere oportet esse Deum, & praemia largiri iis qui ipsum requirunt. Secundò inde concludit, quum nemo absque fide Deo placere possit, ideo eos omnes qui unquam Deo placuerunt, fide illa praeditos fuisse, omnesque quotquot Deo placere velint, eadem illa fide praeditos esse oportere, id est, omnes tam qui ante legem, & sub lege extiterunt, quàm qui sub Euangelio viuent, vno eodemque modo à Deo iustificari: nempe per fidem in Deum, quae nihil aliud sit, quā confidentia seu fiducia in Deo collocata, & obedientia ipsi praestita. Quoniam enim credant Deum non tantum esse, sed etiam remuneratorem existere eorum qui ipsum quaerunt, id est, eorum qui ipsum timent, & debitam obedientiam ipsi praestant, ideo illos perspicere, se nisi Deum praedicto modo quaerant, ipsi placere non posse. Tertiò ait, Deum quicquid vnquam egerit, vt homines ad singularem beneficiorum suorum participationem adduceret, ideo praestitisse, vt fidem illam in illis operaretur, praesertim verò omnia illa quae per Christum praestiterit, vtpote quod Euangelium, id est, propensam suam erga nos voluntatem per ipsum nobis annunciauerit, idemque variis miraculis confirmauerit, Christūmque quatumuis sanctum, iustum & innocentem horrendis modis cruciari & trucidari permiserit, postmodum verò potenter & gloriosè ex mortuis excitauerit, ad dextram suam collocauerit, ipsumque Iudicem, Dominum ac Regem super omnia, tam quae in coelis, quàm quae in terra sunt, constituerit, illa omnia, inquit, Deum tantum ideò fecisse, vt, quoniam nos ad se adducere, id est, vitam aeternam, cuius sine fide nemo particeps fieri potest. test,nobis largiri voluit fidem illam, per Christum in nobis operaretur, atque eadem de causa Christum Hebr. 2.vers.12. fidei nostræ ducem ac perfectorem appellari.
units.tr: The fifth argument is handled in such a way that he first affirms that that faith through which holy men have hitherto pleased God was of such a kind (namely, of the kind he has so far defined), and that no one can please God except through the same faith, as is plainly taught in the Epistle to the Hebrews, chapter 11, verse 6: For he that cometh to God must believe that he is God, and that he rewards those who seek him. Secondly, from this he concludes that, since no one can please God without faith, therefore all those who have ever pleased God were endowed with that faith, and all who wish to please God must be endowed with the same faith, that is, all, both those who existed before the law and under the law and those who live under the Gospel, are justified by God in one and the same way: namely, through faith in God, which is nothing other than confidence or trust placed in God and obedience rendered to him. For since they believe that God not only exists but is also a rewarder of those who seek him, that is, of those who fear him and render him due obedience, therefore they see that they cannot please him unless they seek him in the manner described. Thirdly he says that whatever God has ever done, he did in order to lead men to a singular participation in his benefits, so that he might work that faith in them; especially all those things which he has accomplished through Christ, inasmuch as he announced through him the Gospel, that is, his well-disposed will toward us, and confirmed the same by various miracles, and permitted Christ, however holy, just and innocent, to be tortured and slaughtered in horrible ways, and afterwards powerfully and gloriously raised him from the dead, set him at his right hand, and appointed him Judge, Lord and King over all things, both those in heaven and those on earth: all these things, he says, God did only so that, since he wished to bring us to himself, that is, to eternal life, of which no one can be a partner without faith, he would bestow on us that faith which he works in us through Christ; and for this same reason Christ is called in Hebrews 2:12 the leader and perfecter of our faith.

units.la: Argumentum,quod præsentem quæstionem concernit, tale est.
units.tr: The argument that bears on the present question is this.

units.la: Si nemo placere potest Deo nisi per fidem, & omnes tam in veteri quàm Nouo Testamento, uno eodémque modo, id est, per fidem à Deo iu-stificantur: quotquot vero Deo per fidem placent, non tantùm credunt Deum esse, verùm etiam remuneratorem existere eorum qui ipsum quærunt: tum sequitur fidem iustificantem nihil aliud esse quàm confidentiam seu fiduciam in Deo collocatam, & obedien-tiam præceptis ipsius præstitam:
units.tr: If no one can please God except through faith, and all, both in the Old and in the New Testament, are justified by God in one and the same way, that is, through faith; and whoever pleases God through faith not only believes that God exists but also that he is a rewarder of those who seek him: then it follows that justifying faith is nothing other than confidence or trust placed in God, together with obedience rendered to his precepts.

units.la: Atqui prius verum est,vt patet ex Heb.11.vers.6.
units.tr: But the first is true, as is evident from Heb. 11.6.

units.la: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: Therefore the last is also true.

units.la: Connexi probatio hæc est.
units.tr: The proof of the connection is as follows.

units.la: Si quærere Deum nihil aliud est quàm ipsum timere & ei obedire,& illi ipsi qui in Deum credunt, sciunt se Deo placere non posse, nisi prædictò modo ipsum quærant: tum si nemo placere potest Deo, nisi per fidem, & omnes tam in Veteri quàm Nouo Testamento, uno eodémque modo, id est, per fidem, iustificantur, quotquot vero Deo per fidem placent, non tantùm credunt Deum esse, verùm etiam remuneratorem existere eorum qui ipsum quærunt: tum sequitur fidem iustificantem nihil aliud esse quàm confidentiam, seu fidu-ciam in Deo collocatam,& obedientiam ipsi præstitam.
units.tr: If to seek God is nothing other than to fear him and obey him, and those who believe in God know that they cannot please God unless they seek him in the aforesaid manner; then, if no one can please God except through faith, and all, both in the Old and in the New Testament, are justified in one and the same way, that is, through faith, and whoever pleases God through faith not only believes that God exists but also that he is a rewarder of those who seek him: then it follows that justifying faith is nothing other than confidence, or trust, placed in God, together with obedience rendered to him.

units.la: Atqui prius verum est: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: But the first is true; therefore the last is also true.

units.la: Resp.Nos prius sententiam Aduersarii breuiter refutabimus, deinde ad singula confirmationis allata argumenta ordine responde-bimus.Et primum quidem quantū concernit, tria illa ordine sunt tenenda. Primò,in definitione fidei iustificantis ab Aduersario tra-dita, & genus,nempe habitum spiritualem, & formam, videlicet notitiam ac assensum, contrà iustæ definitionis leges omitti, & vice illius duplicem effectum, nempe fiduciam, & pietatis bonorúmque operum studium substitui. Notitiam enim, & cognitionem veritatis, ad essentiæ & naturæ ipsius fidei iustificantis constitutionem necessario requiri, capite antecedente à nobis est demonstratum,& ex eo liquet euidentissimè,quòd rei ignotæ nec assentiri nec fidere possumus : & quod Efaiæ capite quinquagesimo tertio, versu vndecimo de Christo dicitur, Cognitione sui seruus meus iustificabit multos : vnde apparet, fidem iustificantem esse cognitionem ac notitiam, si quidem in nobis nihil est præter fidem, quo coram Deo iustificemur. Et Christus ipse Iohan. capite decimo septimo, versu tertio, vitam æternam collocat in cognitione Dei : Hæc est vita æterna, inquiens, vt te solum cognoscant verum Deum, & quem misisti Iesum Christum. Cum igitur nemo ignarus vitæ æternæ particeps fieri possit, omnis autem qui credit, vitam æternam habeat, necessario sequitur, eum qui credit, credendo Deum cognoscere, atque ita fidem esse notitiam. Eandem verò fidem etiam assensum esse, præterquam quod ex multis scripturæ sacræ testimoniis probari potest, ipse etiam Samosatenianorum Antesignanus, Faustus Socinus disertè fatetur : sic enim in libro de Iesu Christo Seruatore, parte quarta, capite vndecimo inter cætera scribit : Quamuis credere in aliquem, proprie illi confidere significet, adeo vt in eum quoque qui nihil affirmet, credi possit, tamen cum ad eum qui aliquid affirmat, refertur, tum non ipsam confidentiam nostram, sed assensum quoque affirmatæ rei declarat. Et paulò post : Quapropter, quamuis fides in Christum, id est, hac loquutio propria vi nihil aliud quàm confidentiam in Christo declaret, quæ alicuius rei ab ipso affirmatæ assensum, citráque obedientiam aliquam suapte natura consistere potest : tamen, cùm Christus nonnulla præceperit, & affirmauerit, fide in Christum non simplex quædam, quæ in Christo collocetur, confidentia solùm exprimitur, sed ÿs etiam quæ affirmauit firmus adhibitus assensus, & eius præceptorum obedientia omnino comprehenditur. Ex quibus apparet definitionem fidei iustificantis ab Aduersario allatam, vitiosam ac heterogeneam esse.
units.tr: Reply. We shall first refute the opponent's view briefly, and then answer in order the separate arguments brought forward in the confirmation. And, as far as concerns the first point, three things must be kept in order. First, in the definition of justifying faith given by the opponent, the genus, namely a spiritual habit, and the form, namely knowledge and assent, are omitted contrary to the rules of a proper definition, and in their place a twofold effect is substituted, namely trust and a zeal for piety and good works. For we demonstrated in the preceding chapter that knowledge and cognition of the truth are necessarily required for the constitution of the essence and nature of justifying faith itself; and from this it is quite evident that we can neither assent to nor trust in a thing unknown. And in Isaiah 53.11 it is said of Christ, By his knowledge shall my servant justify many; whence it appears that justifying faith is cognition and knowledge, since in us there is nothing, besides faith, by which we are justified before God. And Christ himself, in John 17.3, places eternal life in the knowledge of God: This is eternal life, he says, that they may know you the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent. Since, then, no one who is ignorant can become a partaker of eternal life, and since everyone who believes has eternal life, it necessarily follows that he who believes knows God by believing, and so faith is knowledge. That this same faith is also assent, besides what can be proved from many testimonies of holy Scripture, Faustus Socinus, the forerunner of the Samosatenians, plainly confesses himself; for in his book on Jesus Christ the Saviour, part four, chapter eleven, he writes among other things: Although to believe in someone properly signifies to trust in him, so that one can be believed even if he affirms nothing, yet when it is referred to one who affirms something, it declares not only our trust but also assent to the thing affirmed. And a little later: Wherefore, although faith in Christ, that is, this expression by its proper force declares nothing other than confidence in Christ, which can exist in its own nature apart from assent to some thing affirmed by him and apart from any obedience; yet, since Christ has commanded and affirmed several things, by faith in Christ is expressed not merely a certain simple confidence placed in Christ, but also the firm assent given to what he has affirmed, and obedience to his precepts is wholly included. From these things it appears that the definition of justifying faith given by the opponent is faulty and incongruous.

units.la: Secundò, fidem iustificantem à fiducia non quidem diuellendam ac separandam, sed distinguendam, nec confundendam cum illa,sed tanquam effectum cum sua causa coniungendam esse, superiori capite à nobis prolixè fuisse demonstratum.
units.tr: Second, justifying faith is not to be torn apart and separated from trust, but distinguished from it, not confused with it, and joined to it as an effect with its cause; this was demonstrated by us at length in the preceding chapter.

units.la: Tertiò fidem iustificantem, cum eius fructibus, obedientia videlicet & bonis operibus, seu pietate erga Deum, & charitate erga proximum, contra ipsius Scripturæ veritatem, & fidei iustificantis cantis naturam, imperitè ab Aduersario confundi, dum videlicet statuit, fidem iustificantem nihil aliud esse quàm confidentiam, seu fiduciam in Deum collocatam : hanc verò, nempe fiduciam, nomine obedientiæ præceptis diuinis præstandæ definiri debere. Necessariò enim inde sequitur, fidem iustificantem & bona opera, ac studium pietatis reipsa vnum idémque esse, & charitatem fidei iustificanti formam constituere.
units.tr: Third, justifying faith, together with its fruits, namely obedience and good works, or piety towards God and charity towards neighbour, is rashly confused by the opponent, contrary to the truth of Scripture itself and to the nature of justifying faith; namely, when he lays down that justifying faith is nothing other than confidence, or trust, placed in God, and that this trust, namely, must be defined as obedience to be rendered to the divine commands. For it necessarily follows from this that justifying faith and good works and the zeal for piety are in fact one and the same thing, and that charity constitutes the form of justifying faith.

units.la: Quod ipsum etiam Faustus Socinus docuit. Sic enim in respon-sione ad quæstiones Anonymi cuiusdam, de fide & operibus, quod attinet ad iustificationem nostram, inter cætera inquit: Hæc sola res est, quæ pro Dei misericordia nos illi ad vitam æternam gratos efficit, nempe Christo confidere, eique se totum tradere, id quod reipsa nihil aliud est, quàm eius præceptis obedire, spe futuræ immortalitatis, quemadmodum breuiter explicat Paulus in epistola ad Titum, circa finem secundi capitis. Et paulò post in responsione ad quæstionem primam: Quod attinet ad opera, quæ Christi fidem subsequuntur, si de vera ac propria subsequutione loquimur, ita vt opera sint quiddam reipsa à fide distinctum, hæc Christi fides in tua quæstione nihil aliud erit, quàm prior illa fides, hoc est, credere Christum Iesum reuera esse Christum Dei filium, &c. opera verò erunt reipsa posterior illa fides, id est, Christo confidere. Item : Vnde constat opera nequaquam simpliciter esse fidei fructus, vt vulgò dicitur, sed fidei formæ perfectionem indere, & vitam, vt sic dixerim, tribuere. Hæc ille.
units.tr: Faustus Socinus himself also taught this. For in his reply to the questions of a certain Anonymous on faith and works, as far as concerns our justification, he says among other things: This alone is the thing which, by God's mercy, makes us acceptable to him for eternal life, namely to trust in Christ and to surrender ourselves wholly to him, which in fact is nothing other than to obey his precepts, in the hope of future immortality, as Paul briefly explains in his epistle to Titus, near the end of the second chapter. And a little later, in the reply to the first question: As for works which follow faith in Christ, if we speak of a true and proper following, so that works are something in fact distinct from faith, then this faith in Christ in your question will be nothing other than that former faith, that is, to believe that Jesus Christ is truly the Christ, the Son of God, etc.; and the works will in fact be that latter faith, that is, trust in Christ. Likewise: Whence it is clear that works are by no means simply the fruits of faith, as is commonly said, but bestow on the form of faith its perfection and, so to speak, its life. Thus he.

units.la: Atqui fidem iustificantem, & obedientiam diuinis mandatis præstandam non vnum ac idem, verum illam ob hæc tanquam arborem à fructu, & causam ab effecto distin-guendam esse, plurimis, iisque certissimis argumentis demonstratur. Quæ enim non ὁμωνύμως tantùm & ratione, sed etiam definitione perfecta differunt, illa reipsa vnum ac idem esse non possunt : Atqui fides iustificans, & bona opera differunt definitione, quia fides testante Apostolo, est ὑπόστασις ἐλπιζομένων, & πραγμάτων οὐ βλεπομένων ἔλεγχος, id est, hypostasis, quæ facit vt extent quæ sperantur, & quæ demonstrat quæ non videntur. Seu: Fides iustificans est habitus infusus à Spiritu S. in animo hominis, quo Christum Iesum Mediatorem Dei & hominum, cum bonis & donis ipsius omnibus, nouimus, apprehedimus ac percipimus, ad Dei gloriam, & animarum nostrarum salutem: Atqui bona opera non sunt ciufmodi habitus à Spiritu sancto infusus, sed sunt actiones supernaturales, quæ operante spiritu sancto,à regeneratis & iustificatis,ex vera fide proficiscuntur,& fiunt fecundùm legem Dei, ad nominis diuini gloriam, proximi ædificationem,& fidei ac electionis nostræ confirmationem, quæ definitio ipsi fidei iustificanti competere non potest. Ergo fides iustificans, & bona opera nō sunt vnum & idem. Seu:quæ genere & forma,seu differentia fpecifica differunt,ea reipfa & effentia vnum & idem esse nequeunt: Atqui fides iustificans& bona opera differunt genere & forma seu differentia fpecifica. Genere: quia fides iustificans, vtpote virtus theologica est habitus infusus,bona vero opera non sunt habitus,sed actiones: Forma,quia fidei iustificatis forma est πληροφορία seu certa perfuafio,de veritate sermonis Euangelici,& salute,per solum Christum obtinenda,firmúsque assensus veritati illi adhibitus, ac proinde legitima ad obiectum suum proprium & adæquatum,Christum videlicet,ordinatio:bonorum vero operum forma est ipsa εὐνομία, seu congruentia eorum, & conformitas cum lege Dei, quemadmodū peccati & mali operis forma est ἀνομία, & aberratio à lege. Atqui vt lex & Euangelium, ita quoque vtriusque fœderis, legalis & Euangelici conditiones forma differunt, ac proinde fides iustificans nec præscribitur, nec iudicatur à lege,nec formam ac differentiam fpecificam à lege accipit. Lex enim perfectam, & numeris ac gradibus omnibus absolutam iustitiam & obedientiam flagitat, & vel minimam transgressionem æternæ maledictioni adiudicat: fides vero delictorum veniam deprecatur, eámque per & propter Christum promissam amplectitur. Vnde iam necessariò sequitur, fidem iustificantem & bona opera reipfa ac effentia vnum & idem esse non posse. Secundò: Si fidei iustificanti in scripturis sacris illi tribuuntur effectus, quæ bonis operibus, & charitati nulla ratione competere possunt: tum sequitur fidem iustificantem,& bona opera,seu charitatem reipfa vnum & idem dici non posse: Atqui prius verum esse,ex ipsis Scripturis sacris liquidò constat. Nam per fidem,nō vero per bona opera, aut charitatem ius filiorum Dei impetramus, cum Christo vnimur, omniúmque beneficiorum,ex vi mortis sepulturæ, resurrectionis, ac vitæ ipsius promanantium participes reddimur:Ioh.1.v.12. Quotquot eum acceperunt,dedit eis hanc dignitatem, tatem, vt filii Dei fierent, nempe iis, qui credunt in nomen eius. Rom. 11. v. 23. Sed & illi si non permanserint in infidelitate inserentur. Rom. 6. v. 3. 4. §. 6. 8. 11. An ignoratis, nos quotquot baptizati sumus in Christum Iesum, in mortem eius baptizatos esse? Sepulti igitur sumus unà cum eo per baptismum in mortè: vt sicut excitatus est Christus ex mortuis in gloriam Patris, ita & nos nova vita ambulemus. Nam si cum eo plantari coaluimus conformatione mortis eius, nimirum etiam resurrectionis conformatione coalescemus. Illud scientes, veterem illum hominem nostrum cum eo crucifixum esse, vt eneruetur corpus peccati, ne posthac nos seruiamus peccato &c. Quod si mortui sumus cum Christo, credimus fore vt etiam viuamus cum eo. Ita etiam vos colligite, vos ipsos tùm mortuos esse peccato, tum verò viuere Deo, per Christum Iesum Dominum nostrum. Galat. 2. v. 20. Vna cum Christo crucifixus sum. Viuo autem non amplius ego, sed viuit in me Christus, & vitam, quam nunc viuo in carne, viuo per fidem Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, & tradidit semetipsum pro me. Ephes. 3. v. 17. Det vobis, vt inhabitet Christus per fidem in cordibus vestris. Col. 2. v. 10. 11. 12. 13. Et estis in eo completi, qui est caput omnis imperii, ac potestatis: in quo etiam circumcisi estis circumcisione, quae fit sine manibus, dum corpus carnis peccato obnoxia exuistis, per circumcisionem Christi: Consepulti cum eo per baptismum, per quem etiam cum eo resurrexistis, per Fidem Dei efficaciter agentis qui excitauit eum ex mortuis, vosque mortuos in peccatis, & praeputio carnis vestra, cum eo viuificauerit condonatis vobis omnibus peccatis, &c. & c. 3. v. 1. 2. 3. Itaque si resurrexistis cum Christo, superna quaerite, vbi Christus est ad dexteram Dei sedens, superna curate, non terrestria. Nam mortui estis, & vita vestra abscondita est cum Christo in Deo. Atque vt vinculum vnionis cum Christo, ex parte credentium, est ipsa fides iustificans, per quam Christus habitat in cordibus nostris, ex parte vero Christi ipse Spiritus Christi, qui ex Christo capite nostro in credentes fluit, & per quem fideles ipsi Christo tanquam membra capiti adununtur: ita vinculum, quo ipsi fideles inter se copulantur est ipsa charitas, & mutua dilectio, ac concordia, Col. 2. v. 2. Vt consolationem accipiant eorum corda, ipsis charitate compacti, & omni opulentia certò persuasi intelligentia, ad cognitionem mysterij Dei, & Patris & Christi. Per fidem deinde, non autem per bona opera viuimus. Galat. 2. v. 20. Viuo autem non amplius ego, sed viuit in me Christus, & vitam quam nunc viuo in carne, viuo per fidem Filij Dei, qui dilexit me, & tradidit semetipsum pro me. Fide, non autem bonis operibus purificantur corda nostra. Act.15.v.9. Nihil discreuit inter nos, & il-los fide purgatis,cordibus eorum. Per fidem denique, non autem per bona opera, iustificamur: Rom.4.v.3.4.5 Quid scriptura dicit? Credidit Abraham Deo, & imputatum est ei pro iustitia: Atqui ei qui operatur,merces non imputatur ex gratia, sed ex debito: ei vero,qui non operatur, sed credit in eum, qui iustificat impium, imputatur fides sua pro iustitia: & 11.v.6. Quod fi per gratiam, iam non ex operibus, alioquin gratia iam non est gratia: sin ex operibus iam non est gratia: alioquin opus iam non est opus. Gal.2.v.16. Scientes non iustificari hominem ex operibus Legis, sed per fidem Iesu Christi: etiam nos in Christum Iesum credidimus, vt iustificaremur ex fide Christi, & non ex operibus Legis, propterea quod non iustificabitur ex operibus Legis vlla caro. Neque euertit hac doctrinam, quod alibi etiam ex operibus non vero ex fide tantum iustificari dicimur, & Abrahamus ex operibus iustificatus fuisse perhibetur, quum obtulisset Ifaac filium suum super altare. Iac.2.v.21.24. Quia iustificationem, salutem, ac vitam aeternam bonis operibus ab Apostolo Iacobo ita tribui, fideique foli derogari, vt, in voce operum metonymia statuenda & agnoscenda fit effecti, qua videlicet nomen effecti,pro causa, opera fidei effecta,pro fide, causa sua efficiente ponantur: vox vero fidei non proprie, ac σωσῳνύμως sed ὁμωνύμως,ac καθολικῶς fumatur, quo videlicet titulo Aduersariis, contra quos disputat, largitur Iacobus, fidem verbis toties, licet falso iactatam,appellandam esse,sed mortuam,& ad iustificandum inefficacem, luculenter apparet ex ipsa quaestione ac sententia, quam vbi demonstrandam proponit,fidem videlicet fine operibus esse mortuam, inutilem,adque iustificandum & feruandum plane inefficacem,quam thefin ac sententiam v.14.proponit,ac postmodum tum similitudine declarat, tum argumentis grauissimis demonstrat. Tertio, quia fides iustificans, opponitur dubitationi, ac incredulitati, quum ipsa bona opera, nec dubitationi, nec incredulitati,sed impietati & malis operibus,opponantur.Matt.14.v.31. Iesus vero extenta manu apprehendit eum, dicitque ei, O exigua fide praedite quid dubitasti? Marc.9.v.24. Pater puer: statim clamans, cum lachrymis dixit, Credo Domine succurre incredulitati mea, Rom.2.v.6. 7.8. Qui reddet vnicuique fecundum opera ipsius: iis quidem qui perstant,boni operis gloriam, & honorem,& immortalitatem, id est,iis qui quaerunt vitam aeternam. Iis vero qui sunt contentiosi, & qui veritati quidem non obtemperant,sed obtemperant iniustitiae, reddetur excandescentia & ira. Quarto, quæ officio & obiecto differunt, ea reipsa unum ac idem esse nequeunt: Atqui fides iustificans, & charitas, differunt officio & obiecto, quia fides iustificans immediatè respicit in Euangelio Christum, & citra omne virtutum aliarum adminiculum, veritati sermonis Euangelici, cum certò persuasa intelligentia, assentitur: Ioh. 6. v. 68. Domine ad quem ibimus? verba vitæ æternæ habes. Et nos credidimus & cognouimus, te esse Christum illum Filium Dei viuentis. & 17. v. 3. Hæc est vita æterna, vt te solum agnoscant verum Deum, & quem misisti Iesum Christum. 2. Thess. 2. v. 11. 12. Deus illis mittet efficaciam deceptionis, vt credant mendacio, vt damnentur omnes qui non crediderunt veritati. Tit. 1. vers. 1. Paulus seruus Dei, Apostolus autem Iesu Christi, secundum fidem electorum Dei, & agnitionem veritatis, quæ est secundum pietatem: quanquam & illa bonorum operum assiduos fructus edat, sed mediatè & per charitatem agens: unde etiam per charitatem agere dicitur: Gal. 5. v. 6. Ipsa verò charitas, circa bonū proximi & virtutes secundæ tabulæ praeceptis imperatas, versatur & occupatur: Rom. 13. v. 8. 9. 10. Qui diligit alterum, Legem impleuit: Siquidem illud, Non mœchaberis, Non occides, Non furaberis, Non falsum testimonium dices, Non concupisces, & si quod aliud mandatum, in hoc sermone summatim comprehenditur, nempe, Diliges proximum tuum sicut teipsum, charitas proximum non afficit malo: Itaque impletio legis est charitas. Ex quibus necessariò sequitur, fidem iustificantem & charitatem bonáque opera, reipsa & essentia, vnum ac idem non esse. Quinto, quia virtutum diuersarum vna alterius formam ac essentiam constituere non potest: Atqui fides iustificans, & charitas tanquam diuersę virtutum species in scripturis sacris passim introducuntur, & commendantur, vt 1. Cor. 13. v. 13. Nunc verò manet fides, spes, charitas, tria hæc: maxima autem harum charitas. Ephes. 6. v. 23. Pax fratribus, & charitas cum fide à Deo Patre, & Domino Iesu Christo. Col. 1. v. 3. 4. Gratias agimus Deo, & Patri Domini nostri Iesu Christi, semper pro vobis precantes, audita fide vestra in Christo Iesu, & charitate in omnes sanctos. 1 Thess. 1. v. 3. Indesinenter memoria repetentes efficacem vestram fidem & laboriosam charitatem, & toleräntem illam spem in Domino nostro Iesu, coram Deo & Patre nostro. 1. Tim. 4. v. 12. Nemo tuam iuuentutem despiciat, sed esto exemplar fidelium in sermone, in conuersatione, in charitate, in spiritu, in fide, in puritate. & 6. v. 11. Tu verò homo Dei, ista fuge, sectare autem iustitiam, pietatem, fidem, charitatem, tolerantiam, lenitatem. 2. Pet. 1. v. 5. 6. 7. Ad hoc ipsum vero omni praterea collato studio, adiicite fidei vestrae virtutem, virtuti vero scientiam, scientiae vero temperantiam, temperantiae vero tolerantiam, tolerantiae vero pietatem, pietati vero animum in fratres propensum, animo vero in fratres propensō charitatem. 1. Ioh. 3. v. 23. Haec est eius doctrina ut credamus nomini Filii eius Iesu Christi, & diligamus alij alios, sicut mandauit nobis: & alibi passim. Ex quibus omnibus luce meridiana clarius apparet, charitate & bona opera fidei iustificantis formam constituere non posse. Sexto & vltimo: Si fides & bona opera re-ipsa ac essentia vnum & idem essent constituenda: tum duae illae partes Theologiae fides nempe, & actiones fidei, vel sapientia, ac iustitia verúsque de Deo sensus, & rectus ipsius cultus, inter se confunderentur, quae tamen duae diuersae partes in Scripturis sacris apertissimè distinguuntur: Act. 24. v. 14. 15. 16. Hoc tibi fateor, me secundum viam illam quam haeresin dicunt, ita seruire patrio Deo, ut qui credam omnia, quae in lege, ac Prophetis scripta sunt, & spem habeam in Deo fore, quam etiam ipsi expectant, resurrectionem mortuorum, tum iustorum, tum iniustorum. Interea vero ipse me exerceo ad conscientiam habendam sine offendiculo, apud Deum & apud homines. Marc. 1. v. 15. Expletum est tempus, & appropinquauit regnum Dei, conuertimini & credite Euangelio. Sic Paulus Tit. 3. v. 8. praecipit ut bonis operibus operam dent, qui Deo crediderunt: id est, ut omnes suas curas & cogitationes, eò conferant quò bonis operibus, quibus seu peculiaribus ornamentis conspicuos & laudatos esse oporteat ipsorum mores, exercendis, praealiis excellentes sint, sicuti eos deceat, qui Deo credidisse, séque ei conseruasse videri volunt. Et 1. Ioh. 3. v. 23. Hoc est eius praeceptum, ut credamus nomini Filij eius, & diligamus alij alios, sicut praecepit. Ex quibus testimoniis lucu-lenter apparet, vniuersam religionem nostram, ac totius Christianae pietatis summam, duobus illis capitibus, fide nimirum, quam Dei verbo in Scripturis sacris patefacta adhibemus, & bonorum operum, seu bonae conscientiae apud Deum: hoc est eius obedientiae, quam Deus à nobis in suo verbo flagitat, quámque Deo, subspe promissae salutis praestamus studio comprehendi. Harum verò duarum partium hunc esse ordinem, vt fides actiones fidei, seu rectus de Deo sensus, verum eiusdem cultum praecedat, & natura, & Scriptura confirmat. Illa enim docet, actionem mentis, qualis est Dei cognitio, priorem esse actione voluntatis, cuiusmodi est cultus Dei, & pietatis bonorúmque operum studium. Hæc verò aperte testatur, inuocationem Dei nullam esse posse, absque fide, neque hanc absque prædicatione: Rom.10.v.14. Quomodo inuocalunt eum in quem non crediderunt? quomodo autem credent de quo nó audiuerunt? quomodo verò audient absque prædicante? & Ephef.4. v. 18.dicuntur incredulæ gentes abalienatæ esse à vita Dei, propter ignorantiam quæ in ipsis est: quasi hæc ignorantia videlicet non simplex & innoxia, sed culpata & affectata, atque cum improbitate animi coniuncta, dicatur in causa esse, cur istæ Gentes impiè viuant, nec Deum sub spe vitæ æternæ consequendæ,rite colant. Et Heb.11.v. 6. Accedentem ad Deum, oportet hæc duo arcte tenere, Deum esse & cultores suos remunerari. quia videlicet fieri non potest, vt recté serióque Deum colat qui illius naturam, opera, & voluntatem ignorat, quum ignoti nulla sit cupido. Ex quibus omnibus euidentissimè apparet fidem iustificantem à bonis operibus,tanquam causam ab effectu, & arborem à fructibus, non separandam quidem, sed distinguendam esse, illamque ab Aduersario cum hisce, aduersus fidei ipsius naturam, & Scripturæ sacræ autoritatem imprudentissimè confundi. Hisce igitur sic præmissis, argumenta ipsius Aduersarii, quibus absurdam suam sententiam stabilire conatur,ordine nobis sunt examinanda.
units.tr: Yet that justifying faith and obedience to the divine commandments are not one and the same thing, but that faith must be distinguished from them as a tree is from its fruit and a cause from its effect, is demonstrated by many and most certain arguments. Things that differ not merely synonymously [ὁμωνύμως] and in name, but in their complete definition, cannot be one and the same in reality. Now justifying faith and good works differ in definition, because faith, as the Apostle testifies, is "the substance [ὑπόστασις] of things hoped for and the evidence [ἔλεγχος] of things not seen," that is, a substance which makes subsistent what is hoped for and demonstrates what is not seen.
