units.la: Tertio explicat ac definit, quidnam iustificatio nostra coram Deo sit, eamque nihil aliud esse dicit, quam quod Deus nos iustos censeat ac pronunciet, ac proinde ut iustos tractet. Hoc enim sensu verbum iustificare in sacris Scripturis intelligendum esse, unde tam is qui reuera iustus, quam is qui in se consideratur iniustus est, iustificari dicitur. Deu. 25.v.1. Si fuerit controuersia inter aliquos, ideoque accesserint ad iudicium, ut iudices sententiam de eis ferant, tum iustificaturi sunt eum qui iustus est, & improbaturi eum qui improbus est. 1. Reg 8.v.32. Tunc tu exaudito e coelis, & conficiens iudicato seruos tuos, improbando improbum, reddendo viam eius in caput eius: & iustificando iustum, reddendo ei secundum iustitiam eius. Proverb. capite decimo septimo, vers.15. Qui iustificat improbum, & qui condemnat iustum, abominationi sunt Iehouae aeque ambo. Et.5.v.23. Vae iustificantibus improbum, propter munus, & iustitiam iustorum abiudicantibus ab unoquoque eorum. Atque hac ipsa de re,ait,nullam esse inter ipsos nempe Socinianos,& eos, contra quos ille disputat,controuersiam. Quod quidem verum est,fi generalem vocis huius vsum,& significationem spectes,at cum agitur de iustificatione hominis Euangelica coram Deo, & tribunali,ac iudicio diuino, ad quod vocabulum illud à iudicio,ac tribunali politico & forensi translatum,& deductum est, tū eandem quidem significationem obtinet, sed subiectum ipsius significationis tunc est limitandum,quia illi tantum coram tribunali gratiæ Dei iustificantur,qui in fe considerati peccatores sunt,& iniusti : Rom.4. v.5. Ei vero qui non operatur, sed credit in eum qui iustificat impium, imputatur fides sua pro iustitia. Gal.3.v.22.Conclusit Scriptura omnia sub peccatum, vt promissio ex fide Iesu Christi daretur credentibus, sed per imputationem iustitiæ & obedientiæ Christi, iusti à Deo constituuntur,& pro iustis habentur. Rom.5.v.19. Sicut per inobedientiam vnius hominis peccatores constituti sunt multi, ita per vnius obedientiam iusti constituentur multi. Quum igitur iustificationis gratuitæ subiectum sint foli peccatores , sed ad Christum, per fidem confugientes,& iustificatio fit iustitiæ,& obedientiæ alienæ nempe Christi applicatio , hinc luce meridiana clarius apparet, vehementissimè errare illos , qui in perfecta iustificationis definitione subiectum priuatiuum omitti posse , falso arbitrantur.
units.tr: Thirdly, he explains and defines what our justification before God is, and says that it is nothing other than God judging and pronouncing us righteous, and therefore treating us as righteous. For in this sense the word to justify is to be understood in the Sacred Scriptures, whence both him who is truly righteous and him who is considered unrighteous in himself are said to be justified. Deut. 25. v. 1: If there be a controversy between men, and they come to judgment, that the judges may judge them, then they shall justify the righteous and condemn the wicked. 1 Kings 8. v. 32: Then hear thou from heaven, and do, and judge thy servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way upon his head; and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness. Proverbs ch. 17, v. 15: He that justifies the wicked, and he that condemns the just, even they both are an abomination to Jehovah. And Isaiah 5. v. 23: Woe to those who justify the wicked for a bribe, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from each of them. He says that on this very matter, namely, between the Socinians and those against whom he disputes, there is no controversy. This is indeed true if you look at the general use and meaning of the word. But when the question concerns the evangelical justification of man before God, and before the tribunal and judgment of God, to which that word, transferred and derived from the political and forensic judgment and tribunal, applies, then it keeps the same meaning, but the subject of that meaning must be limited, because only those are justified before the tribunal of the grace of God who are, considered in themselves, sinners and unrighteous. Rom. 4. v. 5: But to him who does not work, but believes in him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Gal. 3. v. 22: Scripture has concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe; but through the imputation of the righteousness and obedience of Christ, they are constituted righteous before God and are held as righteous. Rom. 5. v. 19: As by the disobedience of one man many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one many shall be made righteous. Since, therefore, the subjects of gratuitous justification are sinners alone, who flee to Christ by faith, and justification consists in the application of the alien obedience and righteousness of Christ, it is clearer than the noonday sun that those are most gravely mistaken who falsely think that the privative subject can be omitted from a complete definition of justification.

units.la: Quarto,ostendit,quomodo quāve ratione hoc fieri possit, vt Deus nos iustos censeat ac pronunciet, & quasi iustos tractet, id est, à morte liberet,ac vitæ æternæ præmio,iuxta promissionem per Christum factam, ornet. Quicunque igitur,inquit,coram Deo iustificati vult, eum à peccato immunem esse oportet.Vbicunque enim peccati reatus est, ibi mortem regnare,quandoquidem , testante Apostolo , stipendium peccati mors est: Roman.cap.6.versu vigefimo tertio. Hoc ipsum autem duobus modis fieri posse,addit, vel vt quis nunquam peccauerit, vel fi maximè peccauerit,vt peccata ipsius,ab ipso,coramDeo sint ablata. Quoniam vero nullus reperiatur , qui nunquam peccauerit ( 1. Iohan. capite primo, versu 8. Si dixerimus nos peccatum non habere,nos ipsos fallimus, & veritas in nobis non est. 1.Reg. 8. v. 46. nemo est qui nō peccet)ideo priori modo neminem coram Deo iustificari posse ,ac proinde necessarium esse , fi iustificari velimus , vt peccata nostra deleantur , & à nobis auferantur. Quoniam vero peccata nostra duobus modis deleri,& à nobis auferri posse videantur, vel per satisfactionem, vel per vel per remissionem & condonationem, ideo quum explicandum sit, quo modo per Christum iustificemur, diligenter dispiciendum esse, utro modo peccata nostra coram Deo a nobis auferantur, quandoquidem Deus vitam ac salutem aeternam nobis per solum Christum, non vero per quenquam alium promiserit: & Christus non eo fine in hunc mundum venerit, ut nos in pristinum statum, in quo Adamus ante lapsum fuit constitutus, sed ut in meliorem ac praestantiorem nos restitueret, necillius restitutionis in Scriptura sacra, quum inter Christum & Adamum instituitur comparatio, vsquam facta sit mentio, sed ubique Adamus mortis tam naturalis quam aeterna, Christus vero vita aeterna autor consideretur.
units.tr: Fourthly, he shows how and by what means it can come about that God judges and pronounces us righteous, and treats us as righteous, that is, frees us from death and adorns us with the reward of eternal life, according to the promise made through Christ. Whoever therefore wishes to be justified before God, he says, must be free from sin. For wherever there is the guilt of sin, there death reigns, since, as the Apostle testifies, the wages of sin is death (Rom. ch. 6, verse 23). This itself, however, can happen in two ways, he adds: either that someone has never sinned, or, even if he has sinned most grievously, that his sins are taken away from him before God. But since no one is found who has never sinned (1 John ch. 1, verse 8: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us; 1 Kings 8. v. 46: there is no man who does not sin), therefore in the first way no one can be justified before God, and it is necessary, if we wish to be justified, that our sins be blotted out and taken away from us. Since our sins seem able to be blotted out and taken away from us in two ways, either by satisfaction or by remission and forgiveness, therefore, since it must be explained how we are justified through Christ, it must be carefully examined in which way our sins are taken away from us before God, since God has promised eternal life and salvation to us through Christ alone and not through anyone else; and Christ did not come into this world for this purpose, that he might restore us to the former state in which Adam was placed before the fall, but that he might restore us to a better and more excellent one. Nor is there any mention anywhere in Holy Scripture of such a restoration, although a comparison is drawn between Christ and Adam; rather, Adam is everywhere regarded as the author of both natural and eternal death, and Christ as the author of eternal life.

units.la: Quibus verbis proponere videtur Aduersarius discrimen iustitiae legalis, & Euangelicae: quorum illa est, cum in cuius vita reperitur ea puritas, quae testimonium iustitiae apud Dei thronum mereatur, seu quum quis iustitia legali, circa omnem transgressionem functus, ac proinde coram tribunali seuerae iustitiae diuinae constitutus, operum suorum integritate, rigido Dei iudicio ita respondere ac satisfacere potest, vt nullius delicti per legem accusari atque conuinci possit, & consequenter iustus a Deo, vitaeque aeternae praemio dignus, in se, & ex debito, citraque remissionis gratiam, censeri ac pronuntiari debeat: haec vero quum quis operum iustitia exclusus, & peccati contra legem admissi conscius, ac proinde morti ac damnationi obnoxius, atque ad gratiam confugiens, a peccatorum, quae mortis ac damnationis causa sunt, liberatur.
units.tr: In these words the Adversary seems to set out the difference between legal righteousness and evangelical righteousness. The former is the case where someone is found in such purity of life that he deserves a witness of righteousness before the throne of God; that is, when a man, by legal righteousness, has performed every obligation, and so, standing before the tribunal of God's strict justice, can by the integrity of his works answer and satisfy the rigorous judgment of God, so that he cannot be accused or convicted of any transgression of the law, and consequently ought to be judged and pronounced righteous by God, worthy of the reward of eternal life, on his own account and as a matter of debt, without any grace of remission. The latter is the case where someone, shut out from the righteousness of works, aware of having sinned against the law, and therefore liable to death and condemnation, flees to grace, and is freed from those sins which are the cause of death and condemnation.

units.la: Atque si hoc sensu Aduersarius verba sua velit intelligi, minime refragamur: sin vero ipse illam liberationem a mortis causis, videlicet peccatis nostris, praecedaneum quid ipsius iustificationis constituat: tum falsam esse ipsius sententiam, ex iis liquido constat, quibus nos iustificationem ipsam in peccatorum remissione positam esse demonstrauimus. Quod vero Ostorrodius duos illos modos, quibus peccata nostra auferantur, nempe satisfactionem & gratuitam remissionem atque condonationem tanquam oppositos inter se adducit, eo grauissime hallucinatus ipsum, ex sequentibus patebit. Quae denique de vtriusque status, futuri nimirum in quem electi & saluandi sunt transferendi, & illius praeteriti, in quo Adamus per creationem fuit constitutus, discrimine subiungit, illis libenti animo subscribimus: sed quod ille Adamu etia ante peccatum, & in statu integritatis & conditionis natiuę consideratum, mortis temporalis (quam contra veritatem, naturalem appellat) autorem & causam constituit, eúmque hoc etiam respe-ctu indutum atque conuestitutum, ipsi Christo vitæ æternæ auto-ri opponit, eo ipso grauissimum errorem ab ipso committi, suprà capite vigesimoseptimo à nobis luculenter est demōstratum. Re-stat igitur, vt nos ad quæstionis illius coutrouersæ, An nimirum in iustificationis negotio, peccata nostra per meritum & satisfactionē Chri-sti: an vero per gratuitam remissionem, videlicet satisfactioni & me-rito Christi oppositam, tollantur atque auferantur? tractationem & explicationem accingamus. Atque quum illa grauissimi sit mo-menti, vtpote in qua totius iustificationis ac salutis nostræ cardo vertitur, ac proinde vberius & prolixius explicanda: ideo lubet illi peculiare caput assignare.
units.tr: If the Adversary wishes his words to be understood in this sense, we by no means contradict him. But if he makes that deliverance from the causes of death, namely our sins, something preliminary to justification itself, then his opinion is plainly false, as is clear from the arguments by which we have shown that justification itself consists in the remission of sins. That Ostorodius brings forward those two modes by which our sins are taken away, namely satisfaction and free remission and pardon, as opposed to each other, is a very grave error on his part, as will appear from what follows. As for the distinction he adds between the two states, the future one, namely that into which the elect and saved are to be transferred, and that past one in which Adam was established at creation, we gladly subscribe to those points. But that he, against the truth, considers Adam even before the sin, in the state of integrity and natural condition, as the author and cause of temporal death (which he calls natural, contrary to the truth), and that he even in this respect sets him, clothed and arrayed in this way, against Christ the author of eternal life, is by that very fact a most serious error committed by him, as we have clearly demonstrated above in the twenty-seventh chapter. It remains, therefore, that we turn to the treatment and explanation of that controverted question: whether, in the business of justification, our sins are taken away and removed through the merit and satisfaction of Christ, or rather through free remission, opposed to the satisfaction and merit of Christ. Since this question is of the greatest weight, as the hinge on which the whole of our justification and salvation turns, and therefore must be explained more fully and at greater length, we think it right to assign it a separate chapter.

units.la: CAPVT XXXIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXXIV.

units.la: In quo explicatur quæstio illa controuersa, An videlicet Christus morte & passione sua Deo Patri pro peccatis nostris satisfecerit, & an peccata nostra per meritum & satisfactionem Christi, an vero per gratuitam remissio-nem & condonationem illi satisfactioni oppositam, de-leantur atque auferantur? Ac proinde, An Christus id-circo in hunc mundum venerit, vt Deo Patri, mor-te & passione sua, pro peccatis nostris satisfaceret, & qua-re, & qua ratione Iesus Christus dicatur & sit seruator noster, & quo pacto nobis æternam salutem pepererit?
units.tr: In which the disputed question is explained: whether Christ, by his death and passion, satisfied God the Father for our sins, and whether our sins are removed and taken away through the merit and satisfaction of Christ, or rather through a free remission and pardon opposed to that satisfaction? And accordingly: did Christ come into this world so that by his death and passion he might satisfy God the Father for our sins, and why and in what manner is Jesus Christ called and is our Saviour, and how did he obtain eternal salvation for us?

units.la: ET quoniâ Aduersarius hæsce quæstiones sciungit, cùm tamen vna ab altera dependeat, & in ipsa tractatione & explicatione eiusdem cum ipsa confundit: ideo vt tota rei veritas eò clariùs elucecscat, nos primò omnium ipsam quæstionem controuersam proponemus, deinde sententiam ac doctrinam Ecclesiarum nostrarum, de hoc capite, proponemus ac demonstrabimus: & quidnam Aduersarii hac de re sentiant ac doceant, exponemus: denique sententiam cr-roneam & argumenta Aduersarii refutabimus. Et primum quidem, nempe statum controuersiæ quantum concernit, quæritur inter nos & Aduersarios: An Christus morte & passione sua Deo pro peccatis nostris satisfecerit, & an peccata nostra per & propter meritum, obedientiam & satisfactionem Christi, an vero per gratuitam remissionem, & liberalem condonationem, merito & satisfactioni oppositam, nullaque satisfactione interveniente acquisitam, deleantur & auferantur? Ac proinde, An Christus idcirco in hunc mundum venerit, vt Deo Patri morte & passione sua pro peccatis nostris satisfaceret, & cur denique, quàve ratione Iesus Christus dicatur & sit Seruator noster, & quo pacto nobis æternam salutem pepererit? An videlicet tantùm doctrina quatenus videlicet æternæ salutis viam ipse nobis annuntiauit: deinde exemplo, quatenus nimirum annuntiatam salutis viam nobis in sua ipsius persona ostendit, & multis modis confirmauit: denique communicatione, quatenus nempe plenissima potestate in cœlo ac terra accepta, se vitam æternam nobis daturum probauit? & credentibus in ipsum reipsa largitur? An vero merito & efficacia simul, id est, non tantum doctrina, exemplo, & communicatione, sed etiam, & quidem maximè merito & satisfactione, quatenus videlicet ipse, qui idem est & sanctus Pontifex, & sancta victima, passione & morte sua pro nostris peccatis iusto Dei iudicio satisfecerit, & pœnas nobis ob peccata nostra debitas in se vt sponsorem nostrum deriuauerit, denique amissam Dei gratiam, & vitæ æternæ præmium nobis sit promeritus? Ostorrodius Institutionum suarum capite trigesimoseptimo, & in disputatione sua aduersus Georgium Tradelium Syndicum Augustanum, meritum & satisfactionem Christi totis viribus impugnat, ac negat Christum Deo Patri in orte & passione sua pro peccatis satisfecisse, ac proinde peccata nostra per & propter meritum, obedientiam, & satisfactionem Christi, sed per gratuitam remissionem, & liberalem condonationem, nulla interveniente satisfactione, imo satisfactioni e diametro oppositam, deleri atque auferri, tam confidenter affirmat, vt vanum appellare sermonem nefaria voce audeat, si quis gratuitam peccatorum remissionem cum illa Christi satisfactione coniungere & copulare velit. Doctrinæ vero ac sententiæ i-
units.tr: And since the Adversary separates these questions, although one depends on the other, and in the very treatment and explanation of them confuses the one with the other, therefore, so that the whole truth of the matter may shine out more clearly, we will first set out the controverted question itself, then propose and demonstrate the doctrine of our Churches on this head, then expound what the Adversary thinks and teaches about it, and finally refute his erroneous view and arguments. First, then, as far as the state of the controversy concerns, the question between us and the Adversaries is this: Whether Christ by his death and passion satisfied God for our sins, and whether our sins are blotted out and taken away through and on account of the merit, obedience and satisfaction of Christ, or rather through free remission and liberal pardon, opposed to merit and satisfaction, and obtained with no satisfaction intervening? And accordingly: Whether Christ therefore came into this world, that by his death and passion he might satisfy God the Father for our sins, and why, and in what way, Jesus Christ is called and is our Saviour, and how he has won eternal salvation for us? Whether, that is, only by doctrine, namely in so far as he himself announced to us the way of eternal salvation; then by example, namely in so far as he showed us in his own person the way of salvation he had announced, and confirmed it in many ways; finally by communication, namely in so far as, having received full power in heaven and on earth, he proved that he would give eternal life to us and actually bestows it on those who believe in him? Or rather by merit and efficacy together, that is, not only by doctrine, example and communication, but also, and indeed chiefly, by merit and satisfaction, in so far as he himself, who is also the holy High Priest and the holy victim, by his passion and death satisfied God's just judgment for our sins, took upon himself as our surety the punishments due to us for our sins, and finally merited for us the lost grace of God and the reward of eternal life? In chapter thirty-seven of his Institutes, and in his disputation against Georg Tradelius, Syndic of Augsburg, Ostorrodius attacks with all his strength the merit and satisfaction of Christ. He denies that Christ satisfied God the Father by his death and passion for our sins, and consequently he affirms so confidently that our sins are blotted out and taken away not through and on account of the merit, obedience and satisfaction of Christ, but through free remission and liberal pardon, with no satisfaction intervening, indeed diametrically opposed to satisfaction, that he dares to call it an empty word, with that impious phrase, if anyone wishes to join and couple free forgiveness of sins with that satisfaction of Christ. The doctrine and opinion of his concerning the end and cause for which Christ came into this world seems to be this:

units.la: Iiii 3. psius de fine & causa ob quam Christus in hunc mundum venerit, summa hæc videtur esse : [Christum videlicet non iccirco potis- simum in hunc mundum venisse, neque idcirco potissimùm tam multas eásque acerbissimas calamitates,ac inprimis mortem igno- miniosissimam pertulisse, vt sua obedientia, vel passione & morte sua,id totum Deo persolueret quod nos illi debebamus : nec pœ- nas nobis ob peccata nostra debitas in se vt sponsorem nostrum deriuaret, nec denique amissam Dei gratiam, & vitæ æternæ præ- mium nobis promereretur : verùm ideo potissimum, vt inessabi- lem illam Dei Patris gratiam, qua is remissionem peccatorum, & salutem æternam, omnibus mundanas cupiditates negantibus, & iustè piéque in hoc seculo viuentibus, dare decreuerit, humano generi patefaceret, eiúsque effectum ad omnes homines, quan- tum in ipso esset,deriuaret,videlicet in illis efficiendo spem beatæ immortalitatis,eósque hac spe incitatos,ad fidem & pœnitentiam adducendo, denique peccata iis iam resipiscentibus condonando, imò vitam æternam in die nouissimo largiendo. Atque ad hunc finem perfectè assequendum tum humiliationem, tum exaltatio- nem Christi adhibitam à Deo fuisse.] Ne verò sententiam Aduer- sarii fortasse non assequutus aliquid ipsi affingam contra Christia- nas & æquas disputationis leges, à mente ipsius alienum: ideò ip- sam doctrinâ, prout ab Ostorrodio capite trigesimoseptimo pro- ponitur, ad certas breuésque theses redigemus ac recensebimus, quæ in hunc modum sese habent. I. Christus non iccirco in hunc mun- dum venit, aut passus est, vt aliquid apud Deum perageret, ipsúmque ad gratiam, qua nobis peccata remitteret & condonaret, permoueret: sed ideo, vt veram obedientiam, quam præceptis per Christum traditis præstare tenemur,in nobis efficeret. II. Quum enim Deus apud se de- creuerit nobis resipiscentibus, & præceptis Christi obedientibus, remis- sis peccatis nostris vitam æternam donare, nec aliud quicquam ad de- cretum illud exequendum restiterit, nisi vt resipisceremus, ac præ- stam obedientiam præstaremus,quod tamen humanæ natura admodum est difficile, secundùm illud Christi, Matth. capite septimo, versu 14. Angusta est porta,& stricta via, quæ ducit ad vitam, & pauci sunt qui inueniant eam : idcirco Deum pro inessabili sua misericordia & sapientia, humanæ imbecillitati succurrere, certisque mediis ad fidem excellentissimis suis promissionibus, sibi obedientibus factis, haben- dum adducere voluit: quæ fides seu confidentia statim omnem in homine homine obedientiam efficere potest: iuxta illa scriptura testimonia. Mar.9.v.23.omnia fieri possunt credenti. 1.Ioh.5.v.3.4.5. Haec est charitas Dei, ut mandata eius seruemus, & mandata eius grauia non sunt: quoniam quicquid natum est ex Deo, vincit mundum, & haec est victoria quae vicit mundum, fides nostra: quis est, qui vincit mundum, nisi qui credit Iesum esse Filium Dei?III. Primum autem medium est, Christi innocentia, id est vita perfecta sanctitas & iustitia, sic ut nemo iustam habuerit causam ipsum mali alicuius insimulandi, atque de Euangelio ipsius, id est, promissionibus, nomine Dei nobis facta, dubitandi, Iohan. 8. uersu 46. Quis ex vobis arguit me de peccato? si veritatem dico, quare vos non creditis mihi? IIII.
units.tr: Iiii 3. The sum of it appears to be this: [that Christ did not come into this world, nor endure so many and so bitter calamities, and above all the most shameful death, chiefly so that by his obedience, or by his passion and death, he might pay to God everything that we owed him, nor so that he might take upon himself as our surety the punishments due to us for our sins, nor finally so that he might merit for us the lost grace of God and the reward of eternal life; but chiefly so that he might reveal to mankind that ineffable grace of God the Father, by which he has resolved to give forgiveness of sins and eternal salvation to all who renounce worldly desires and live righteously and piously in this age, and so that he might extend its effect to all men as far as in him lay, namely by producing in them the hope of blessed immortality, and by urging them on, stirred by this hope, to faith and repentance, and finally by pardoning sins to those now repenting, and even by bestowing eternal life on the last day. And to attain this end perfectly, both the humiliation and the exaltation of Christ were employed by God.] Lest perhaps, not having grasped the Adversary's opinion, I attribute to him something foreign to his mind, contrary to the Christian and fair laws of disputation, I will reduce and set out the doctrine, as Ostorrodius proposes it in chapter thirty-seven, to certain brief theses, which stand thus. I. Christ did not come into this world, or suffer, in order to accomplish anything with God, or to move him to the grace by which he would remit and pardon our sins; but in order to produce in us the true obedience which we are bound to render to the precepts delivered through Christ. II. For since God has decided in himself to give eternal life to us, our sins forgiven, when we repent and obey the precepts of Christ, and nothing else remained to carry out that decision except that we should repent and render the obedience, which nevertheless is very difficult for human nature, according to that saying of Christ, Matthew chapter seven, verse 14: "Narrow is the gate and strait is the way that leads to life, and few there are who find it"; therefore God, in his ineffable mercy and wisdom, wished to help human weakness and to bring us to have faith by certain most excellent means, namely his promises, to those who are obedient to him; this faith or confidence can at once produce in a man all obedience, according to those testimonies of Scripture: Mark 9:23, "All things are possible to him who believes." 1 John 5:3-5, "This is the love of God, that we keep his commandments, and his commandments are not grievous; for whatever is born of God overcomes the world, and this is the victory that has overcome the world, our faith. Who is he that overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?"* III. The first means is the innocence of Christ, that is, his perfect life, holiness and righteousness, so that no one had a just cause to accuse him of any wrong, and so that no one should doubt his Gospel, that is, the promises made to us in the name of God, John 8:46, "Which of you convicts me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me?" IV.

units.la: Secundum medium sunt miracula a Christo patrata, quae non exiguam vim & virtutem habent, nos ad fidem permouendi, quapropter Christus etiam Apostolis potentiam miranda eiusmodi opera patrandi concessit, quibus salutiferam Christi doctrinam confirmarent. Heb.2. Quomodo nos effugiemus, si tantam neglexerimus salutem? quae cum primum enarrari coeperit per ipsum Dominum, ab iis qui ipsum audierant fuit nobis confirmata. V. Quamuis vero praedicta duo media ad confirmandam Christi doctrinam maximum pondus & momentum habeant, hoc tamen Deo satis visum non fuit, sed insuper in ipsius Christi persona nobis demonstrare voluit, viam illam salutis ab ipso monstratam, veram salutis viam esse, etiam si propter acerbissimarum afflictionum, & calamitatum salebras res aliter se habere videatur. Ac proinde [voluit ut Christus ignominiosissimae mortis supplicium subiret, quam ingentia, & innumerabilia mala & incommoda sunt antegressa. Et quum ille penitus derelictus, & peffumdatus videretur, ecce Deus praesto fuit qui ipsum ex mortuis ad immortalitatem excitatum, & aliquot ex discipulis ipsius viuum monstratum, & potenti illa resurrectione multis aliis argumentis confirmata, spectantibus Apostolis, in caelos sustulit, ac euexit, ipsumque Regem ac Dominum constituit, data videlicet illi omni potestate in caelo, & in terra, & subiectis dominio ipsius non tantum Spiritibus fortissimis, ac potentissimis, quorum potentia diuina est, & ob quam Dii sunt, ac dicuntur, nec vlli vnquam nisi Deo inseruierunt, sic ut ipsi ia videl. Christo inseruire, ac obedire, ipsumque adorare & colere teneatur: verum etiam Spiritib. malis vna cum morte & inferno, quae ille, suo tempore, in stagnum ignis ac sulphuris coiectum est. Ro.6.9. Vt qui sciamus Christum excitatum ex mortuis non amplius mori, & morte ei non amplius dominari. Act.10. v.40.41. Huc Deus excitauit tertio die, fecitque vt conspicuus fieret:nō toti populo,sed testibus quos ipse prius designauerat,nimirum nobis,qui comedimus, ac bibimus vnà cum eo posteaquā resurrexit ex mortuis .1.Cor.15. v 4.5.6.7. Christum sepultum fuisse,& excitatum tertio die secundum scripturas, & visum fuisse Cephæ,deinde duodecim illis : postea visus est amplius,quàm quingentis fratribus semel,ex quibus plerique manet vique adhuc,quidam autem obdormierunt : postea visus est Iacobo,deinde Apostolis omnibus. Eph.1 v.20.21. Excitauit eum ex mortuis, & collocauit ad dexteram suam in cœlis longè supra omne imperium , ac potestatem , & potentiam,& dominium , & omne nomen quod nominatur,non solum in hoc seculo, verum etiam in futuro.Mat.28. v.18.Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo, & in terra. 1.Pet.3. v.22.Qui est ad dexteram Dei profectus in cœlum,subiectis ipsi Angelis,& potestatibus, ac virtutibus. Apoc.5. v.12.13. Dignus est agnus ille mactatus,qui accipiat virtutē,& diuitias,& sapientiam,& fortitudinem,& honorem,& gloriam , & benedictionem:sed & omnem creaturā quæ in cœlo est,& super terrā,& sub terra,& in mari,& quæ in eis sunt omnia &c. Phil.2. v.10. vt ad nomen Iesu omne genu se flectat cœlestium, ac terrestrium, & subterraneorum. Apoc.1. v.18. Ego sum qui viuo , sed fui mortuus,& ecce viuo in secula seculorum: Amen:& habeo claues inferorum,& mortis.1. Cor.15. v.24 Deinde erit finis, quum tradiderit regnum Deo ac Patri,quum aboleuerit omne imperium, & omnem potentiam & virtutem &c.Apoc.20. v.10. Et Diabolus qui seducebat eos,coniectus est in stagnum ignis & sulphuris , vbi & bestia, & Pseudopropheta,& cruciabuntur die ac nocte in secula seculorū:&v.14.Infernus ac mors cōiecti sunt in stagnū ignis,quę est mors secunda.
units.tr: The second means is the miracles wrought by Christ, which have no small force and power to move us to faith; for this reason Christ also granted to the Apostles the power to work such wonderful works, by which they might confirm the saving doctrine of Christ. Heb. 2: "How shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? which, having at the first been spoken by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard him." V. Although the two means mentioned above have the greatest weight and importance for confirming the doctrine of Christ, yet God did not think this sufficient, but wished further to show us in the person of Christ himself that the way of salvation shown by him is the true way of salvation, even though, because of the stumbling-blocks of most bitter afflictions and calamities, things seem to be otherwise. And so [he willed that Christ should undergo the punishment of the most shameful death, though vast and countless evils and hardships had gone before. And when he seemed utterly forsaken and cast down, behold, God was at hand, who raised him from the dead to immortality, and showed him alive to some of his disciples, and confirmed by many other proofs that mighty resurrection, the Apostles looking on; he took him up into the heavens and exalted him, and appointed him King and Lord, having given him all power in heaven and on earth, and making subject to his dominion not only the most mighty and powerful spirits, whose power is divine and on account of which they are called gods, and who never served anyone except God, so that they too should be bound to serve, obey, worship and honour Christ, but also the evil spirits, together with death and hell, which at his appointed time he will cast into the lake of fire and brimstone. Romans 6:9, "knowing that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more, and death no longer has dominion over him." Acts 10:40-41, "God raised him up on the third day and caused him to be seen, not by all the people, but by witnesses whom he had chosen beforehand, that is, by us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead." 1 Cor. 15:4-7, "that Christ was buried, and that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures, and that he was seen by Cephas, then by the twelve; afterwards he was seen by more than five hundred brethren at once, most of whom remain until now, though some have fallen asleep; afterwards he was seen by James, then by all the Apostles." Eph. 1:20-21, "He raised him from the dead and set him at his right hand in the heavenly places, far above all rule and authority and power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in that to come." Matt. 28:18, "All power is given to me in heaven and on earth." 1 Pet. 3:22, "who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels and authorities and powers made subject to him." Rev. 5:12-13, "Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honour and glory and blessing"; and every creature in heaven, on earth, under the earth, in the sea, and all that is in them, etc. Phil. 2:10, "that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, on earth, and under the earth." Rev. 1:18, "I am he who lives, and was dead, and behold I am alive for evermore, Amen; and I have the keys of Hades and of death." 1 Cor. 15:24, "Then comes the end, when he delivers the kingdom to God the Father, when he has abolished all rule and all authority and power." Rev. 20:10, "And the devil who deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and they will be tormented day and night for ever and ever." And v. 14, "Death and Hades were cast into the lake of fire, which is the second death."

units.la: VI. Sed alia etiam de causa hæc Christi exaltatio necessaria fuit, nempe quia Deus ipsum Redemptorem ac Saluatorem populi sui constituit,quem ille,nisi tanta potestate præditum esset,nec contra Diabolum tueri, nec à morte liberare,nec denique vitam æternam participem reddere posset. VII. Quum igitur Christus,per illam ipsam viam, quam nobis sequendam proponit atque iniungit, ad tantam salutem ac gloriam peruenerit, quis non videt hanc ipsam veram salutis,felicitatis,ac gloriæ æternæ consequenda viam esse? Ac proinde ipse homo qui hoc scit, atque credit,nullam amplius causam habet,de veritate promissionum diuinarum dubitandi, ac proinde,vt ineffabilis illius gaudij , & gloriæ particeps fieri possit(quis autem illam non vehementissimè desi-derei?) deret?(quin omnes cupiditates carnis per Spiritum (Spiritus autem ille est ipses vitæ æternæ)mortificet,piéque,& sanctè viuat, ( quisquis enim hanc spem habet in eo,purificat se sicut & ille purus est.1. Ioh. 3.v.2. ) imò omnes calamitates, & mortem quantumuis acerbissimam subire minimè vereatur,non dubitans quin tandem,ex Dei decreto, remissio omnium peccatorum ipsius,& vitæ æterna præmium,hoc factum, & opus suum sit cösequuturum. Atque hæc est Aduersarii sententia,ac doctrina,quam prolixius recensere non piguit:Vnde porrò liquidò constat,Christum Iesum iuxta sententiam ipsius ideò seruatorem nostrum esse, quia salutis æternæ viam nobis annuntiauerit, & in sua ipsius persona,cum vitæ exemplo, tum miraculis, tum denique ex mortuis resurgendo,manifestè ostenderit,vitamque æternam nobis ei fidem habentibus ipse daturus sit,non verò quia vitam æternam morte & passione suâ promeruerit, & Deo Patri pro nostris peccatis satisfecerit: ac proinde ipsum vitam ac salutem æternam nobis peperisse, non satisfaciendo pro peccatis nostris,sed æternæ salutis consequendæ viam annuntiando,spem vitæ beatæ in nobis accendendo,nosque hac spe incitatos,ad fidem,& pœnitentiam adducendo.
units.tr: VI. But this exaltation of Christ was also necessary for another reason: God appointed him the Redeemer and Saviour of his people, and unless he were endowed with such power, he could neither defend them against the devil, nor free them from death, nor finally make them partakers of eternal life. VII. Since, therefore, Christ attained to such salvation and glory by that very way which he sets before us to follow and enjoins upon us, who does not see that this is the true way to obtain salvation, happiness and eternal glory? So a man who knows and believes this has no further cause to doubt the truth of the divine promises. And that he may share in that ineffable joy and glory (who would not most eagerly desire this?), he will mortify all the lusts of the flesh through the Spirit (and this Spirit is the Spirit of eternal life), and live devoutly and holily. (For everyone who has this hope in him purifies himself, just as he is pure. 1 John 3.2.) Indeed, he will not shrink from undergoing any calamity or even the most bitter death, not doubting that in the end, by God's decree, he will obtain the forgiveness of all his sins and the reward of eternal life, as the fruit of this deed and work of his. This is the opponent's view and teaching, which I have not been reluctant to set out at some length. From this it is clear beyond doubt that Jesus Christ, according to his own view, is our Saviour only because he has announced to us the way of eternal salvation, and has shown it plainly in his own person, both by the example of his life, by miracles, and finally by rising from the dead, and that he himself will give eternal life to us who believe in him; not because he merited eternal life by his death and suffering and satisfied God the Father for our sins. Thus he obtained life and eternal salvation for us not by satisfying for our sins, but by proclaiming the way to attain eternal salvation, kindling in us the hope of a blessed life, and leading us, stirred by this hope, to faith and repentance.

units.la: Nos verò contrà docemus ac profitemur, Christum Deo Patri pro peccatis nostris plenissimè satisfecisse, peccatáque nostra per, & propter meritum,obedientiam,ac satisfactionem Christi, quæ gratuitam eorundem remissionem minime euertit, deleri, atque auferri,nosque per illius obedientiæ,iustitiæ, ac satisfactionis imputationem coram tribunali diuino iustificari,atque absolui. Ac proinde Christum idcirco in hunc mundum venisse, & à Deo Patre missum esse,vt nobis non tantum salutis promissæ viam annuntiaret,eamque innocentia vitæ,miraculis,morte,passione, resurrectione, & exaltatione confirmaret, & credentibus in ipsum tandem largiretur,sed etiam,& quidem potissimum, vt Deo Patri morte,& passione sua,pro peccatis nostris satisfaceret, pœnásque nobis ob peccata debitas, in se, vt sponsorem nostrum deriuaret, denique amissam Dei Patris gratiam,& vitæ æternæ præmium notis promereretur,atque pareret. Et Iesum Christum Seruatorem nostrum esse atque dici non tantum doctrina, quatenus videlicet æternæ salutis viam ipse nobis annuntiauit, exemplóque, quatenus nimirum annuntiatam salutis viam nobis in sua ipsius persona ostendit, & multis modis confirmauit, & communicatione, quatenus nempe plenissima potestate,in cœlo,& in terra accepta, se vitam æternam nobis daturum probauit, & credentibus in ipsum reipsa largiturus est, verum etiam, & quidem maximè, quatenus videlicet ipse, qui idem est & sanctus Pontifex, & sancta victima passione & morte sua, Deo Patri, pro nostris peccatis satisfecit, & pœnas nobis ob peccata nostra debitas, in se, vt sponsorem nostrum deriuauit, denique amissam Dei gratiam, & vitæ æternæ præmium nobis promeruit. Atque hanc vltimam thefin nostram ex Scripturis sacris, fauente Domino demonstrabimus, quia hac adstructa, & confirmata, antecedentes illæ necessariò ponuntur, & concedantur, quū certissimum sit, Christum propter idipsum, quod reipsa effecit, ac præstitit, in mundū venisse, atq; à Patre missū esse.
units.tr: We, on the contrary, teach and profess that Christ fully satisfied God the Father for our sins, and that our sins are blotted out and taken away through and on account of the merit, obedience and satisfaction of Christ, which does not in the least overturn their gratuitous forgiveness; and that we are justified and absolved before the divine tribunal by the imputation of his obedience, righteousness and satisfaction. Accordingly, Christ came into this world and was sent by God the Father not only to announce the way of the promised salvation, to confirm it by the innocence of his life, by miracles, by death, suffering, resurrection and exaltation, and finally to bestow it on those who believe in him; but also, and indeed chiefly, so that by his death and suffering he might satisfy God the Father for our sins, take upon himself, as our surety, the punishments owed to us for our sins, and finally merit and obtain for us the lost grace of God the Father and the reward of eternal life. And we hold that Jesus Christ is and is called our Saviour not only by his teaching, insofar as he himself announced to us the way of eternal salvation; nor by his example, insofar as he showed the announced way of salvation in his own person and confirmed it in many ways; nor by his communication, insofar as, having received full power in heaven and on earth, he proved that he will give eternal life to us and will in fact bestow it on those who believe in him; but above all, insofar as he himself, who is both the holy High Priest and the holy victim, by his suffering and death satisfied God the Father for our sins, took upon himself as our surety the punishments owed to us for our sins, and finally merited for us the grace of God and the reward of eternal life. We shall demonstrate this final thesis of ours from the holy Scriptures, the Lord favouring us. For once it is established and confirmed, the preceding points are necessarily granted and conceded, since it is most certain that Christ came into the world and was sent by the Father precisely for that which he actually accomplished and performed.

units.la: Quum igitur, Christū Iesum à Deo Patre constitutū esse Mediatorem, Seruatorem, ac Redemptorem nostrum, inter nos & Aduersarios extra controuersiæ, ac dubitationis aleam sit constitutum, sed de illo ambigatur, quotuplex sit illud Christi Mediatoris, ac Redemptoris nostri officium, & consequenter, quænam actiones, atq; functiones tum ad muneris, ac officii Mediatorii exequutionem, tū salutis, ac vitæ æternę impetratione, & comunicatione requiratur: & nos, Christū Iesum, vt Mediatoris, ac Seruatoris officio rite fungi posset, à Deo Patre Prophetā, Sacerdotē, ac Regē constitutū esse, & hæc tria officia nempe, Propheticū, Sacerdotale, & Regium ipsi in Scripturis sacris distinctè, ac discertè tribui, iam supra capite vigesimotertio demonstrauimus (quod ipsum ad confirmandam sententiam nostram, non parum momenti, & ponderis adfert) ideò hoc loco ex Sacra scriptura recensebimus, omnes illas actiones, & functiones, quæ Christo ibi tribuuntur, ac proinde tum ad officium illud rite præstandum, tum ad vitam, ac salutem æternā nobis impetrādā, necessarię sunt. Quoniā enim ex illis, quę Christo in Scripturis tribuuntur, actionibus, ac functionibus, solidè demonstrari possunt, integram officii Christi vim duobus illis actibus, videl. tum iustitiæ, salutis, ac vitæ æternæ, per expiationem peccatorū, perfectissimo satisfactionis, & redemptionis persoluto ἀντρῳ factam, impetratione, & acquisitione: tum salutis, iustitiæ, ac vitæ æternæ, merito obedientiæ, & satisfactione acquisitæ, communicatione, ac distributione: perfectissimè contineri: ideò veritas sententiæ, ac doctrinæ nostræ, etiam clarissimè inde elucescet.
units.tr: Since, therefore, it is beyond controversy and doubt between us and our opponents that Jesus Christ was appointed by God the Father to be our Mediator, Saviour and Redeemer, but it is disputed how many offices belong to Christ our Mediator and Redeemer, and consequently what actions and functions are required both for the performance of the office of Mediator and for obtaining and imparting salvation and eternal life: we have already shown above, in chapter twenty-three, that Christ was appointed by God the Father to be Prophet, Priest and King, so that he could rightly discharge the office of Mediator and Saviour, and that these three offices, namely the prophetic, priestly and royal, are distinctly and expressly ascribed to him in the holy Scriptures (which contributes no little weight and force to confirming our view). Therefore in this place we shall recount from holy Scripture all those actions and functions which are ascribed to Christ there, and which are therefore necessary both for rightly performing that office and for obtaining eternal life and salvation for us. For from those actions and functions which the Scriptures ascribe to Christ, it can be solidly shown that the whole force of Christ's office is contained in two acts: namely, first, the obtaining and acquiring of righteousness, salvation and eternal life through the expiation of sins, accomplished by the most perfect satisfaction and by the payment of redemption (a ransom [ἀντίλυτρον]); and second, the communicating and distributing of salvation, righteousness and eternal life, acquired by the merit of obedience and satisfaction. Hence the truth of our view and teaching will also shine out most clearly from this.

units.la: Prima igitur fūctio, & actio quę Christo Mediatori, ac Redēptosi nostro tribuitur, ad officiū eius Propheticum pertinet, quatenus videvidel. nobis æternæ salutis via annuntiauit,& voluntatem Patris sui,de redemptione generis humani,plane plenéque patefecit, eădémque doctrinā suam plurimis stupendis miraculis cōfirmauit. Deut.18.15 .Prophetam e medio tui,& fratribus tuis,sicut ego sum, suscitabit tibi Iehouah Deus,ei auscultate:& v.18.Prophetam suscitabo eis,emedio fratrum ipsorum,sicut tu es,&indā verba mea ori eius,vt eloquatur ipsis quicquid præcepero ipsi:Esa.41.27.Primarium Tziioni ecce ecce ista,& Ierufchalaimis euangelizantem dabo.& 6.1.Spiritus Domini Iehouæ super me, eò quòd vnxit Iehouah me ad euangelizandum mansuetis misit me , ad sanandum contritos animo ad proclamandum captiuis libertatem,&vinctis apertură ergastuli: [quippe qui solus nouit Patrem,& omnes thesauros sapientiæ & cognitionis cœlestis in sese continet.]Ioh.1.18. Deum nemo vidit vnquam, vnigenitus Filius , qui est in sinu Patris,ipse enarrauit. Ich.15.15.Vos autē dixi amicos,quia omnia quæ audiui à Patre meo,nota feci vobis. Matth.11.27.Omnia mihi tradita sunt à Patre meo,& nemo nouit Filiū nisi Pater, neque quisquam Patrem nouit nisi Filius , & cuicūque voluerit Filius reuelare. Actor.1.3. Quibus etiam seipsum,postquam ipse passus fuit,repræsentarat viuum multis indubitatis signis , per dies quadraginta conspectus ab eis,& dicens,quæ ad regnum Dei spectant.Coloss. 2.verf.3. In Christo sunt omnes sapientiæ & cognitionis thesauri absconditi. Ephef.2.verf.17. Christus veniens euangelizauit pacem vobis qui procul eratis, & iis qui propè erant. Iohan.5.verf.36. Ego testimonium habeo maius testimonio Iohannis: Opera enim quæ dedit mihi Pater, vt ea perficerem, ipsa inquam opera,quæ ego facio,testantur de me quod Pater miserit me:Ioh.10.v.37. Si non facio opera Patris mei , nolite mihi credere : sin vero facio , etiamsi mihi non credatis,operibus credite,vt cognoscatis, & credatis Patrem in me esse,& me in eo. Ioh.20.v.30 31. Multa etiam alia signa edidit Iesus in discipulorum suorum cōspectu,quæ non sunt scripta in hoc libro : hæc autem scripta sunt , vt credatis Iesum esse Christum,& vt credentes vitam habeatis per nomen eius.
units.tr: The first function and action ascribed to Christ our Mediator and Redeemer pertains to his prophetic office, insofar as he announced to us the way of eternal salvation, plainly and fully revealed the will of his Father concerning the redemption of mankind, and confirmed this teaching with very many astonishing miracles. Deut. 18.15: "The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among you, from your brothers, like me; listen to him." And v. 18: "I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brothers, like you, and will put my words in his mouth, so that he may speak to them whatever I command him." Isa. 41.27: "Behold, behold, I will give these things to Zion, and to Jerusalem a messenger of good news." And 61.1 (Isa. 61.1): "The Spirit of the Lord Jehovah is upon me, because Jehovah has anointed me to bring good news to the meek; he has sent me to bind up the broken-hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and release to those in prison." [For he alone knows the Father, and contains within himself all the treasures of wisdom and heavenly knowledge.] John 1.18: "No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has made him known." John 15.15: "But I have called you friends, because all that I heard from my Father I have made known to you." Matt. 11.27: "All things have been delivered to me by my Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him." Acts 1.3: "To these he also presented himself alive after his suffering, by many convincing proofs, appearing to them over forty days and speaking of the things concerning the kingdom of God." Col. 2.3: "In Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge." Eph. 2.17: "Christ came and preached peace to you who were far off and to those who were near." John 5.36: "I have a witness greater than John's; for the works which the Father has given me to accomplish, these very works which I do, bear witness about me that the Father has sent me." John 10.37: "If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me; but if I do them, even if you do not believe me, believe the works, so that you may know and believe that the Father is in me and I in the Father." John 20.30-31: "Jesus did many other signs in the sight of his disciples, which are not written in this book; but these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, and that believing you may have life through his name."

units.la: Atque hinc est,quod iubemur hunc insignem Doctorē,Prophetam & Magistrū,tanquā immediatū diuinæ veritatis testem,in quo tanquam viua ac perfecta imagine Deus Pater ineffabilem suam sapientiam,charitatem,bonitatem, potentiam, φιλανθρωπίαν & misericordiā nobis contemplandā & conspiciendā exhibuit,reuerēter audire.Esa.55.verf.4.Ecce testem populis dedi eum,ducem ac præceptorem gentibus. Matth.17.v. 5.Adhuc eo loquente,ecce nubes lucida obumbrauit eos,& ecce vox e nube dicens,Hic est Filius ille meus dilectus,in quo acquiesco,ipsum audite. Ioh.14.ver. 9.Philippe,qui vidit me,vidit Patrem. Act.3.v.22.23. Prophetam suscitabit Dominus Deus vester vobis,ex fratribus vestris, sicut me, audietis eum in omnibus quæ loquutus fuerit vobis. Futurum est autem, vt quisquis non auscultauit Prophetam illum disperdatur è populo. 2.Cor.4.v.6. Quoniam Deus,qui dixit vt è tenebris lux splendesceret, is est qui splenduit in cordibus vestris, ad lumen cognitionis in facie Iesu Christi. Coloff.1.ver.15. Qui est imago Dei inconfpicui,primogenitus omnis rei creatæ. Hebr.1.v 3 Qui cùm fit splendor gloriæ, & character personæ illius. sustinéatque omnia verbo illo potentiæ, &c. 2.Pet.1.v.16.17.18. Non arte compositas fabulas fequuti, notam vobis fecimus Domini nostri Iesu Christi potentiam & aduentum:sed qui oculis nostris conspeximus ipsius maiestatem. Acceperat enim à Deo Patre honorem & gloriam, voce ad illum delata huiusmodi à magnifica Gloria:Hic est ille filius meus dilectus,in quo mihi complacui.Et hanc vocem nos audiuimus de cælo delatam,cùm essemus cum illo in monte sancto.
units.tr: And hence we are commanded to listen reverently to this distinguished teacher, prophet and master, as the immediate witness of divine truth, in whom God the Father has displayed to us, as in a living and perfect image, his ineffable wisdom, love, goodness, power, [φιλανθρωπίαν] and mercy, to be contemplated and beheld. Isa. 55:4. Behold, I have given him as a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander to the nations. Matt. 17:5. While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice from the cloud said: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear him. John 14:9. Philip, he who has seen me has seen the Father. Acts 3:22-23. The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers, like me; you shall hear him in all things that he says to you. And it shall be that everyone who does not listen to that prophet shall be destroyed from the people. 2 Cor. 4:6. For God, who said that light should shine out of darkness, is the one who has shone in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of God in the face of Jesus Christ. Col. 1:15. Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every created thing. Heb. 1:3. Who, being the brightness of glory and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, etc. 2 Pet. 1:16-18. For we did not follow cleverly devised fables, but made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ; we were eyewitnesses of his majesty. For he received from God the Father honor and glory, when such a voice was conveyed to him by the magnificent Glory: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. And we heard this voice brought from heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain.

units.la: Verùm hanc actionem ac functionem, qua videlicet Christus vitæ ac salutis æternæ consequendæ viam monstrauit,& voluntatem Patris sui de redemptione generis humani plenè nobis annûtiauit, doctrinámque suam multis stupendis miraculis confirmauit, totam ac perfectam officii ipsius mediatorii vim & naturam minimè complecti,ex eo liquet manifestissimè,tum quod Christo præter officium Propheticum, etiam Sacerdotale & Regium munus in scripturis sacris disertè ac distinctè tribuitur, quemadmodum capite vigesimo tertio à nobis est demonstratum, & ipsi aliæ quoque ad munus illud exequendum, & vitam ac salutem æternam nobis acquirendam & communicandam,necessariæ functiones & actiones assignantur,quas frustraneas& inutiles & sine causa ipsi iniunctas, atque ab eo præstitas esse, quis nisi plané impius dixerit? tum etiam, quia ipsi Prophetæ quoque & Apostoli viam salutis annuntiarunt. Act.16.ver.17. Isti homines serui sunt Dei illius summi, qui annuntiant vobis viam salutis: eandémque doctrinam suam multis miraculis & stupendis operibus confirmauerint: sic Moses Exod.7. dictorum suorum veritatem multis prodigiis miraculis coram Pharaone confirmat. Sic Elias facit vt ignis Ieho-uæ decidens consumat holocaustum, & ligna, & lapides, & pulverem in- psum, & aquam, quæ erat in aquæductu, delingat. 1.Reg.18.38. Sic Petrus claudo dicit: Argentum & aurum non habeo, quod autem habeo hoc tibi do: In nomine Iesu Christi surge, & ambula: & prehensa manu eius dextera, erexit eum: illico vero confirmati sunt pedes eius, ac malleoli. Act. 3.v.6. Sic Act.5.vers.12. Per manus Apostolorum edebant signa & miracula multa in populo: vers.15.16. Adeo vt in plateas efferrent ægrotos, & ponerent in lectis ac grabbatis, vt venientis Petri vel vmbra inumbraret aliquem eorum. Conueniebat autem etiam vulgus vicinarum vrbium in Hierusalem, adducens ægrotos, ac vexatos à Spiritibus impuris, qui sanabatur omnes. Huc refer illud Christi Iohan.14.versu duodecimo: Amen amen dico vobis, qui credit in me, opera quæ ego facio, & ipse faciet, & maiora istis faciet. Vnde etiam non paucos suorum Auditorum seruasse dicuntur. Rom.11.v.14. Si quo modo ad æmulandum provocem carnem meam, & se uem aliquot ex illis. 1. Cor. 9. v.22. Omnibus factus sum omnia, vt omnino aliquos seruem. 1.Tim. 4.v.16. Attende tibi ipsi, & doctrinæ per- siste in istis, id enim si feceris, & teipsum seruabis, & eos qui te audierint. Iac.5.v.20. Qui conuerti fecerit peccatorem ab errore viæ suæ, seruabit animam à morte quos tamen Mediatores, seruatores, ac redemptores nostros appellare, nefas esset, quia Christus hoc vnus mediatorium sibi proprium vendicat, sic vt neque ex integro, neque parte aliqua sua ad alium transferri possit. Esai. cap. 43. vers.11. Deus iustos saluans, & seruans non est prater me: & cap. 48.vers.11. Gloriam meam alteri non dabo. Act. 4.vers.12. Nec est in alio quoquam salus, nec aliud nomen est sub cælo, quod datum sit inter homines, per quod oporteat nos saluari. Neque hoc conuellit consequentiam argumenti nostri, quod Prophetæ nonnisi de ventura salute, & quidem obscurius prophetarint: 1.Pet.1.vers.10.11.12. De qua salute inquisierunt & scrutati sunt Prophetæ, qui venturam in vos gratiam prædixerunt. Scrutantes in quem, aut cuius modi temporis articulum, prænuntius ille qui in ipsis erat, Spiritus Christi, declararet euenturas Christo perpes- siones: & gloriam illas consequuturam. Quibus patefactum est, eos non sibi, sed nobis ea administrare, quæ nunc annunciata sunt vobis, per eos qui prædicarunt vobis Euangelium, per emissum è cælo Spiritum sanctum, in quæ desiderant Angeli introspicere. Apostoli verò nomine Christi, tanquam eius legati ac ministri prædicarint, & virtutem, ac autoritatem miracula patrandi, & sic veritatem doctrinæ abipsis traditæ confirmandi ab ipso Christo acceperint:2. Cor.5. verf. 20. Nomine Christi legatione fungimur, velut Deo precante per nos:2. Cor.13.verf.3. Quandoquidem experimentum quaritis, in me loquentis Christi, qui erga vos non est infirmus, sed potens est in vobis. Satis enim est, vtrosque eandem salutis ac vitæ æternæ consequendæ viam prædicaffe, & mundo reuelaffe, nempè Christum crucifixum, eandémque doctrinæ ipsorum veris miraculis confirmaffe, Act.10.v.42.43. Præcepit autem nobis vt prædicaremus populo, ac testificari mur, eum esse qui definitus fit à Deo, Iudex viuorum & mortuorum. Huic enim omnes Prophetæ testimonium dant, remissionem peccatorum accepturum per nomen eius quemuis qui crediderit in eum. Act. 26.v.22.23. Auxilium à Deo nactus perfti in hunc vsque diem, testificans ista tum paruis tum magnis, nec quicquam dicens extra ea, quæ Prophetæ & Moses futura prædixerunt, Christum nempe esse passurum ac primum ex resurrectione mortuorum lucem annunciaturum huic populo & Gentibus. Rom.verf.21.22. Nunc verò absque lege iustitia Dei patefacta est, comprobata testimonio Legis ac Prophetarum, iustitia inquam Dei per fidem Iesu Christi, in omnes & supet omnes qui credunt,& cap.1.v.2. Quod Euangelium ante promiserat per Prophetas in Scripturis sanctis:& cap.10.v.16. Sed non omnes auscultarunt Euangelio: Esaias enim dicit: Domine quis credidit sermoni nostro? aut igitur per sermonem illum: quem Esaias prædicauit, intelligitur eadem doctrina Euangelii quam docuit & prædicauit Paulus, aut certè locus ille Iesaiæ impertinenter à Paulo est allegatus, quod absurdum esset:1. Cor.2. verf.2. Non decreueram quicquam scire inter vos, nisi Iesum Christum, eumque crucifixum. Præsertim cum etiam Christus ipse æterni sui Patris in annunciandis nobis salutis doctrina, Minister ac legatus fuerit: Esai.53.v.11. Cognitione sui Seruus meus iustificabit multos, quorum iniquitates ipse baiulauerit, Ioh.7.v.16. Respondit Iesus & dixit, Mea doctrina non est mea, sed eius qui misit me: & verf.28.29. Et me noftis & vnde sim noftis, & à me ipso non veni, sed est verax qui misit me, quem vos non noftis: ego vero noui eū, quia ab ipso sum, & ille me misit. & cap.14.v.10. Non credis me in Patre, & Patrem in me esse? Verba quæ ego loquor vobis, à meipso non loquor, sed Pater qui in me manet, ipse facit opera, Heb.1.v.1. Deus vltimis diebus hisce nobis loquutus est per Filium. Ex quibus euidenter apparet verissimum esse id quod paulo ante lò ante affirmauimus, nempe hanc actionem muneris Christi prophetici, totius officii ipsius mediatorii vim, & naturam totam minimè constituere.
units.tr: But that this function and office, namely that Christ showed the way to attain eternal life and salvation, fully announced to us the will of his Father concerning the redemption of the human race, and confirmed his teaching by many astonishing miracles, does not embrace the whole and complete force and nature of his mediatorial office, is most plainly evident. First, because in the holy Scriptures Christ is expressly and distinctly assigned, besides the prophetic office, also the priestly and kingly office, as we demonstrated in chapter twenty-three. Second, because other functions and actions necessary for carrying out that office, and for acquiring and communicating eternal life and salvation to us, are assigned to him; and who but a plainly impious man would say that these were pointless and useless, imposed on him without cause, and performed by him to no purpose? Third, because the prophets and apostles too announced the way of salvation. Acts 16:17. These men are servants of the most high God, who announce to you the way of salvation. And they confirmed this same teaching of theirs by many miracles and astonishing works. Thus Moses, in Exodus 7, confirms the truth of his words before Pharaoh by many prodigies and miracles. So Elijah does: so that the fire of the LORD falling consumed the burnt offering, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench. 1 Kings 18:38. So Peter says to the lame man: I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ, rise up and walk; and taking him by the right hand, he raised him up, and at once his feet and ankles were strengthened. Acts 3:6. So Acts 5:12: Through the hands of the apostles many signs and miracles were done among the people. Verses 15-16: so that they carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and couches, so that when Peter came, at least his shadow might fall on some of them. Moreover, the crowd also came together from the neighboring cities into Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those troubled by unclean spirits, and they were all healed. Refer to that saying of Christ, John 14:12: Amen, amen, I say to you, he who believes in me, the works that I do he also shall do, and greater than these he shall do. Whence it is also said that they saved not a few of their hearers. Rom. 11:14: If somehow I may provoke my flesh to jealousy and save some of them. 1 Cor. 9:22: I have become all things to all men, that I might by all means save some. 1 Tim. 4:16: Take heed to yourself and to the teaching; persist in these things, for if you do this you will save both yourself and those who hear you. James 5:20: He who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death. Yet it would be wrong to call them our mediators, saviors and redeemers, because Christ claims this mediatorial role as his own, so that it cannot be transferred to another, either wholly or in any part. Isa. 43:11: There is no God besides me who saves and keeps the just. Isa. 48:11: I will not give my glory to another. Acts 4:12: Nor is there salvation in any other; nor is there any other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved. Nor does this break the force of our argument, that the prophets prophesied only of the coming salvation, and that too rather obscurely. 1 Pet. 1:10-12: Concerning this salvation the prophets inquired and searched, who prophesied of the grace that would come to you, searching what person or what time the Spirit of Christ within them was pointing to, when he testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ and the glories that would follow. To them it was revealed that they were ministering not to themselves but to you those things which have now been announced to you through those who preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, into which things the angels long to look. The apostles, however, preached in the name of Christ as his envoys and ministers, and received from Christ himself the power and authority to work miracles, and so to confirm the truth of the doctrine handed down by them. 2 Cor. 5:20: We act as ambassadors in the name of Christ, as though God were exhorting you through us. 2 Cor. 13:3: Since you seek proof of Christ speaking in me, who is not weak toward you but is powerful among you. For it is enough that both preached the same way of salvation and of attaining eternal life, and revealed it to the world, namely Christ crucified, and confirmed their teaching by true miracles. Acts 10:42-43: He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead. To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him will receive forgiveness of sins through his name. Acts 26:22-23: Having obtained help from God, I have stood firm to this day, testifying these things both small and great, and saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses foretold: that Christ would suffer, and that, as the first to rise from the dead, he would proclaim light to this people and to the Gentiles. Rom. 3:21-22: But now apart from the law the righteousness of God has been revealed, attested by the Law and the Prophets: the righteousness of God, I say, through faith in Jesus Christ, for all and upon all who believe. And ch. 1:2: which he had promised beforehand through his prophets in the holy Scriptures. And ch. 10:16: But not all obeyed the gospel; for Isaiah says: Lord, who has believed our report? Either, therefore, by that report which Isaiah preached is meant the same doctrine of the gospel that Paul taught and preached, or else Paul cited that passage of Isaiah irrelevantly, which would be absurd. 1 Cor. 2:2: I determined to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified. Especially since Christ himself, in announcing to us the doctrine of salvation, was also the minister and envoy of his eternal Father. Isa. 53:11: By his knowledge my servant will justify many, and he will bear their iniquities. John 7:16: Jesus answered and said: My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me. And verses 28-29: You both know me and know where I am from, and I have not come of myself, but he who sent me is true, whom you do not know; but I know him, because I am from him and he sent me. And ch. 14:10: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father in me? The words that I speak to you I do not speak from myself, but the Father who dwells in me does the works. Heb. 1:1-2: God in these last days has spoken to us through the Son. From which it clearly appears most true what we affirmed a little before: that this action of Christ's prophetic office does by no means constitute the whole force and nature of his entire mediatorial office.

units.la: Secunda functio & actio, quæ Christo Mediatori in sacris Scripturis tribuitur, pertinet ad officium Christi sacerdotale, quatenus videlicet ipse exemplo vitæ, passionis, mortis, & gloriosæ resurrectionis suæ, viam salutis æternæ in sua ipsius persona nobis ostendit,& confirmauit. Quantum enim ad sanctam Christi vitam concernit, ipsum nobis viuendi exemplum reliquisse, Christumq; nobis & in vita & in morte ad imitandum propositum esse,& ipsæ Scripturæ sacræ euidenter docent, & illa vnio fidelium cum Christo, & inde nascens communio cum vita, morte, & resurrectione Christi, solidè euincit: Matt.16.v.24. Tunc Iesus dixit discipulis suis: Si quis vult post me venire, abneget sese, & tollat crucem suam, ac sequatur me. Rom. 6.v. 4.5. Sepulti igitur sumus vnà cum Christo per baptismum in mortem vt sicut Christus excitatus est ex mortuis in gloriam Patris, ita & nos in noua vita ambulemus. Nam si cum eo plantari coaluimus conformatione mortis eius, nimirum etiam resurrectionis conformatione coalescemus.Ephes. 4.v.20. 21. 22.23.24. Vos autem non ita didicistis Christum, si modo eum audistis, & per eum edocti fuistis,sicut est veritas in Iesu:nempe deponere, quod ad priStinam conuersationem attinet, veterem illum hominem, qui deceptricibus cupiditatibus corrumpitur, renouari verò spiritu mentis vestræ, & induere nouum illum hominem, qui secundum Deum conditus est ad iustitiam,& sanctimoniam veram. Col.3.v.1.2.3 4.5. Itaque si resurrexistis cum Christo,superna quærite,vbi Christus est ad dexteram Dei sedens, superna curate non terrestria. Nam mortui estis, & vita vestra abscondita est cum Christo in Deo:quando Christus vita nostra patefactus fuerit, tum & vos cum eo patefietis gloriosi:mortificate igitur membra vestra terrestria &c. 1.Cor.11.v.1. Imitatores mei estote sicut ego Christi. 1.Thess.1.verf.6. Et vos imitatores nostri facti fuistis & Domini, recepto sermone cum oppressione multa cum gaudio Spiritus Sancti. 1.Ioh.2.verf.3. Per hoc scimus nos eum nosse,si mandata ipsius obseruamus: & verf.6. Qui dicit se in eo habitare,debet sicut ipse ambulauit,ita & ipse ambulare: & cap.3.verf.16. Per hoc cognouimus charitatem,quod ille animam suam pro nobis posuit, nos igitur debemus pro fratribus animas ponere: & cap. 4. verf. 17. Per hoc expleta est charitas in nobis, vt fiduciam habeamus in die iudicii, quod qualis ille est, tales & nos fumus in hoc mundo.
units.tr: The second function and action that Holy Scripture ascribes to Christ the Mediator belongs to his priestly office, namely that by the example of his life, passion, death, and glorious resurrection, he has shown and confirmed in his own person the way of eternal salvation for us. That Scripture clearly teaches that Christ left us a pattern of living, and that he is set before us, in life and in death, for imitation, is shown by the sacred texts themselves, and the union of believers with Christ, and the communion with the life, death, and resurrection of Christ that springs from it, solidly proves the same: Matt.16.v.24. Then Jesus said to his disciples: If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. Rom. 6.v. 4.5. We are therefore buried with Christ through baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead to the glory of the Father, so we too should walk in newness of life. For if we have grown together with him in the likeness of his death, we shall certainly also grow together in the likeness of his resurrection. Ephes. 4.v.20. 21. 22.23.24. But you have not so learned Christ, if indeed you have heard him and have been taught by him, as the truth is in Jesus: namely, to put off, as regards your former way of life, the old man, who is corrupted by deceitful lusts, and to be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and to put on the new man, who after God is created in true righteousness and holiness. Col.3.v.1.2.3 4.5. If therefore you have risen with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God; set your minds on things above, not on things on earth. For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God; when Christ, who is our life, is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in glory. Put to death therefore your earthly members, etc. 1.Cor.11.v.1. Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ. 1.Thess.1.verf.6. And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, receiving the word in much affliction, with the joy of the Holy Spirit. 1.Ioh.2.verf.3. By this we know that we know him, if we keep his commandments; and verse 6. whoever says he abides in him ought to walk just as he walked; and chapter 3, verse 16. By this we have known love, that he laid down his life for us; so we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers; and chapter 4, verse 17. By this love is perfected in us, that we may have confidence on the day of judgment, because as he is, so are we in this world.

units.la: Quantum deinde ad varias illas actiones, miserias, & calamitates, quas Christus in statu humiliationis sustinuit, & mortem ipsam, quam subiit, concernit, fatemur Christum sanguinem suum etiam in hunc finem profundere voluisse, vt fœdus illud gratiæ à Deo cum hominibus initum, illo obsignaret, vti ipsa sacra scriptura hoc ipsum aperte docet. Marc. 14. verf 24. Hoc est sanguis meus Noui illius Testamenti, qui pro multis effunditur. Hebr. 9. v. 16. 17. 18. 19. Vbi Testamentum est, mors intercedat necesse est Testatoris: Testamentum enim in mortuis ratum est, quandoquidem nodum valet dum viuit Testator: vnde ne prius illud quidem absque sanguine dedicatum fuit. Quum enim Moses omnia mandata fecundum legem recitaffet toti populo, sumpto sanguine vitulorum & hircorum, cum aqua, & lana coccina, & hyssopo simul & ipsum librum, & totum populum aspersit, dicens, Hic est sanguis Testamenti, quod mandauit vobis Deus. & cap. 12. verf. 24. Accessistis ad noui Testamenti mediatorem Iesum, & sanguinem aspersionis, præstantiora loquentem quàm loqueretur sanguis Abel. & cap. 13. verf. 20. Qui magnum illum ouium per sanguinem fœderis æterni pastorem Dominum nostrum Iesum à mortuis reduxit.
units.tr: Next, as regards the various actions, miseries, and calamities that Christ endured in the state of humiliation, and the death itself that he underwent, we confess that Christ wished to shed his blood also for this end, that he might seal with it that covenant of grace made by God with men, as Holy Scripture itself clearly teaches. Marc. 14. verf 24. This is my blood of the New Testament, which is poured out for many. Hebr. 9. v. 16. 17. 18. 19. Where there is a testament, the death of the testator must necessarily intervene; for a testament is valid over the dead, since it has no force while the testator lives. Hence not even the first covenant was dedicated without blood. For when Moses had recited all the commandments according to the law to the whole people, he took the blood of calves and goats, with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people, saying: This is the blood of the testament that God has commanded you. & chapter 12, verse 24. You have come to Jesus, the mediator of the new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood, which speaks better things than the blood of Abel. & chapter 13, verse 20. God, who brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of the eternal covenant.

units.la: Denique quod ad ipsam Christi resurrectionem & exaltationem attinet, etiam profitemur, & ex Scriptura ipsa docemus, Christum gloriosa resurrectione, & fui ipsius exaltatione nos regenerare in spem vitæ æternæ, fidémque nostram ac fiduciam non parum stabilire, dum videlicet in Principem illum vitæ perpetuò respicientes, in via salutis, & confragoso vitæ huius stadio qui per tot ærumnarum salebras emetiendum nobis est, animosè & alacriter decurrendo, confirmemur. 1. Pet. 1. v. 3. 4. 5. Benedictus Deus, & Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui ex multa misericordia regenuit nos in spem viuâ per resurrectionem Iesu Christi ex mortuis, in hæreditatem quæ nec perire potest, nec contaminari, nec marcescere nobis in cœlis seruatam, qui virtute Dei custodimur per fidē ad salutem quæ parata est patefieri tempore vltimo: & 3. v. 21. Cui rei nunc correspondens exemplar Baptismi nos quoque feruet (non quo carnis sordes abiiciuntur, sed quo fit, vt bona conscientia Deum interroget) per resurrectionem Iesu Christi. Rom. 1. Rom.1.v.3. Declarato filio Dei potenter secundum Spiritum sanctificationis, per resurrectionem a mortuis. Act.5.v.30. Deus Patrum nostrorum excitauit Iesum, quem vos interfecistis suspensum in ligno. Hunc Deus dextra sua exaltauit, constituit Principem ac Sacerdotem, vt det resipiscentiam Israeli, & remissionem peccatorum, Rom. 10.verf.9. Quod si confessus fueris ore Dominum Iesum, & credideris in corde tuo, quod Deus eum excitauit a mortuis, seruaberis.
units.tr: Finally, as regards Christ's own resurrection and exaltation, we likewise profess, and teach from Scripture itself, that by his glorious resurrection and his own exaltation Christ regenerates us to the hope of eternal life, and greatly strengthens our faith and trust, namely when, looking constantly to that Prince of life, we are confirmed as we run boldly and eagerly along the way of salvation and through the rough course of this life, which we must traverse over many rocky stretches of trouble. 1. Pet. 1. v. 3. 4. 5. Blessed be God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in his great mercy has regenerated us to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, to an inheritance that cannot perish, nor be defiled, nor fade, reserved in heaven for us, who by the power of God are guarded through faith unto a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. & 3. v. 21. Corresponding to this, baptism now also saves us, as a figure of it (not by putting away the filth of the flesh, but by the answer of a good conscience toward God), through the resurrection of Jesus Christ. Rom. 1. Rom. 1.v.3. Declared to be the Son of God in power, according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead. Act. 5.v.30. The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree. God exalted him at his right hand as Prince and Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins. Rom. 10. verse 9. If you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

units.la: Quamuis vero haec actio Christi insignis sit, & ad fidem, atque spem in nobis gignendam, & fouendam plurimum momenti habeat, hac tamen cum priori licet coniuncta, totam officii mediatorii vim atque naturam & principalem fructum mortis & passionis Christi Seruatoris σωτήρος minime comprehendi, ex sequentibus rationibus, & argumentis solide demonstratur. Primo videlicet, quia Christo in Scripturis sacris praeter has enumeratas, aliae etiam tribuuntur, & assignantur actiones, atque functiones ad munus mediatorium exequendum, & vitam, atque salutem aeternam nobis acquirendam, & communicandam, in sacris Scripturis tribuuntur, quemadmodum paulo post demonstrabimus. Secundo quia hae duae actiones Christi, nempe veritatis diuinae annuntiatio, & confirmatio, ad fidem, & resipiscentiam in nobis gignendam, inutiles sunt & inefficaces, nisi interior ille magister, Spiritus videlicet Christi accedat, cuius illuminatione, & renouatione demum fit, vt in doctrina Christi veritatem, & in operibus, ac miraculis eiusdem potentiam diuinam oculis mentis nostrae cernere queamus. Quandoquidem homo animalis, & in statu natiuae caecitatis, ac dominantis peccati constitutus, sine luce spirituali ipsi praefulgente, res spirituales, etiā cū docetur percipere nequit, quemadmodū capite primo, itē vigesimosexto, & vigesimoseptimo prolixe a nobis est demonstratū. Et diligenter notanda est in hac ipsa controuersia falsa illa hypothesis, quam in disputationibus suis praesupponūt Aduersarii, nēpè posse homine etiam absque interna Sp.
