That is to say, the very death and shedding of the blood of Christ, or that obedience of his which was rendered to God the Father even unto death on the cross and the shedding of blood, is the cause on account of which God justifies believers and remits their sins. He raised Christ to such a height of majesty, glory and honour. For that power of forgiving our sins, and of washing and cleansing us through renewal and regeneration, is to be referred, as the efficient cause of justification, to God himself, who alone forgives sins, and who, by the Holy Spirit, consecrates to himself as a special people, eager for good works, believers who have been renewed and regenerated. From this it is plain that the adversary's inference labours under a double fault. For it rests on a false hypothesis, since it attributes to us an opinion that is not ours. And, by removing one effect of a single cause which has many effects and fruits, it commits the gravest of fallacies of opposites, drawing its argument from the truth of another effect. For each effect, namely both the forgiveness of sins and the exaltation of Christ resulting from his obedience, is ascribed in the holy Scriptures to his obedience as the efficient cause. The former is found in Rom. 3:24-25: "They are justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God set forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness through the forgiveness of past sins"; and in 5:9: "Therefore, having been justified by his blood, we shall be saved much more through him from wrath." The latter is found in Phil. 2:6-9: "Who, being in the form of God, did not count being equal with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men, and found in appearance as a man, he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death,

units.la: Nnn tem,mortem autē crucis : quapropter etiam Deus ipsum extulit in sum-mam sublimitatem,ac donauit ei nomē,quod est supra omne nomen, &c.
units.tr: even the death of the cross. Therefore God also exalted him to the highest place and gave him the name that is above every name," and so on.

units.la: Secundum, quod contra argumentum nostrum excipit Aduer-sarius, est : purgandi seu emundandi verbum in sacris literis non semper rem ipsam, sed rei ipsius declarationem & demonstrationem significare:vt Leu.12.v.7.8. Qui offerens illam coram Iehoua expiationem faciet pro ea:sic purgata erit à profluuio sanguinis sui : quod si non assequatur manus eius quantum satis est pro par-ua pecude, tum accipiet duos turtures, aut duos pullos columbæ, vnum in holocaustum, alterum in peccatū, & expiationem faciet pro ea Sacerdos,sic munda erit : Sic cap.15. v.15.30.& c.13.14.totis. Ex vsu igitur sacræ Scripturæ recte dici posse, sanguinem Christi nos ab omnibus peccatis nostris purgare, etiamsi tantummodo significaret Deum nos à peccatis nostris purgasse, quandoquidem Deus illo veluti sigillo nobis promissam peccatorum remissionem obsignauit, & sic nouum atque æternum fœdus nobiscum pepigit atque sanciuit.
units.tr: Second, what the adversary objects against our argument is this: the word "to purge" or "to cleanse" in the sacred letters does not always signify the thing itself, but a declaration and demonstration of that thing. Thus Lev. 12:7-8: "He shall offer it before the LORD and make atonement for her; so she shall be cleansed from the flow of her blood. But if her hand does not reach as far as enough for a lamb, then she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering, and the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean." So also 15:15, 30, and chapters 13 and 14 throughout. Therefore, from the usage of Holy Scripture, it can rightly be said that the blood of Christ cleanses us from all our sins, even if it only signified that God has cleansed us from our sins, since God, as with a seal, has sealed to us the forgiveness of sins promised by that blood, and thus has made and ratified a new and eternal covenant with us.

units.la: Syllogismus talis est:
units.tr: The syllogism runs thus:

units.la: Si verbum purgare,siue mundare non semper rem seu mundationem & purgationem ipsam,sed ipsius declarationem, atque demōstra-tionem significat, & Deus sanguine Christi veluti sigillo promis-sam remissionem peccatorum nobis obsignauit, & sic nouum at-que æternum fœdus nobiscum pepigit,atque sanciuit:tum sanguis Iesu Christi,ideo nos à peccatis nostris purgare recte dicatur,qua-tenus videlicet nobis promissam à Deo remissionem peccatorum obsignat :
units.tr: If the word "to purge" or "to cleanse" signifies not always the thing itself, that is, the cleansing and purging, but its declaration and demonstration, and God has sealed to us by the blood of Christ, as with a seal, the forgiveness of sins promised, and thus has made and ratified a new and eternal covenant with us, then the blood of Jesus Christ is rightly said to cleanse us from our sins, insofar as it seals to us the forgiveness of sins promised by God.

units.la: Atqui prius est verum: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: But the first is true; therefore the second is too.

units.la: Resp. Primo,mundationem seu purgationem non tantum expia-tionem ab externa cōtaminatione per sacra,& ritus ceremoniales, verum etiam sanationem, atque adeo etiam solam pronuntiatio-nem,aut iustificationem de munditie alicuius significare ex Leui-tico constat:sed quum interdum,imò frequentiore vsu veram et-iam liberationem, & emūdationem à peccato vox eadem denotet quæ fit vel per remissionem peccatorum,vt Psal.51.v.3.4.Gratiam fac mihi ô Deus secudum benignitatē tuā,secundum amplitudinem mi-serationum tuarum dele defectiones meas, multum ablue me ab iniqui-tate mea, & à peccato meo munda me, vel per renouationem ac re-generationem Spir.S.vt Psal.51.ver.12. Animum mundum crea in me Deus.Ephef.5. v.25.26.27. Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, & semetipsum exposuit pro ea,vt eam sanctificaret,postquàm eam purgasset lauacro aquæ per verbum: vt sisteret eam sibi gloriosam Ecclesiam non habetem maculam, aut rugam,aut quicquam eiusmodi, sed vt esset sancta & inculpata: hinc apparet connexum syllogismi esse falsum. Ex eo enim quod verbum mundare, & purgare interdum mundationis declarationem significat,nõ sequitur Christi sanguine nos ideò tantùm mundari,seu purgatos dici,quia videlicet nobis promissam peccatorũ remissionem declaret, atq; obsignet, seu verbum illud etiam in illis Scripturæ dictis,in quibus sanguis Iesu Christi nos à peccatis nostris purgare dicitur, primo illo significatu intelligedum esse. Secundò totum argumentum,omissa illa particula exclusiua tantummodò,cõcedi posse : Quemadmodum enim Christus nobis per mortem,passionem ac effusionem sanguinis sui, remissionem peccatorum apud Deum Patrẽ impetrauit:ita etiam efficit,vt Sp. S. mediante verbo gratiæ, remissionis peccatorum & iustitiæ imputatæ testimonium nobis perhibeat. Vt verò hæc testificatio & hic fructus ipsam remissionem peccatorũ non tollit,sed presupponit: ita posterior hæc verbi illius significatio obsignationem confirmationem & testificationẽ denotans,priorẽ,quę ipsam remissionẽ significat,minimè euertit. Neq; etiam ex eo quòd sanguis Christi,sanguis Noui ac perpetui Testamenti appellatur, sequitur effusione sanguinis, & morte Christi nobis remissionẽ peccatorũ partā non esse.Nā mortis & sanguinis Christi effusi, duplex fuit vsus:respectu quidẽ sacerdotii,quod per mortẽ &effusionẽ sanguinis agni illius immaculati redẽptionẽ, & absolutionẽ obtinemus ab iis omnib.præuaricationib.quib.priori illo Testam.nexi & obligati tenebamur:respectu verò Testameti,quia nõ satisfuit, nos absolui ac liberari à transgressionib. & peccatis nostris, nisi prout hæredes Testaméto instituti fumus àChristo Seruatore nostro,ita morte ipsius Testamentum fuisset ratũ. Christus igitur,propriè loquendo, tripliciter nos morte & sanguine suo à peccatis nostris lauare ac purgare dicitur : Primùm videlicet merito suo, quoniam mors & effusio sanguinis sui ἀπολύτρωσιν,& pretiũ satisfactorium Deo, pro peccatis nostris,propter quod nos à peccatorũ & mortis reatu absoluit,persolutum vt ex antecedentibus liquet & deinceps plurib. demõstrabitur. Secundò,Quatenus per & propter mortẽ Christi,iustificationis & remissionis peccatorũ ita participes reddimur, vt simul per Spiritum Christi, de paterno Dei erga nos amore, & gratuita remissione peccatorum,& reconciliatione cum Deo certiores reddamur, & sic à metu mortis, quo perpetuò trepidabamus,liberemur.Tertiò cùm per Spiritum sanctum, circumcisione ἐχρίσματι virtute mortis & resurrectionis Christi natura nostra regeneratur,& peccatum in carne nostra mortificatur. Atque hæc triplex purgatio intelligitur, quoties sanguis Iesu Christi nos à peccatis purgare,& liberare dicitur.
units.tr: Reply. First, it is clear from Leviticus that cleansing or purging signifies not only the expiation of external contamination through sacred rites and ceremonial observances, but also healing, and even the mere pronouncement or declaration of someone's cleanness. But since, at times, and indeed more often in use, the same word also denotes true liberation and cleansing from sin, which is effected either through the forgiveness of sins, as in Ps. 51:3-4, "Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love; according to your abundant mercy blot out my transgressions. Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin," or through the renewal and regeneration of the Holy Spirit, as in Ps. 51:12, "Create in me a clean heart, O God." Eph. 5:25-27: "Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for her, that he might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water with the word, so that he might present the Church to himself in splendour, without spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she might be holy and blameless." Hence it appears that the connection of the syllogism is false. For from the fact that the words "to cleanse" and "to purge" sometimes signify the declaration of cleansing, it does not follow that we are cleansed by the blood of Christ and said to be purged only because it declares and seals to us the forgiveness of sins promised, or that the word, in those passages of Scripture where the blood of Jesus Christ is said to cleanse us from our sins, must be understood in that first sense. Second, the whole argument may be granted, with the exclusive particle "only" omitted. For just as Christ obtained for us, through his death, passion and shedding of blood, the forgiveness of sins before God the Father, so also, through the Holy Spirit and by means of the word of grace, he brings it about that the testimony of the forgiveness of sins and of imputed righteousness is borne to us. But just as this testimony and this fruit do not take away the forgiveness of sins itself but presuppose it, so this latter meaning of the word, which signifies sealing, confirmation and testimony, by no means overturns the former, which signifies the forgiveness itself. Nor does it follow, from the fact that the blood of Christ is called the blood of the New and Everlasting Testament, that the forgiveness of sins was not obtained by the death of Christ and the shedding of his blood. For the death and the shed blood of Christ had a twofold use: with respect to the priesthood, by which through the death and shedding of blood of that spotless Lamb we obtain redemption and absolution from all the transgressions by which we were bound and obligated under the former covenant; and with respect to the testament, because it was not enough that we should be absolved and freed from our transgressions and sins, unless we were also made heirs instituted in the testament by Christ our Saviour, and so the testament would have been ratified by his death. Christ, therefore, properly speaking, is said to wash and cleanse us from our sins by his death and blood in three ways. First, namely by his merit, since the death and shedding of his blood, as a redemption [ἀπολύτρωσιν] and a satisfactory price paid to God for our sins, by which he absolved us from the guilt of sin and death, is paid, as is clear from what has gone before and will be shown at greater length later. Second, insofar as, through and on account of the death of Christ, we are made so to share in justification and the forgiveness of sins that, at the same time, through the Spirit of Christ, we are made more certain of the Father's love towards us, of the free forgiveness of sins and of reconciliation with God, and so are freed from the fear of death, by which we were constantly trembling. Third, when, through the Holy Spirit, our nature is regenerated by the anointing [ἐχρίσματι] and by the power of the death and resurrection of Christ, and sin is mortified in our flesh. And this threefold cleansing is understood whenever the blood of Jesus Christ is said to cleanse and free us from sins.

units.la: Tertium quod Aduersarius contra illud argumentum nostrum excipit,est,quod videlicet Christus,cum semetipsum victimâ pro peccatis nostris Deo obtulisse perhibetur,hoc per comparationem ac similitudinem cum victimis in Veteri Testamento oblatis, inprimis autem cum solenni & anniuersario illo sacrificio, ad quod peragendum Sacerdos sanctum sanctorum ingrediebatur,fecisse dicitur, quemadmodum ex epistola ad Hebraeos,in qua de sacrificio Christi prolixè agitur, manifestè appareat. Quemadmodum igitur,inquit,tum temporis, populus peracto illo sacrificio,à peccatis liberabatur, non quòd vis, ac virtus aliqua in illo sacrificio Deo pro peccatis satisfaciendi fuerit: sed quia ipse effectus, nempe liberatio à peccatis, ex Dei decreto & voluntate sequutus est: ita etiam sacrificio Christi peracto, à peccatis liberantur omnes qui in ipsum credunt,& ipsi obediunt, non quod vis, & δυνάμεις aliqua satisfactoria pro peccatis nostris,in iis quae in persona Christi facta sunt,latuerit:sed quia effectus ipse oblationem illam sequutus sit,quandoquidem Deus decreuerat Christum,si ipsi ad mortem crucis usque obedire, non tantùm beata immortalitate, verùm etiam eiusmodi potestate donare, qua suos quoque omnes immortales ac saluos reddere posset. Quandoquidem igitur Deo eiusmodi obedienti am praestitit,&sic praedictam potestatem assequutus est,ideò certum est nos qui in ipsum credimus, & quos ille amat, propter peccata nostra non condemnabimur, sed per Christum à morte, ad vitam æternam ac beatam immortalitatem perducemur. Hisce verò,& hoc addendum, dicit, quod quemadmodum vetus illud & anniuersarium sacrificium non tum temporis,quo illud macta batur.sed tu demum, cùm à Sacerdote sanguis illius in Sanctum sanctorum deferebatur,plane peractum fuerat: ita etiam sacrificium Christi, non eo tempore quo ille occisus & crucifixus est, sed tum demum cùm ille in cœlum ingressus Deo Patri se pro nobis sistit ac obtulit, peractum est: nam ipsum cœlum in hac similitudine Sancto sanctorum respondere,ex epistola ad Hebraeos manifestè apparet. Ac proinde ex victima & sacrificio Christi,nulla sa-tisfactio. tisfactio pro peccatis nostris concludi ac demonstrari potest, quandoquidem secundum Aduersariorum sententiam satisfactio illa non in cœlo, sed in cruce facta est, Christi vero sacrificium in cœlis peractum est. Per quod sacrificium Christi Scriptura sacra nihil aliud intelligit quàm ipsam potestatem seu potentiam Christi admirabilem, quam ille per sui ipsius præsentationem coram Deo exercet, & per quam peccata nostra revera auferuntur atque tolluntur. Verùm hac ipsa de re pollicetur Aduersarius, se in explicatione muneris Christi Regii pluribus acturum esse.
units.tr: The third point that my opponent raises against our argument is this: that Christ, when he is said to have offered himself as a victim for our sins to God, is said to have done so by comparison and likeness with the sacrifices offered in the Old Testament, and especially with that solemn and yearly sacrifice, for which the priest entered the Holy of Holies, as is clearly evident from the Epistle to the Hebrews, where the sacrifice of Christ is treated at length. Therefore, he says, just as at that time the people were freed from sins once that sacrifice had been completed, not because any force or virtue in that sacrifice had power to satisfy God for sins, but because the effect itself, namely liberation from sins, followed from God's decree and will; so also, once the sacrifice of Christ has been completed, all who believe in him and obey him are freed from sins, not because some force and power [δυνάμεις] of satisfaction for our sins lay hidden in the things done in the person of Christ, but because that effect itself followed that offering, since God had decided to grant Christ, if he obeyed unto the death of the cross, not only blessed immortality but also such power that he could make all his own immortal and safe. Since, therefore, he rendered such obedience to God and so attained that power, it is certain that we who believe in him, and whom he loves, will not be condemned for our sins, but through Christ will be brought from death to eternal life and blessed immortality. To these things he adds, that just as that old and yearly sacrifice was not completed at the time when the animal was slain, but only when its blood was carried by the priest into the Holy of Holies, so also the sacrifice of Christ was completed not at the time when he was slain and crucified, but only when he entered heaven and presented and offered himself to God the Father for us; for it is clearly evident from the Epistle to the Hebrews that heaven itself corresponds to the Holy of Holies in this likeness. And therefore from the victim and sacrifice of Christ no satisfaction for our sins can be concluded or demonstrated, since, according to the opinion of the opponents, that satisfaction was made not in heaven but on the cross, whereas the sacrifice of Christ was completed in heaven. By the sacrifice of Christ Holy Scripture understands nothing other than the admirable power of Christ itself, which he exercises by presenting himself before God, and through which our sins are truly taken away and removed. But my opponent promises that he will treat this very matter at greater length in the explanation of the kingly office of Christ.

units.la: Syllogismus talis est:
units.tr: The syllogism is as follows:

units.la: Si cùm Christus semetipsum victimam & sacrificium Deo obtulisse perhibetur, hoc per similitudinem cum victimis in Veteri Testamento oblatis, inprimis autem cum solenni & anniuersario illo sacrificio, ad quod peragendum Sacerdos in Sanctum sanctorum ingrediebatur, fecisse dicitur: tum ex sacrificio & victima Christi nulla satisfactio pro peccatis nostris concludi, ac demonstrari potest:
units.tr: If, when Christ is said to have offered himself as a victim and sacrifice to God, this is said to have been done by likeness with the victims offered in the Old Testament, and especially with that solemn and yearly sacrifice for the performance of which the priest entered into the Holy of Holies: then from the sacrifice and victim of Christ no satisfaction for our sins can be concluded or demonstrated:

units.la: Atqui prius est verum: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: But the first is true: therefore the second also.

units.la: Connexi duæ subiunguntur probationes. Prima est:
units.tr: Two linked proofs are added. The first is:

units.la: Si populus in Veteri Testamento, peracto solenni & anniuersario illo sacrificio, à peccatis liberabatur, non quod vis ac virtus aliqua in illo sacrificio fuerit Deo pro peccatis ipsorum satisfaciendi, sed quia effectus ille, nempe liberatio à peccatis, ex Dei decreto & voluntate sequutus est: tum, si Christus, quum semetipsum victimam & oblationem Deo pro peccatis nostris obtulisse perhibetur, hoc per similitudinem cum victimis in Veteri Testamento fecisse dicitur: nulla inde satisfactio pro peccatis nostris concludi ac demonstrari potest: Seu: Sacrificio Christi peracto à peccatis liberantur omnes quiin ipsum credunt, & ipsi obediunt, non quod vis ac δυναμις aliqua satisfactoria pro peccatis nostris, in iis, quæ in Christi persona perácta sunt, latuerit, sed quia effectus ille, ex Dei voluntate & decreto, quo statuit, Christum, si ipsi ad mortem usque crucis obediret, non tantùm beata immortalitate, sed etiam eiusmodi potestate donare, qua quoque immortales ac saluos reddere possit, illam oblationem sequutus est: Atqui prius,ut patet ex epistola ad Hebraos, verum est: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: If the people in the Old Testament, once that solemn and yearly sacrifice had been completed, were freed from sins, not because any power or virtue in that sacrifice existed to satisfy God for their sins, but because that effect, namely liberation from sins, followed from God's decree and will: then, if Christ, when he is said to have offered himself as victim and oblation to God for our sins, is said to have done this by likeness with the victims of the Old Testament: no satisfaction for our sins can be concluded or demonstrated from this: Or: Once the sacrifice of Christ has been completed, all who believe in him and obey him are freed from sins, not because some power and [δυναμις] of satisfaction for our sins lay hidden in the things done in the person of Christ, but because that effect followed that offering, by God's will and decree, by which he determined to grant Christ, if he obeyed unto the death of the cross, not only blessed immortality but also such power that he could make all his own immortal and safe: But the first is true, as is plain from the Epistle to the Hebrews: therefore the second also.

units.la: Secunda est:
units.tr: The second is:

units.la: Si vetus illud & anniuersarium sacrificium, non tum temporis quo illud mactabatur,sed tum demum,cum sanguis illius à Sacerdote in Sanctum Sanctorum deferebatur, peractum fuit: tum si Christus, quum semetipsum victimam & oblationem Deo, pro peccatis nostris obtulisse perhibetur, hoc per similitudinem cum victimis in Veteri Testamento oblatis, in primis autem cum solenni & anniuersario illo sacrificio, ad quod peragendum, Sacerdos in Sanctum Sanctorum ingrediebatur,fecisse dicitur, sequitur,sacrificium Christi,non tum cum ille occisus & crucifixus est, sed tum demum cum ille caelum, quod in hac similitudine Sancto Sanctorum respondet, Deo Patri se pro nobis stitit ac obtulit, peractum esse, ac proinde ex sacrificio & victima Christi, nullam satisfactionem pro peccatis nostris concludi aut demonstrari posse: quia satisfactio pro peccatis nostris,ut volunt Aduersarij,non in caelo,sed in cruce facta est.
units.tr: If that old and yearly sacrifice was completed not at the time when the animal was slain, but only when its blood was carried by the priest into the Holy of Holies: then, if Christ, when he is said to have offered himself as victim and oblation to God for our sins, is said to have done this by likeness with the victims offered in the Old Testament, and especially with that solemn and yearly sacrifice for the performance of which the priest entered into the Holy of Holies, it follows that the sacrifice of Christ was completed not when he was slain and crucified, but only when he, in heaven, which in this likeness corresponds to the Holy of Holies, presented and offered himself to God the Father for us; and therefore no satisfaction for our sins can be concluded or demonstrated from the sacrifice and victim of Christ, because satisfaction for our sins, as the opponents hold, was made not in heaven but on the cross.

units.la: Atqui prius verum est:
units.tr: But the first is true:

units.la: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: Therefore the second also.

units.la: Resp. Ipsam similitudinis vocem esse æquiuocam: vel enim significat similitudinem absolutam, ut vocant, in qua videlicet earum rerum, quæ inter se comparantur, similis tantum qualitas, seu affectio Logica consideratur: vel significat illam similitudinis speciem, quam alii parabolicam, alii vero analogiam seu proportionem, & personæ, actionis, aut rei vnius, ad personam, actionem, aut rem aliam comparationem, & typi cum antitypo, signi ac symboli cum re significata, vmbræ denique & figuræ cum ipso corpore, & expressa imagine conuenientiam appellant ac definiunt. Si itaque Aduersarius priorem similitudinis speciem intelligat, sic vt sacrificia illa legalia, similem vim ac virtutem peccata expiandi, cum sanguine & victima Christi habuisse intelligantur: Seu quòd mors & sanguis Christi, eodem modo sese habeat ad expiationem peccatorum nostrorum, quo sese habuerunt sacrificia legalia ad expiandum peccata populi Israelitici: seu,quod talis fuerit vis ac virtus peccata expiandi, in morte & sanguine Christi, qualis extiterit in victimis & sacrificiis legalibus, ac proinde, quod quemadmodum sacrificia illa legalia non ideo peccata expiare dicta fuerint, quod in ipsis aliquid esset quod vel Deum ad condonanda peccata mouere posset, vel eius pro quo offerebantur,culpam compensaret: sed quia ipsis peractis, expiatio quę ex pura Dei benignitate pendebat, statim consequebatur,hoc est,ille à poena suis peccatis debita penitus eximebatur: ita etiam Christi mors peccata nostra expiasse dicetur, non quia illa vel Deum ad condonanda nobis peccata nostra mouerit, vel delictorum nostrorum culpam compensauerit : sed quia peccatorum nostrorum expiatio, quæ ex sola Dei clemētia tota pendebat, Christi supplicio peracto, statim consecuta fit : si inquam hanc similitudinis speciem intelligat Aduersarius,tum connexum syllogismi principalis verum est, sed assumptio eiusdem falsa,quemadmodum tum ex Scripturæ sacræ testimoniis, tum analogiæ ipsius inter sacrificia & ritus legales, atque mortem & passionem Christi,natura, tum denique ratione euidenti, liquidò constat. Nam Christus per mortem abolevit eum qui mortis imperium habet, hoc est Diabolum, & liberos reddit, quotquot metu mortis per omnem vitam obnoxij erant seruituti: Heb.2.14.15. Quod ipsum de sacrificiis & victimis legalibus nusquam legitur, sed contrarium affirmatur: Hebr.7. 18.19 Mandatum praecedens abrogatur, quod nullis viribus sit praeditū & inutile:nihil enim sanctificauit Lex,sed adscita spes melior, per quam appropinquamus Deo:& 9.v.9.10. Quod erat exemplar pro tempore illo praesenti,quo dona sacrificiaque offeruntur, quę non possunt conscientia sanctificare cultorem, in cibis duntaxat, & potionibus & diuersis ablutionibus ac ritibus carnalibus,vsque ad tempus correctionis impositta: & 12.13.14.15.Neque per sanguinē hircorum & vitulorum, sed per proprium sanguinem ingressus est semel in sacrarium aeternam redemptionem nactus. Nam si sanguis taurorum & hircorum , & cinis iuuencae aspergens inquinatos, sanctificat ad carnis puritatem,quantò magis sanguis Christi , qui per Spiritum aeternum seipsum obtulit inculpatum Deo , purgabit conscientiam vestram à mortuis operibus ad seruiendum Deo viuo? Itaque ob id Noui foederis Mediator est, vt morte intercedente ad redemptionem earum praeuaricationum, quae fuerat sub priori Testamento , vocati, promissionem accipiant æternæ hæreditatis. & 10. verf.1.Lex enim vmbram continens futurorum bonorum, non expressam formam rerum, iis hostiis, quas singulis annis eosdem assidue offerunt, nunquam potest accedentes sanctificare: & verf.4. Non potest sanguis taurorum & hircorum auferre peccata: & verf.10. Qua voluntate sanctificati sumus per oblationem corporis Iesu Christi semel factam. Ex quibus omnibus luculenter apparet, ipsi sacrificio, & victimae Christi longe excellentiorem ἐνέργειαν ac virtutem peccata nostra expiandi, atque praestantiores effectus, quam victimis & oblationibus legalibus, imo ea beneficia, quae hisce plane adimuntur, attribui, quod vel solum falsam illam Aduersariorum similitudinem ac proportionem euertit. Quum deinde sacrificia illa, & victimae legales ipsius Christi & sacrificii ab ipso oblati, typi fuerint, quemadmodum paulo ante demonstrauimus: ideo necessario sequitur, sacrificio seu morti ac sanguini Christi & victimis legalibus, eundem effectum, nempe expiationem peccatorum nostrorum, eodem modo, eandemque ob causam & similem efficiendi virtutem, attribui non posse, vt ex natura typi & antitypi: signi item ac symboli analogia constat. Quia enim typus & signum, seu symbolum personae, actionis, & effectus, ac euentus alicuius, non est ipsa persona, res, seu actio, & euentus, sed personam, actionem, & euentum representat & significat: ac Sacerdotes legales officio, Christi munus sacerdotale, oblationibus deinde & victimarum mactatione, Christi immolationem, euentu denique nempe expiatione peccatorum, purgationem peccatorum nostrorum sanguine Christi factam, & victimae illae Veteris Testamenti victimam & sacrificium Christi adumbrarunt, ideo hic effectus, nempe peccatorum expiatio & purgatio, sacrificio seu morti, & sanguini Christi reipsa, ac proprie, victimis autem & sacrificiis legalibus nonnisi metonymice, sacramentaliter, & symbolice attribui potest. Confirmat hoc Ioannes, cum Legem per Mosen datam, gratiam veritatem per Iesum Christum factam esse, testatur, Ioh. 1. v. 17. Quibus verbis docet, Lege, id est ministerium mortis & condemnationis, ac futurorum bonorum adumbratam imaginem, per Mosen ministrum literae traditam, per Christum vero salutis autorem, gratuitam peccatorum remissionem, nobis impetratam esse, & veritatem, id est saluti feram doctrinam Euangelii, quae sub lege obscuris typorum & allegoriarum umbris inuoluta fuit, beneficio Christi, pleno splendore & fulgore nobis illuxisse: & Paulus Legē futurorum bonorum non ipsam expressam imaginem rerum continere, & corpus & corpus Christi esse, affirmans Col.2. v.17. Heb.10. v.1. id est, bona illa futura, nempe æternam redemptionem, quam Christus nactus est, remissionem & abolitionem peccatorū, conscientiarum mundationem, iustitiam, sanctificationem, vitam deniq; sempiternam, ac beneficia spiritualia & salutaria omnia, ritibus illis legalibus adumbrata quidem, sed per Christum revera præstita & collata nobis esse. Quemadmodum vero umbra ipsa corporis nec potest, nec præstat, quæ potest ac præstat ipsum corpus: ita etiam perficere cultores, expiare peccata & mundare conscientias, quod morti Christi, tāquam veritati tribuitur, sacrificiis ac ritibus cæremonialibus tāquam umbræ vere ac proprie competere nō potest. Quàm futilis igitur, stolida ac falsa sit illa Socinianorum inter Christi mortem, ac passionem atque sanguinis effusionem, & sacrificia, atque victimas legales, instituta comparatio, vel infans animaduertere potest. Denique, si qualis fuit virtus, & δύναμις in victimis ac sacrificiis legalibus ad expiandum peccata populi Israelitici, talis etiam est in morte, passione ac sanguine Christi, tum revera inter dignitatem ac valorem brutæ alicuius pecudis, & dignitatem, ac valorem sanguinis ipsius Dei, & agni illius immaculati & incontaminati, nempe Christi, discrimen revera nullum fuerit, quod cogitatu impium, dictu horrendum est, atque blasphemum. Assumptione igitur principalis syllogismi destructa, cætera per se corruunt: quæstionem vero alteram, in cælone videlicet, an vero in cruce peractum sit Christi sacrificium, in loco de Regno Christi, quò illam etiam Aduersarius reiicit, excutiemus, iam ad reliqua argumenta nostra progressuri.
units.tr: Reply. The word similitude itself is ambiguous. It either signifies absolute similitude, as they call it, in which only a similar quality or affection of the things compared is considered in a logical sense; or it signifies that kind of similitude which some call parabolical, and others analogy or proportion, and which they define as a comparison of one person, action or thing with another person, action or thing, and as the correspondence of type with antitype, of sign and symbol with the thing signified, and finally of shadow and figure with the body itself and the expressed image. If therefore the Opponent understands the former kind of similitude, so that those legal sacrifices are taken to have had a like force and power to expiate sins with the blood and victim of Christ; or that the death and blood of Christ stand in the same relation to the expiation of our sins as the legal sacrifices stood to the expiation of the sins of the people of Israel; or that the power to expiate sins in the death and blood of Christ was of the same kind as it was in the legal victims and sacrifices; and therefore that, just as those legal sacrifices were not called expiatory because there was anything in them that could move God to pardon sins, or compensate for the guilt of the one for whom they were offered, but because when they were performed, the expiation, which depended wholly on the pure goodness of God, immediately followed, that is, the person was entirely freed from the punishment owed for his sins; so too the death of Christ will be said to have expiated our sins, not because it moved God to pardon our sins or compensated for the guilt of our offences, but because the expiation of our sins, which depended wholly on the sole mercy of God, followed immediately upon the completed punishment of Christ: if, I say, the Opponent understands this kind of similitude, then the connection of the principal syllogism is true, but its assumption is false, as is clear both from the testimonies of holy Scripture, and from the nature of the analogy itself between the sacrifices and legal rites on the one hand and the death and passion of Christ on the other, and finally from evident reason. For Christ by death abolished him who has the power of death, that is the devil, and set free all who through fear of death were subject to bondage all their life (Heb. 2:14-15). This is nowhere read of the legal sacrifices and victims, but the contrary is affirmed: Heb. 7:18-19 A preceding commandment is abrogated, because it is weak and unprofitable, for the Law made nothing perfect, but a better hope was introduced, through which we draw near to God; and 9:9-10: It was a figure for the present time, in which gifts and sacrifices are offered which cannot make the worshipper perfect in conscience, but consist only of foods, drinks, various washings and fleshly ordinances, imposed until the time of reformation; and 12-15: Not by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood, he entered once into the sanctuary, having obtained eternal redemption. For if the blood of bulls and goats, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on the defiled, sanctify to the cleansing of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? Therefore he is the Mediator of a New Covenant, so that, by means of his death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the former Testament, those who are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance. And 10:1: For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never by those sacrifices, which they offer continually year by year, make perfect those who draw near; and v. 4: It is not possible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins; and v. 10: By which will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once made. From all these things it appears clearly that a far more excellent energy [ἐνέργειαν] and power to expiate our sins, and more excellent effects, are attributed to the sacrifice and victim of Christ itself than to the legal victims and offerings; indeed, the very benefits which are plainly taken away from these are attributed to it. This alone overthrows that false similitude and proportion of the Opponents. Moreover, since those legal sacrifices and victims were types of Christ and of the sacrifice offered by him, as we showed a little earlier, it necessarily follows that the same effect, namely the expiation of our sins, cannot be attributed to the sacrifice, or death and blood, of Christ and to the legal victims in the same way, and for the same cause, and with a similar power of producing it, as is evident from the nature of type and antitype and from the analogy of sign and symbol. For since a type or sign, or symbol, of a person, action, effect or event, is not the person, thing, action or event itself, but represents and signifies the person, action and event; and since the legal priests, by their office, the priestly function of Christ, and by their offerings and slaughter of victims, foreshadowed the immolation of Christ, and those victims of the Old Testament foreshadowed the victim and sacrifice of Christ, and finally the effect, namely the expiation of sins, and the purging of our sins made by the blood of Christ; therefore this effect, namely the expiation and purging of sins, can be attributed really and properly to the sacrifice or death and blood of Christ, but to the victims and legal sacrifices only metonymically, sacramentally and symbolically. John confirms this when he testifies that the Law was given by Moses, grace and truth came by Jesus Christ (John 1:17). By these words he teaches that by the Law, that is the ministry of death and condemnation, and the shadowed image of good things to come, delivered through Moses the minister of the letter, but by Christ the author of salvation, the gratuitous remission of sins has been obtained for us; and that the truth, that is the saving doctrine of the Gospel, which under the Law was wrapped in the obscure shadows of types and allegories, has by the benefit of Christ shone upon us in full splendour and brightness. And Paul, affirming that the Law contained a shadow of good things to come and not the very image of the things, but that the body is Christ (Col. 2:17; Heb. 10:1), means that those good things to come, namely the eternal redemption which Christ obtained, the remission and abolition of sins, the cleansing of consciences, righteousness, sanctification, finally eternal life, and all spiritual and saving benefits, were indeed foreshadowed by those legal rites, but were in truth performed and bestowed upon us through Christ. But just as the shadow of a body neither can nor does what the body itself can and does, so too sacrifices and ceremonial rites, as shadows, cannot properly and truly possess the power to perfect worshippers, to expiate sins and to cleanse consciences, which is attributed to the death of Christ as the truth. How futile, foolish and false is that comparison, made by the Socinians, between the death, passion and effusion of blood of Christ and the legal sacrifices and victims, even an infant can see. Finally, if the power and dynamis [δύναμις] in the legal victims and sacrifices for expiating the sins of the people of Israel was of such a kind, and it is the same in the death, passion and blood of Christ, then there would truly be no difference between the dignity and worth of some brute beast and the dignity and worth of the blood of God himself and of that spotless and undefiled Lamb, namely Christ; which is impious to think, horrible to say, and blasphemous. Therefore, with the assumption of the principal syllogism destroyed, the rest falls of itself. As for the other question, whether Christ's sacrifice was accomplished in heaven or on the cross, we will examine it in the place about the Kingdom of Christ, to which the Opponent also refers it; now we proceed to our remaining arguments.

units.la: Argumentum tertium ad confirmandam veritatem sententiæ nostræ desumitur ex illis Scripturæ sacræ testimoniis, quæ docent, Iesum Christum ideo mortuum esse, ut peccato in carne nostra damnato peccata nobis remitterentur propter nomen eius, & obedientia ipsius per fidem nobis imputata, iustitia, qua coram Deo consistendum nobis est, repararetur. Galat. 6. ver. 21. Quod si per Legem esset iustitia, Christus sine causa mortuus est. Rom. 8. versu tertio & quarto. Quum Legis impotentia nihil posset in carne, Deus suo ipsius Filio missō conformato carni peccato obnoxiæ, idque pro peccato, condemnauit peccatum in carne, vt illius Legis compleatur in nobis. Colos. 2. versu decimoquarto, Deleto, quod aduersum nos erat ritum chirographo, quod erat nobis contrarium, ipse vero cruci affixum e medio sustulit: Galat.4.v.4.5. Postquam venit plenum tempus,emisit Deus Filium suum factum ex muliere, factum legi obnoxium, vt eos, qui legi erant obnoxij,redimeret, vt adoptionem acciperemus. 1.Ioh.2.v.12. Scribo vobis Filioli, quoniam remissa sunt vobis peccata propter nomen eius. Rom.5.v.19. Sicut per inobedientiam vnius hominis peccatores constituti sunt multi: ita per vnius obedientiam iusti constituentur multi. Roman.3.v.24.25. Iustificantur gratis,eius gratia, per redemptionem factam in Iesu Christo, quem proposuit Deus placamentum per fidem in sanguine ipsius. Rom.5.v.17. Qui redundantiam gratiæ, & doni iustitiæ accipiunt in vita regnabunt,per vnum Iesum Christum: & v.9. Iustificati eius sanguine seruabimur nunc multo magis per eum ab ira. Ephes.5.v.7. In quo habemus redemptionem per sanguinem ipsius,remissionem peccatorum ex diuite ipsius gratia. Phil.3.v.9. Vt inueniar in eo non habens meam iustitiam quæ est ex lege, sed eam quæ per fidem est, Christi. 1.Cor.1.v.30. Iesus Christus factus est nobis à Deo sapientia, iustitiaque, sanctificatio & redemptio. (iustificari autem nos per iustitiæ Christi imputationem,capite vigesimosecundo, & vigesimotertio demonstrauimus) 1.Cor.15.ver.55.56.57. Absorpta est mors ad victoriam,vbi tua ô mors victoria? vbi tuus ô sepulchrum stimulus? stimulus vero mortu est peccatum,vis autem peccati Lex: sed Deo sit gratia,qui dedit nobis victoriam per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum. Hebr.2. versu decimoquarto, Quoniam pueri participes sunt carnis & sanguinis, ipse quoque consimiliter particeps factus est eorundem, vt per mortem aboleret eum qui mortis imperium habet, hoc est, Diabolum.
units.tr: The third argument for confirming the truth of our position is drawn from those testimonies of holy Scripture which teach that Jesus Christ died so that sins might be forgiven us for his name, with our sin condemned in his flesh, and so that his obedience, imputed to us through faith, might restore the righteousness by which we must stand before God. Gal. 6. ver. 21: "If righteousness came by the Law, then Christ died in vain." Rom. 8, verses 3 and 4: "What the Law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did by sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin condemned sin in the flesh, that the requirement of the Law might be fulfilled in us." Col. 2, verse 14: "Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross." Gal. 4, verses 4 and 5: "When the fullness of time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the Law, to redeem them that were under the Law, that we might receive the adoption." 1 John 2, verse 12: "I write unto you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name's sake." Rom. 5, verse 19: "For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous." Rom. 3, verses 24 and 25: "Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Jesus Christ, whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood." Rom. 5, verse 17: "They which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ"; and verse 9: "Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him." Eph. 1, verse 7: "In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace." Phil. 3, verse 9: "And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the Law, but that which is through the faith of Christ." 1 Cor. 1, verse 30: "Jesus Christ, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption." (That we are justified by the imputation of Christ's righteousness we have demonstrated in chapters twenty-two and twenty-three.) 1 Cor. 15, verses 55 to 57: "Death is swallowed up in victory. O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory? The sting of death is sin, and the strength of sin is the Law. But thanks be to God, who giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ." Heb. 2, verse 14: "Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil."

units.la: Argumentum tale est;
units.tr: The argument is as follows:

units.la: Qui ideò passus ac mortuus est, vt nobis peccata nostra propter ipsum remitterentur,& peccato in carne ipsius condemnato, ius legis in nobis impleretur,nofqz legi obnoxios, à maledictione ipsius liberaret,deniqz nos per imputationem iustitiæ ipsius iustificaremur,& mors æterna nobis ob peccata debita aboleretur: ille peccata nostra in se vt sponsorem deriuauit, ac proinde Seruator noster est,non tantùm quia viam salutis nobis annuntiauit,& doctrinam suam innocentiâ vitæ,miraculis,& morte ac passione sua,& gloriosa resurrectione confirmauit: verùm etiam,& quidem potissimùm, quia peccata nostra reuera expiauit & pro iis satisfecit: Atqui Iesus Chri- stus ideò passus ac mortuus est, vt nobis peccata nostra pro- pter ipsum,& nomen ipsius remitteretur,& peccato in carne ipsius condemnato,ius legis in nobis impleretur,nosque legi obnoxii à maledictione ipsius liberaremur,denique per impu- tationem iustitiæ & obedientiæ ipsius iustificaremur, morsq; æterna,nobis ob peccata debita aboleretur.
units.tr: He who suffered and died so that our sins might be forgiven us for his sake, and so that, with our sin condemned in his flesh, the right of the Law might be fulfilled in us, and so that he might free us, who were bound to the Law, from its curse, and finally so that we might be justified by the imputation of his righteousness, and eternal death, owed to us for our sins, might be abolished, has taken our sins upon himself as surety, and therefore is our Saviour; not only because he has announced to us the way of salvation and confirmed his teaching by the innocence of his life, by his miracles, by his death and passion, and by his glorious resurrection, but also, and chiefly, because he truly made expiation for our sins and satisfied for them. But Jesus Christ suffered and died so that our sins might be forgiven us for his sake and for his name, and so that, with our sin condemned in his flesh, the right of the Law might be fulfilled in us, and we, who were bound to the Law, might be freed from its curse, and finally be justified through the imputation of his righteousness and obedience, and eternal death, owed to us for our sins, might be abolished.

units.la: Ergo Iesus Christus peccata nostra in se vt sponsorem deriua- uit, ac proinde Seruator noster est, non tantum quia viam sa- lutis nobis annuntiauit, & doctrinam suam innocentia vitæ, miraculis,morte,& passione sua confirmauit,verùm etiam,& quidem potissimum, quia peccata nostra reuera expiauit, & pro iis satisfecit.
units.tr: Therefore Jesus Christ has taken our sins upon himself as surety, and so is our Saviour; not only because he has announced to us the way of salvation and confirmed his teaching by the innocence of his life, by his miracles, his death and his passion, but also, and chiefly, because he truly made expiation for our sins and satisfied for them.

units.la: Assumptionem citata Scripturæ sacræ testimonia euidenter de- monstrat: sed & maioris propositionis veritas est manifesta. Quum enim δικαίωμα seu ius illud Legis, nihil aliud sit, quàm κατάκειμα & damnatoria sententia Legis, qua maledictionis & mortis æternæ supplicio adiudicantur quotquot non manserunt in omnib. quæ scripta sunt in libro legis,vt facerent ea, seu δικαίωμα τῆς sὺς ius illud illud Dei,morti,ac damnationi addicens ac devouens,illud autem tum demum in nobis impleatur,quum vel nos ipsi mortem ac damnationem æternam subimus, vel alius quispiam vice,& loco nostro moritur,& velut vas ac sponsor noster, peccatum,& pœnam peccati in se recipit, ac deriuat, & sic peccato in carne ipsius condemnato,id est, ipsi ceu victimæ piaculari imposito, remissionem peccatorum, & ius vitæ æternæ impetrat, nósque à maledictione legis liberatos, per imputationem iustitiæ & obedientiæ suæ iustificat, non secus ac si nosmetipsi iustitiæ ac legi diuinæ satisfecissemus:ideò luce meridiana clarius elucescit,eum,qui ideò passus ac mortuus est, vt per & propter ipsum, prædicto modo iustificaremur, & à maledictione legis liberaremur, peccata nostra in se, vt vadem, ac sponsorem nostrum deriuasse, ac proinde Seruatorem nostrum esse, non tantum quia salutis, ac vitæ æternæ consequen- dæ viam nobis monstrauit, & doctrinam suam innocentia vitæ, miraculis,morte, passione ac gloriosa resurrectione sua confirma- uit, verùm etiam & quidem potissimùm,quia peccata nostra re- uera expiauit, & pro iis satisfecit. Hisce adde quod ad osten- dendam tantum, & obsignandam, atque confirmandam salutis viam nihil opus fuisset, tantis cruciatibus & tam dirę mortis supplicio Christum exponi, nisi morte ipsius peccata nostra vere expianda,& sic mors abolenda fuisset.
units.tr: The minor premise is clearly shown by the cited testimonies of holy Scripture, and the truth of the major premise is also plain. For the right [δικαίωμα] of that Law is nothing other than the condemnatory sentence of the Law [κατάκριμα], by which all who have not remained in all the things written in the book of the Law, to do them, are adjudged to the punishment of curse and eternal death. The Law's right, which assigns and devotes them to death and damnation, is then fulfilled in us only when either we ourselves undergo death and eternal damnation, or someone else dies in our place and stead, and, as our surety and guarantor, takes upon himself and bears sin and the penalty of sin. In this way, with sin condemned in his flesh, that is, with sin laid upon him as a sacrificial victim, he obtains the forgiveness of sins and the right to eternal life, and justifies us, freed from the curse of the Law, through the imputation of his righteousness and obedience, just as if we had satisfied divine righteousness and the Law ourselves. Therefore it shines more clearly than noonday light that he who suffered and died so that we might be justified through him and for his sake in the aforesaid manner, and be freed from the curse of the Law, took our sins upon himself as our bail and surety, and so is our Saviour; not only because he showed us the way of salvation and of attaining eternal life, and confirmed his teaching by the innocence of his life, his miracles, his death, his passion and his glorious resurrection, but also, and chiefly, because he truly made expiation for our sins and satisfied for them. To this add that, to show, seal and confirm the way of salvation alone, there was no need for Christ to be exposed to such great torments and the punishment of so dreadful a death, unless by his death our sins were to be truly expiated and so death abolished.

units.la: Argumentum quartum ad confirmandam veritatem sententiæ ac doctrinæ nostræ desumitur ex illis Scripturæ sacræ testimoniis, quæ docent Christum Mediatorem nostrum esse, non ideò tantū quod internuntius fuerit diuinæ voluntatis, vt Moses, Gal.3.vers. 19.Lex ordinata per manum internuntij, sed quod dissidentes partes vtrinque in nouum amicitiæ fœdus verè restituit,& tum Dei, tum nostri respectu æternum fœdus gratiæ, sua morte sanciuit: Heb.8.vers.6. At nunc noster ille Pontifex, eò excellentius ministerium sortitus est,quo prꝶstantioris est fœderis intercessor, quod prꝶstatio-ribus promissis sancitum est.& 9.vers.15. Itaque ob id noui fœderis Mediator est.& 12.ver.24. Accessistis ad nouì Testamenti Mediatorem Iesum,& sanguinem aspersionis, prꝶsantiora loquentem,quàm loqueretur sanguis Abel. Et quod nos, qui propter peccata & iniquitates nostras filii iræ,& in offensis mortui, ac proinde extra gratiā & communionem vitæ Dei constituti fuimus,Deo reconciliauit: Ephef. 2.vers.1. Et vos quum essetis mortui in offensis & peccatis vnà viuifi-cauit:& vers.3. Eramus natura filij iræ. Rom.5.vers.10. Nam si quum inimici essemus,reconciliati suimus Deo per mortem filij eius,multo magis reconciliati seruabimur per vitam ipsius. 2.Cor.5. vers.19. Deus erat in Christo mundum reconcilians sibi,non imputando eis peccata ipsorum, nimirùm quatenus ipsum constituit ἱλαστήριον, seu placamentum per sidem in sanguine ipsius: Rom.3.vers.25 ita vt hac ratione sublata sit inimicitia inter Deum & inter nos:Ephef.2.vers.14.15.16.Ipse est pax nostra, qui vtraque fecit vnum, & intergerini parietis septum soluit : inimicitias. id est, lege Mandatorum,quæ in ritibus posita est, per carnem suam aboleuit, vt ex duobus illis conderet in semetipso,vnum nouum hominem faciens pacem,& vtrosque in vno corpore reconciliaret Deo per crucem,peremptis inimicitiis per eam, quia videlicet Pater in Christo,vt sponsore nostro,acquiescit: Matt.3.vers.17. Atque hinc est,quod Christus calcare dicitur lacum vini furoris & iræ. Apocalyp. 19.vers.15. & quod propitiatio per Christum facta, plerumque solet coniungi cum eius intercessione:1.Ioh.2.vers.1.2. Si quis peccauerit, aduocatum habemus apud Patrem Iesum Christum iustum, & ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris. Hebr.9.vers.24. Postquam dixerat Apostolus,absque sanguinis effusione non fieri remissionem, dicit, cit, Christum in ipsum caelum ingressum esse, ut appareat nunc in conspectu Dei pro nobis: Hebr. 10. versu 12. Hic una pro peccatis oblata victima in perpetuum sedet ad dextram Dei: unde apparet obedientia Christi pro nobis praestita Deum vere nobis factum esse propitium.
units.tr: The fourth argument for confirming the truth of our position and doctrine is drawn from those testimonies of holy Scripture which teach that Christ is our Mediator, not only because he is the messenger of the divine will, as Moses was (Gal. 3, verse 19: "The Law was ordained by the hand of a mediator"), but because he truly restored the parties at variance on both sides to a new bond of friendship, and by his death sealed the eternal covenant of grace, both with respect to God and with respect to us. Heb. 8, verse 6: "But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises." Heb. 9, verse 15: "And for this cause he is the Mediator of the new testament." Heb. 12, verse 24: "And to Jesus the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel." And because he reconciled to God us, who, on account of our sins and iniquities, were children of wrath and dead in trespasses, and so had been placed outside the grace and fellowship of God's life. Eph. 2, verse 1: "And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins." Verse 3: "We were by nature the children of wrath." Rom. 5, verse 10: "For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life." 2 Cor. 5, verse 19: "God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them," namely, in so far as he set him forth as a propitiation [ἱλαστήριον], or placation, through faith in his blood (Rom. 3, verse 25), so that by this means enmity between God and us has been removed. Eph. 2, verses 14 to 16: "For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us, having abolished in his flesh the enmity, that is, the law of commandments contained in ordinances, for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace; and that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby." Namely, because the Father is well pleased with Christ as our surety (Matt. 3, verse 17). Hence it is that Christ is said to tread the winepress of the wrath of God (Rev. 19, verse 15), and that the propitiation made through Christ is generally joined with his intercession: 1 John 2, verses 1 and 2: "If any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, and he is the propitiation for our sins." Heb. 9, verse 24. After the Apostle had said that without shedding of blood there is no remission, he says that Christ entered into heaven itself, to appear now in the presence of God for us. Heb. 10, verse 12: "But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God." Whence it is evident that the obedience of Christ performed for us has truly made God propitious to us.

units.la: Argumentum tale est:
units.tr: The argument runs as follows:

units.la: Qui eiusmodi est Mediator, ut partes dissidentes, Deū videlicet & homines, vtrinque in nouum amicitiae foedus restituerit, & tum Dei, tum nostri respectu, aeternum foedus gratiae sanciuerit morte sua, & constitutus ἱλαστήριον, seu placamentum per fidem in sanguine ipsius, peremptis inimicitiis, & sublatis peccatis nostris, quae inter Deum & nos distinerminarunt, nos inimicos Dei & mortuos in peccatis nostris, ac filios irae, Deo reconciliauit per mortem suam, & gratiam ac fauorem Dei nobis conciliauit: ille peccata nostra in se, ut sponsorem nostrum deriuauit, ac proinde Seruator noster est, non tantum quia viam salutis nobis annunciauit, & doctrinam suam vitae integritate, miraculis, morte, passione, & gloriosa resurrectione sua confirmauit, verum etiam, & quidem potissimum, quia amissam Patris gratiam nobis conciliauit, peccatáque nostra expiauit, & pro iis satisfecit.
units.tr: He who is such a Mediator that he restores the dividing parties, namely God and men, to a new friendship on both sides, and by his death ratifies an eternal covenant of grace with respect both to God and to us, and is appointed propitiation [ἱλαστήριον], or a means of appeasement, through faith in his blood; who, with enmities removed and our sins taken away (sins which stood between God and us), reconciled us to God by his death, though we were enemies of God and dead in our sins and children of wrath, and won for us the grace and favour of God: this man took our sins upon himself as our surety, and is therefore our Saviour, not only because he announced to us the way of salvation and confirmed his teaching by the integrity of his life, by his miracles, his death, his passion and his glorious resurrection, but also, and chiefly, because he won for us the Father's lost grace, expiated our sins and made satisfaction for them.

units.la: Atqui Iesus Christus eiusmodi Mediator est, ut partes dissidentes, Deū videlicet, & homines, vtrinque in nouum amicitiae foedus restituerit, ac tum Dei, tum nostri respectu, aeternum foedus gratiae sanciuerit morte sua, & constitutus ἱλαστήριον, seu placamentum per fidem in sanguine ipsius, peremptis inimicitiis, & sublatis peccatis nostris, quae inter Deum & nos distinerminarunt, nos inimicos Dei, & mortuos in peccatis nostris, ac filios irae Deo reconciliauit per mortem suam, & gratiam ac fauorem Iesu Christi nobis conciliauit.
units.tr: But Jesus Christ is such a Mediator that he restores the dividing parties, namely God and men, to a new friendship on both sides, and with respect both to God and to us ratifies by his death an eternal covenant of grace, and is appointed propitiation [ἱλαστήριον], or a means of appeasement, through faith in his blood; with enmities removed and our sins taken away (sins which stood between God and us), he reconciled us, who were enemies of God and dead in our sins and children of wrath, to God by his death, and won for us the grace and favour of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Ergo Iesus Christus peccata nostra in se vt sponsorem nostrum deriuauit, ac proinde Seruator noster est, non tantum quia viam salutis nobis annunciauit, & doctrinam suam vitae integritate, miraculis, morte, passione, & gloriosa resurrectione sua confirmauit: verum etiam, & quidem potissimum, quia nobis amissam Patris gratiam conciliauit, peccatåque nostra expiauit,& pro iis satisfecit.
units.tr: Therefore Jesus Christ took our sins upon himself as our surety, and is therefore our Saviour, not only because he announced to us the way of salvation and confirmed his teaching by the integrity of his life, by his miracles, his death, his passion and his glorious resurrection, but also, and chiefly, because he won for us the Father's lost grace, expiated our sins and made satisfaction for them.

units.la: Assumptio disertis verbis in citatis Scripturæ sacræ testimoniis affirmatur : propositionis autem maioris veritas per se manifesta est. Quum enim aliud plane sit homini peccatori gratuitam Dei beneuolentiam,& paternæ beneuolentiæ effecta,nempe remissionem peccatorum, iustificationem, & beneficia spiritualia reliqua offerre, annuntiare, & obsignare,& sic Deo ipsi ( quod ex Aduersariorum sententia necessario sequitur)hominum gratiam conciliare, eósque ipsi alioquin inimicos, amicos & propitios reddere: aliud vero iustissimæ iræ diuinæ grauissimas causas, nempe peccata & iniquitates, quæ Deum benignum à nobis abalienarunt, & nos filios iræ, ac mortis & damnationis æternæ reos constituerunt, ignominiosissimæ & crudelissimæ mortis supplicio tollere, & sic peremptis inimicitiis, & earundem causis, nos in Patris æterni gratiam reducere:quis non videt, eum qui eiusmodi Mediator est, vt peccata nostra, quibus Deum à nobis abalienabamus, sanguine suo expiauerit, & vice ac loco nostro lacum vini furoris & iræ Dei calcauerit, & sic iustitiæ diuinæ satisfecerit, Deúmque nobis reconciliauerit, non tantùm viam salutis ac vitæ æternæ nobis annuntiasse, & doctrinam suam euidentissimis documentis & argumentis confirmasse, verùm etiam peccata nostra, & peccatorum pœnas in sese, vt vadem, & sponsorem deriuasse, nobisque amissam Dei gratiam, ac vitam æternam, acquisinisse?
units.tr: The minor premise is affirmed in plain words in the cited testimonies of holy Scripture, and the truth of the major premise is self-evident. For it is one thing to offer, announce and seal to a sinful man God's free goodwill and the effects of his fatherly goodwill, namely the forgiveness of sins, justification and the other spiritual benefits, and so to win the favour of men for God himself (which, on the opponents' view, necessarily follows), making those who were otherwise his enemies his friends and well-disposed towards him. It is quite another thing to remove, by the most ignominious and cruel death, the very grave causes of God's most just wrath, namely the sins and iniquities which estranged the kindly God from us and made us children of wrath, liable to death and eternal damnation, and so, with enmities and their causes removed, to bring us back into the favour of the eternal Father. Who does not see that he who is such a Mediator that he expiated with his blood the sins by which we estranged God from ourselves, and in our place and stead trod the winepress of the wine of the fury and wrath of God, and so satisfied divine justice and reconciled us to God, has not only announced to us the way of salvation and eternal life and confirmed his teaching by the most evident proofs and arguments, but has also taken our sins and the penalties of our sins upon himself as surety and guarantor, and has obtained for us the lost grace of God and eternal life?

units.la: OSTORRODIVS Institutionum suarum capite trigesimoseptimo, sectione secunda, ad hoc argumentum nostrum excipit, ac dicit, Christum ideo propitiationem pro peccatis nostris appellari, & reconciliationis in sacra Scriptura mentionem fieri, non quod Christus Patrem suum nobis reconciliauerit, sed quòd Deus nobis per Christum significauerit, se nobis propitium esse, hoc est, se peccatorum nostrorum non recordaturum esse amplius, sed ea clementer nobis condonaturum, modò serio resipiscamus, & nos à peccatis conuertamus. Atque hoc duobus argumentis probare conatur:Primum est quod quamuis in Nouo Testamento reconciliationis fiat mentio, & Christus ipse propitiatio pro peccatis nostris appelletur, nusquam tamen scriptum esse, quod Christus Deum nobis reconciliauerit: neque hoc mirum esse, quum vt id fieret, necesse non fuerit, quandoquidem Deus mundum dilexerit, rit, non tantùm priusquam Christus mortuus est ( ex cuius tamen morte illa reconciliatio & propitiatio potissimùm profecta fuisse dicitur )verùm etiam antequam munus suum in terra auspicaretur, & exequeretur : imò ipsa charitas & dilectio Dei, mortis & passionis Christi causa extiterit.
units.tr: Ostorrodius, in the second section of the thirty-seventh chapter of his Institutes, takes up our argument and says: Christ is called the propitiation for our sins, and mention is made of reconciliation in Holy Scripture, not because Christ reconciled his Father to us, but because God signified to us through Christ that he is propitious to us, that is, that he will no longer remember our sins but will graciously pardon them, provided only that we seriously repent and turn from our sins. And he tries to prove this by two arguments. The first is that although mention is made of reconciliation in the New Testament, and Christ himself is called the propitiation for our sins, nowhere is it written that Christ reconciled God to us; nor is this surprising, since there was no need for it to happen, seeing that God loved the world, not only before Christ died (from whose death that reconciliation and propitiation are said chiefly to have proceeded), but even before he began and carried out his office on earth; indeed, the very charity and love of God was the cause of the death and passion of Christ.

units.la: Syllogismus talis est:
units.tr: The syllogism is this:

units.la: Si nusquam in Scripturis sacris docetur, quòd Christus Deum nobis reconciliauerit, neque vt hoc fieret necesse fuit, tum Christus ideo propitiatio pro peccatis nostris appellatur, & reconciliationis mentio fit in Scripturis sacris, non quòd Christus Patrem suum nobis reconciliauerit, sed quod Deus nobis per Christum significauerit, se nobis propitium esse, hoc est, se peccatorum nostrorum non recordaturum esse amplius, sed ea clementer nobis condonaturum, modò seriò resipiscamus, & nos à peccatis conuertamus.
units.tr: If nowhere in the holy Scriptures is it taught that Christ reconciled God to us, and it was not necessary for this to happen; then Christ is called the propitiation for our sins, and mention of reconciliation is made in the holy Scriptures, not because Christ reconciled his Father to us, but because God signified through Christ that he is merciful to us, that is, that he will no longer remember our sins but will graciously pardon them to us, provided that we truly repent and turn from our sins.

units.la: Atqui prius verum est:
units.tr: But the first is true:

units.la: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: Therefore the second is also true.

units.la: Assumptionis hæc est:
units.tr: The proof of the assumption is this:

units.la: Si Deus mundum dilexit, non tantùm priusquam Christus mortuus est, verùm etiam antequam munus suum in terra auspicaretur, & exequeretur, imò ipse amor seu dilectio Dei, mortis & passionis Christi causa extitit : tum non fuit necesse, vt Deus nobis per Christum reconciliaretur:
units.tr: If God loved the world, not only before Christ died but even before he began and carried out his office on earth, and indeed the love and affection of God itself was the cause of Christ's death and passion; then it was not necessary for God to be reconciled to us through Christ:

units.la: Atqui prius verum est:
units.tr: But the first is true:

units.la: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: Therefore the second is also true.

units.la: Alterum argumentum, quo sententiam ac doctrinam suam stabilire conatur Ostorrodius, est, quòd cùm Scriptura sacra de reconciliatione ac propitiatione loquitur, id fiat nostri respectu, nempe quod Christus nos Deo reconciliauerit, imò quod maius est, quod Deus ipse per Christum nos sibi reconciliauerit, quandoquidem non ipse inimicus noster fuerit, sed nos inimici ipsius extiterimus : nec nos ipsum quæsiuerimus, sed ipse nos quæsiuerit : deniq. non nos ipsum, sed ipse nos dilexerit, 1. Ioh. 4. 10. In hoc est charitas, non quod nos dilexerimus Deum, sed quod ipse dilexerit nos, & miserit Filium suum vt esset propitiatio pro peccatis nostris.Vnde factum vt nusquam legatur quod Deus nobis reconciliatus sit, sed quod nos ipsi reconciliati simus, & quod Deus ipse nos sibi reconciliauerit:2. Cor.5. vers.18.19.20.21. Hæc omnia sunt ex Deo, qui reconciliauit nos sibi per Iesum Christum, deditque ministerium reconciliationis, nempe quia Deus erat in Christo, mundum reconcilians sibi, non imputando ipsis peccata ipsorum, posuitque in nobis sermonem hunc reconciliationis: Itaque nomine Christi legatione fungimur, velut Deo precante per nos, oramus Christi nomine reconciliamini Deo, fecit enim, vt qui non nouit peccatum, pro nobis peccatum esset, vt nos efficeremur iustitia Dei in eo.
units.tr: The second argument by which Ostorodius tries to establish his opinion and doctrine is this: when Holy Scripture speaks of reconciliation and propitiation, this is said with respect to us, namely that Christ reconciled us to God, or rather, which is greater, that God himself reconciled us to himself through Christ, since he was not our enemy but we were his enemies; nor did we seek him, but he sought us; finally, not we loved him, but he loved us (1 John 4:10: "Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins"). Hence it is nowhere read that God was reconciled to us, but that we ourselves were reconciled, and that God himself reconciled us to himself (2 Cor. 5:18-21): "All these things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave us the ministry of reconciliation; namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not imputing their sins to them, and he has placed in us the word of reconciliation. So we act as ambassadors for Christ, as though God were pleading through us; we beg you in Christ's name, be reconciled to God. For he made him who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God."

units.la: Syllogismus talis est:
units.tr: The syllogism is this:

units.la: Si cum Scriptura sacra de reconciliatione ac propitiatione loquitur, id sit respectu nostri, nempe quod Christus nos Deo reconciliauerit, seu quod Deus ipse per Christum nos sibi reconciliauerit, tum Christus ideo propitiatio pro peccatis nostris appellatur, & reconciliationis mentio fit in Scripturis sacris, non quod Christus Patrem suum nobis reconciliauerit, sed quod Deus nobis per Christum significauerit, se nobis propitium esse, hoc est, se peccatorum nostrorum non esse recordaturum amplius, sed ea clementer nobis condonaturum, & remissurum, modo serio resipiscamus, & nos a peccatis conuertamus.
units.tr: If, when Holy Scripture speaks of reconciliation and propitiation, this is with respect to us, namely that Christ reconciled us to God, or that God himself reconciled us to himself through Christ; then Christ is called the propitiation for our sins, and mention of reconciliation is made in the holy Scriptures, not because Christ reconciled his Father to us, but because God signified through Christ that he is merciful to us, that is, that he will no longer remember our sins but will graciously pardon and remit them to us, provided that we truly repent and turn from our sins.

units.la: Atqui prius verum est: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: But the first is true: therefore the second is also true.

units.la: Assumptionis probatio hæc est:
units.tr: The proof of the assumption is this:

units.la: Si Deus nobis non fuit inimicus, sed nos Dei inimici extitimus: si deinde non nos Deum quæsiuimus, sed ipse nos quæsiuit: si denique non ipsum dileximus nos, sed ipse nos dilexit: tum sequitur, cum Scriptura sacra de reconciliatione & propitiatione loquitur, id fieri respectu nostri, quatenus videlicet Christus nos Dei inimicos, qui ipsum odio prosequuti sumus, Deo reconciliauerit, seu quatenus Deus nos sibi per Christum reconciliauerit.
units.tr: If God was not our enemy, but we were the enemies of God; if, further, we did not seek God, but he sought us; if, finally, we did not love him, but he loved us; then it follows that when Holy Scripture speaks of reconciliation and propitiation, this takes place with respect to us, in that Christ reconciled us, who were God's enemies and had hated him, to God, or in that God reconciled us to himself through Christ.

units.la: Atqui prius verum est: Ergo & posterius.
units.tr: But the first is true: therefore the second is also true.

units.la: Resp. Assumptionem syllogismi principalis, quæ bimembris est, falsam esse: & primum quidem ipsius membrum, quo asseritur, nusquam quam in Scripturis sacris extare, quod Christus nobis Deum reconcilia-verit, quantum concernit, si illud simpliciter & absolute intelligatur, verissime à nobis vt falsum negatur. Quauis enim hoc ipsum ἀπολλάξει, & χ̄ τὴν ῥῆσιν, atqz verbotim in scripturis sacris nusquam legatur, res tamen ipsa phrasibus æquipollentibus, innumeris penè in locis Scripturæ sacræ, docetur & inculcatur, quemadmodum ex allegatis, in antecedentibus nostris quatuor argumentis, sacræ Scripturæ testimoniis liquet, tum ex sequentibus, potissimum vero ex iis, quæ ad duo illa Aduersarii argumenta, deinceps respon-deri sumus, patebit amplius. Alterum vero membrum eiusdem assumptionis quod attinet, quo dicitur, ad salutem videlicet ac vitæ ternam nobis consequendam, opus non fuisse, vt Deus nobis reconciliaretur, quia illud sententiæ Aduersariorum, axiomate discreto enunciatæ & comprehensæ, partem tantum vnam videlicet, negationem sententiæ nostræ, assumptio vero syllogismi principalis secundi, thesin ac sententiam Aduersariorum complectitur, & duæ illæ partes iisdem argumentis confirmantur: ideo nos breuitati studentes, illa duo assumpta coniungemus, enuntiatione ac thesi integra, & primo ad illam, deinde vero ad argumentum, quod ad illam confirmandam adducitur, respondebimus. Thesis igitur seu assumptio integra hæc est: Christus morte & passione sua non Deum quasi ipse nobis iratus & inimicus fuisset, placauit aut propitium reddidit, sed nos, qui Dei inimici fuimus, & odio ipsum prosequuti sumus, Deo reconciliauit, & quasi amicos reddidit: Seu, Ad salutem ac vitam æternam nobis comparandam, non opus fuit vt Deus quasi ille nobis iratus fuisset, & inimicus placaretur & reconciliaretur, sed vt nos qui Deo inimici fuimus, & ipsum odio prosequuti sumus, ei reconciliaremur & quasi amici fieremus. Vt autem huius thesis manifesta falsitas eò magis detegatur, & veritas sententiæ ac doctrinæ nostræ clarius elucescat, dispiciendum est, quænam sint partes diffidentes, & an ex partibus diffidentibus vtraque, an vero altera tantum, & quænam offensæ, & inimico animo fuerit? Deinde vero, an vtraque, an vero altera tantum, & quenam reconciliata sit, ac proinde cuiusnam partis respectu, illius reconciliationis ac propitiationis in sacra Scriptura mentio fiat? denique an vtrique parti idem reconciliationis modus competat, atque tribuedus sit? Partes igitur diffidentes, ac per Christum reconciliandas, esse Deum atque homines, testatur Propheta Esaias, Peccata vestra, inquiens, disterminant inter vos & Deum vestrum: Esai.59.v.2. Et Paulus 1.Tim.2.v.5.Vnus Deus,vnus etiam Mediator Dei, & hominum, homo Christus Iesus. Et ex partibus illis diffidentibus, hominem priusquam Spiritus S. virtute,in veram natiuæ miseriæ suæ agnitionem perductus,renovetur ac regeneretur, Deo inimicum esse, ipsumque non quidem tam vt creatorẽ,quam Legislatorẽ ac legum suarum seuerum vindicem,hostili animo prosequi, inter nos,& Socinianos,extra controuersiam opinor,est constitutum. Quinetiam hominem,qui ex natiuæ illius corruptionis & dominantis peccati statu, ad gratiæ, ac beneficiorum spiritualium participatione est perducendus, vero atque syncero amore erga Deum imbuendum esse,minimè diffitemur,sed quomodo,quaue ratione,& cuiusnam virtute hoc fiat postmodum exposituri sumus. Verùm non hominem tantùm,sed etiam Deum offensum,ac nobis iratum fuisse, & per mortemChristi nobis reconciliandum: ex eo apparet,tum quod Efaias loco citato inquit, Peccata hominum distermin asse, inter illos, atque Deum ipsorum,& facere vt occultet faciem suam ab ipsis ne exaudiat:Quibus verbis Propheta docet peccata nostra esse veluti parietem inter Deum & nos interiectum, eaque priuare nos Dei gratia, & benignitatis illius ianuam nobis occludere,ac proinde Deum iusto nos odio prosequi,nisi forte contra infinita & euidentissima documenta existiment Aduersarii, Deum illis offensum,& iratum non esse, à quibus tamen benignitatis & misericordiæ suæ faciem auertit,& ad quorum preces, ille aures suas occludit: & quod Dauid dicit Psal.5. v.6.7.Odisti, inquiens,omnes qui operam dant iniquitati, perditurus es loquentes mendacium,virum sanguinarium & dolosum abominatur Iehouah,& Psal.11. v.5.6.Iehouah iustum explorat, improbum vero,& amantem violentia odit animus ipsius, depluet super improbos prunas,ignem,& sulphur,ventúsque procellocismus,portio cælicis eorũ. Pro.11.20.Abominationi sunt Iehoua,peruersi animo,accepti veró ei integri via:& 17.v.15. Qui absoluit improbum, & qui condemnat iustum, abominationi Iehouasunt æque ambo: Deut.27. v.26. Maledictus qui non manserit in omnibus, quæ scripta sunt in libro legis, vt faciat ea: Vnde Paulus natura filios irae,id est,à gratia & fauore Dei exclusos, & damnationi obnoxios appellat omnes quotquot nimirum carnali, & naturali propagatione ab Adamo descendunt,ad Ephesios capite secundo, versu tertio: tum etiam ex horrendis iudiciis diuinis, atque iræ Dei effectis & peccatorum pœnis potissipotissimum vero ex eo, quod Deus peccata nostra nonnisi per atrocissimum & ignominiosissimum mortis Christi, cum gravissimo irae divinae sensu coniuncto supplicio, expiari voluit. Si enim in supplicio isto & passione Christi nihil fuit atrocius, atque gravius morte aut internecione communi, dicant mihi Aduersarii, cur Christus crucem adeo horruerit, longe supra omnes Martyres, graviora & atrociora in specie, & corporalia tormenta si specties, passos, tanto pavore trepidarit, sanguis ex veneranda ipsius facie distillauerit, in cruce denique se a Deo desertu exclamauerit? Habemus partes diffidetes, de propitiatione ac reconciliatione, & eius modo ac forma, nunc porro videndu ac dispiciendu, homini ne Deus, an vero Deus homini per mortem & crucem Christi placatus & reconciliatus fuerit. Cum vero illius reconciliationis modus atque forma in satisfactione pro peccatis nostris, & irae divinae sensu consistat: hinc luce meridiana clarius euadit, quoties sacra Scriptura reconciliationis & propitiationis illius mentione facit, toties morte Christi, Deum nobis propitium & placatum redditum esse, significari. Apud quem deinde Christus per mortem factus est ἱλασμὸς seu propitiatio, & ἱλαστήριον, seu placamentum eum etiam reconciliauit ac propitium reddidit. Atqui non hominem Deo, sed Deum homini per mortem & sanguinem Christi, propitium esse factum, ex eo liquet apertissime, quod ἱλάσεται & ἵλεως, seu ἵλεως εἴη alicui, vel peccatis alicuius, in Scripturis sacris, significat, peccata alicui remittere, seu peccatorum alicuius non amplius recordari, Luc. 18. v. 13. O Deus propitius esto (ἱλάσθητί μοι) mihi peccatori. Petiit autem Publicanus ille & impetrauit remissionem peccatorum: vt apparet ex v. 14. vbi ille iustificatus domum descendisse dicitur. Sic Heb. 8. 12. Ero propitius peccatis ipsorum (ἵλεως ἔσομαιταῖς ἀδικίαις αὐτῶν) & iniquitatum ipsorum non recordabor amplius.
